M60 ONTOLOGY GAP (`overrides` reverted entirely): the lane emits no `overrides` edge at all, which is the state it was in before this round. This is the defect class `ontology-coverage-gate.ts` exists for — a relationship type absent from BOTH the analyzer and the oracle, so the differential had nothing to disagree about and the type stayed invisible for the whole lane's history. Clean has no `override` KEYWORD, so no keyword probe could ever have found it: the only evidence is the typeclass pairing, and measuring the pairing is what produced it. Measured before the branch existed: 1,036 instance members across 78 classes at the 2,181-file corpus. Caught by clean/typeclass-overrides, whose two `expectRelationships` rows pin `overrides Thing.show -> Show.show` and `overrides Int.show -> Show.show`.

FABRICATION CLASS, and the direction an aggregate count invites. The in-file guard is dropped, so an `instance C T where m` emits `overrides T.m -> C.m` for a class this file never read. Almost every Clean class is IMPORTED — the doc's own `implements` row records 322 of 739 edges as external for exactly that reason — so the unguarded form names a class member the analyzer has no evidence exists. Unlike an `implements` edge, whose meaning survives an external target, an `overrides` edge ASSERTS that this member is the implementation of that specific class member; without having read the class, that is a claim about a declaration the run never saw. Caught by clean/typeclass-overrides, whose `forbidRelationships` row refuses `overrides from: Bool.size` — `instance Show Bool where size b = …` supplies a member (`size`) the imported class does not declare. THE SHAPE IS DERIVED, NOT HARDCODED, and it had to be re-derived when the container was namespaced: the unguarded emission is per INSTANCE, so the mutant reads the instance container (`impl`, `<target>::instance`) for the type and the member's NOMINAL owner for the endpoint — the two facts the naming fix moved. A mutant that still matched `kind === 'class'` would have survived by matching nothing, which is the failure mode a generator-built revert exists to avoid.

LABEL/DIRECTION CLASS, and the confusion this language is most likely to fall into: the edge is emitted class-member -> instance-member instead of instance-member -> class-member. Both ends are real, the type is right, and the graph is silently INVERTED: `bb_graph` on a class member would then report its own subclasses as the things it overrides, and `bb_impact` on `Show.show` would return its implementations where it should return its callers. In Clean the direction is not a convention — a `class_declaration` member is ABSTRACT (`class Show a where show :: !a -> String` carries no body) and therefore overrides nothing; the instance member is the definition. Caught by clean/typeclass-overrides, whose `forbidRelationships` rows refuse `overrides Show.show` (the reverse direction) and require both `Thing.show -> Show.show` and `Int.show -> Show.show`.

PAYLOAD CLASS on the type the lane just added. The `Owner.member` qualification is dropped from both endpoints, so `Thing.show -> Show.show` becomes `show -> show`. The edges still resolve — the store matches a bare name — and a resolution-rate check still reads 100%, so nothing about resolvability convicts this. What is lost is IDENTITY: three symbols in the typeclass-overrides fixture are named `show`, and `bb_graph`/`bb_impact` would merge them into one node. A bare-name edge cannot say WHICH `show`. This is the defect class where only a fixture pin can catch it, because every rate the store computes stays at 100%. Caught by clean/typeclass-overrides, whose `forbidRelationships` rows refuse `overrides show` (the unqualified form) and whose two `expectRelationships` rows carry the qualified endpoints.

FABRICATION CLASS, third direction. The `frameOwner !== className` guard is removed, so a POLYMORPHIC instance of a locally-declared class emits an edge whose two endpoints are the SAME string: `instance List [] a where _cons …` gives `List._cons -> List._cons`. An edge from a declaration to itself asserts a relation between two declarations that is not there, and it is invisible to every rate the store computes — both endpoints resolve (to the same row), the confidence is 1.0, the site line is present. The underlying cause is real and named in the analyzer: a polymorphic instance publishes no symbol, so its members are attributed to the CLASS and share the class member's qualifiedName. Measured on the corpus before the guard: 60 such self-edges over the 2,181-file set. Caught by clean/typeclass-overrides, whose two `forbidRelationships` rows refuse `overrides Sized.size` and an edge targeting `Sized.size`.

SECOND LABEL CLASS: the member-level `overrides` edges are relabelled `implements`. It is a plausible misreading — `instance C T where m` DOES implement `C.m` — and it is wrong because the lane ALREADY emits the instance-level `implements` edge (`Thing -> Show`), so the relabelled form double-counts one relationship under two labels and puts an edge whose SOURCE is a method into a type whose sources the other lanes' oracles derive as a type or a class. `implements` is audited by the differential for clean; `overrides` is in the audited set too, so relabelling moves the edge from one audited label to another and the differential's per-label counts change without the total moving. Caught by clean/typeclass-overrides, which requires `type: "overrides"` on both member edges and already requires `implements Thing -> Show` on the instance edge.

SITE-LINE CLASS (M59.O2). The instance member's own `line_number` is dropped from the `overrides` edges. The rule the whole lane follows is that every relationship carries a 1-based line on the NAME-BEARING node, per-site, and that the line is part of the store key `(source, type, target, line)`. With the line gone, `Int.show -> Show.show` and `Thing.show -> Show.show` differ only by their source, so they survive — but a file with two instances of one class for the SAME target type would collide under `INSERT OR IGNORE` and one becomes unreachable from the graph. Caught by clean/typeclass-overrides, whose two `expectRelationships` rows assert distinct `line_number` values (40 and 43) and whose `expectRelationshipCount` row pins the count.

KEY-MISMATCH CLASS. Reverts `signaturesByNode`: the emitting pass is made to look its signature up ONLY by the derived string key, which is what the code did before this round's correction. The two passes derive that key independently and disagree for an instance member — the declaration pass files it under the MODULE owner (`|::cmp`, because it does not know the instance's target) and the emitting pass asks under the INSTANCE owner (`|[!a]::cmp`, because that is the scope the walk is in) — so the lookup misses, `applySignature` never runs, and the member's types and its `| C a` class context are read and discarded. Nothing is fabricated and nothing is mislabelled: real edges go MISSING, which is why a count-only check cannot see it and why the corpus had to be asked the question directly (of 473 class_context nodes at PROD, 20 published no edge at all). Measured at PROD, 312 files: `references` 10,049 -> 9,551, 498 edges absent, total 30,685 -> 30,187, and NO other type moves. Caught by clean/instance-member-signature-context, whose three `expectRelationships` rows pin `references cmp -> Ord` at L34, `references cmp -> Eq` at L43 and `references cmp -> Ord` at L53 — each an instance member's own dictionary requirement — plus `references inner -> Eq` at L67 for the `where`-local form.

SPELLING-MISMATCH CLASS, first half. An operator IS a class name in Clean and the two sites spell it differently: a DECLARATION writes `class (>>=) a where` and an INSTANCE writes `instance >>= Thing where`. The mutant keys `classMembers` on the declaration's `name` field VERBATIM — `(>>=)` — exactly as the code did before this round's correction — so the `overrides` in-file guard cannot find the member set and refuses every `overrides` edge for an operator-named class declared in the SAME FILE. Nothing is fabricated and nothing is mislabelled: an edge that should exist is silently dropped, which is the failure a count-only check cannot see, because the lane's `overrides` total goes DOWN rather than wrong. It is invisible in aggregate for a second reason too: the corpus spells its operator-named classes on ONE line (`class (==) infix 4 a :: !a !a -> Bool`, clean-stdlib/StdOverloaded.icl:23), and the one-line form gives the member set nothing to read — measured 0 new `overrides` edges on the 312-file corpus when the fix landed. So the fixture had to be written to reach the code at all: clean/extends-probe-roles declares `class (>>=) a where` in the `where` form and requires `overrides Thing.>>= -> >>=.>>=` at line 106.

SPELLING-MISMATCH CLASS, second half, and the one that is a FALSE STATEMENT rather than a missing edge. `isExternalClass` exists to say which of the two cases an `implements` edge is: the class is declared in this file, or it is imported. Almost every Clean class IS imported, so the flag is `true` for the normal case and is the only thing that stops a reader assuming otherwise. The mutant reverts the lookup to `!declaredTypeNames.has(className)` alone, so a class declared here as `class (==) infix 4 a ::` and read back by an instance as `==` is reported EXTERNAL — measured at 24 `implements` edges across the 312-file corpus, the false count after the fix being 0. Unlike the first half this one changes no count at all: same edges, same endpoints, same lines, same labels, and one metadata field quietly wrong on 24 of them. Caught by clean/extends-probe-roles, which pins `meta.isExternalClass: false` on `implements Thing -> ==` (line 75) and `implements Thing -> >>=` (line 105) AND forbids the same key reading false on `implements Thing -> Eq`, so the flag cannot be made constant to pass.

TWO-SPELLINGS-ONE-CONSTRUCT CLASS, and the first mutant in this battery that needs the SOURCE TEXT to be reverted faithfully — which is why `transform` receives `source`. `readClassContext` reset `expectName` on a `,` child and on nothing else, so a `|` context joined by `&` published its first conjunct and dropped the rest. `&` is not a second construct: the child shape is identical with the token swapped (`| == a` -> `!| operator_compare type_variable` against `| == a & UList a` -> `!| operator_compare type_variable !& constructor type_variable`, clean-stdlib/StdOverloadedList.dcl:5,8), which is the same two-spellings-one-handler shape the `fixity` field is already handled for. Measured cost of the `,`-only reader (validation/m14/fixtures/clean/ampersand-context-probe.mts): 365 of the 1,995 WIDE `class_context` nodes carry an `&`, and the conjuncts such a reader drops split 249 that would ADD a row against 264 that name a class already published on the same line. Nothing is fabricated and nothing is mislabelled — an edge that should exist is silently absent, which is the failure a count-only check cannot see because the lane's `references` total goes DOWN rather than wrong. The mutant re-derives the `,`-only reader off `source`: for a `class_context` edge, take the line, cut the context at its first `|`, split on `&`, and drop the edge when its target appears only in a conjunct after the first. A line with no `|` keeps its edges, so the mutant drops only what it can show the pre-fix code dropped. Caught by clean/ampersand-class-context, whose rows at lines 36, 41, 57, 64, 70 and 72 are exactly the shapes this loses.

THE OPPOSITE ERROR TO THE ONE ABOVE, and the reason the dedupe is pinned by a COUNT row rather than by prose. `pushRel` collapses on `source|type|target|line`, so `| Ord Int & Ord Int & Size Int` publishes one edge to `Ord` and one to `Size` — two rows for three conjuncts. The mutant models the alternative that was live before this round settled it: publish one row per conjunct, so the repeated conjunct yields a SECOND identical `references` edge on the same line. Nothing is fabricated about the class — `Ord` really is required — and the edge is still correctly labelled; what is wrong is that the payload carries no multiplicity field, so the second row says nothing the first did not, and `bb_graph`'s edge count and `bb_impact`'s dependent count both rise for a file that did not change. 264 conjuncts at WIDE and 47 at TRACKED have this shape, so it is not a synthetic case: `| toReal a & toReal b & toReal c` is Clyde/Clyde/timeprofile.icl:337. Measured as an A/B on TRACKED (validation/m14/fixtures/clean/references-duplicate-probe.mts) the fix itself changed the count of `references` groups holding more than one edge by ZERO — 387 before, 387 after, identical per discriminator — which is the evidence that the shipped code does not do this. Caught by clean/ampersand-class-context through `expectRelationshipCount` on `repeated -> Ord` at line 96, `equals 1`: under this mutant the real count is 2.

PHANTOM DECLARATION CLASS, and the mutant that keeps the fix falsifiable. `processInstance` publishes a CONTAINER symbol to own an instance's members, and before this round it was named exactly the instance's TARGET TYPE: `instance == Collision where` published a symbol called `Collision` (kind `class`), so a file that declares `:: Collision = …` and an instance for it declared the name TWICE. The invented symbol is not a declaration of anything the source declares — an instance head is a TYPE EXPRESSION, not a name form. MEASURED on the 312-file population (validation/m14/fixtures/clean/phantom-census.mts, +244 / gates): 699 containers in 94 files, 112 distinct names, 150 of them not an identifier at all (`.a`, `[]`, `?`), and the incoming gate resolves on `declCount === 1` ALONE with no kind test, so the phantom did not merely add a row — it MADE RESOLUTIONS. Removing it moved 1,537 residual rows (Int 654 · Bool 426 · Char 320 · Files 50 · File 37 · World 24 · ABCInstructionEntry 17 · ParseError 3 · ParseWarning 3 · Tm 2 · Range 1) into the open, and 100.0% of them are attributed to a name only a container published (validation/m14/fixtures/clean/phantom-attribution.mts). This transform reverts the NAMING and the KIND the pre-fix code published, and moves every edge endpoint that named a container with it, so a fixture that only checks relationships still sees the phantom's own rows. Caught by clean/instance-target-name-collision on three pins: `expectSymbolCount Collision equals 1` (the mutant reads 2), `expectSymbols Collision::instance` (absent), and `forbidRelationships contains -> Collision at line 17` (the instance's containment reappears under the bare name).

THE .dcl/.icl TWIN CLASS, reintroduced. A Clean module is DECLARED in `.dcl` and IMPLEMENTED in `.icl`, so a module-level type, function, class or macro is ONE declaration written in TWO files — and the incoming gate collapses the pair only when every declaration carries the same NON-EMPTY `qualifiedName` that DIFFERS from the bare name (the store's file-scope fallback is `qualifiedName = name`, and a fallback is not a qualification). This analyzer published NO qualifiedName at module scope, so every such pair reached the gate as TWO declarations and the pair was counted as a name collision. MEASURED on the 312-file arm, whole population: `references` ambiguous 1,808 -> 1,011 (-797, exactly the collapse price measured before the change), `exports` 40 -> 12, and the gate's own collapsed-key count 719 -> 3,148 (1,287 of them NAME keys, the rest the new `Module.name` alias keys each symbol now also answers to). Held by the pin on `clean/declaration-forms` (`qualifiedName: CleanDeclForms.Sized` / `CleanDeclForms.MaxBound`), which fails the moment a module-level symbol loses the spelling; the class/instance MEMBER spellings (`Sized.sizeOf`, `Int.sizeOf`) are pinned beside it so a revert that qualified EVERYTHING is caught too.

The `.dcl` ruling reverted: a module-level `type_signature` publishes nothing, so a definition module's declared interface is invisible (measured: 2,002 distinct module-level signature names over the lane's 312 files, 708 published nowhere). Caught by clean/definition-module-interface — its expectSymbols entries for interfaceFunction/NSMakeSize/%./bitxor and their expectExports twins.

The merge resolved the WRONG way: the declaration's range wins instead of the definition's, so a merged symbol points at its prototype line. Caught by clean/signature-definition-merge's expectSymbolRanges (mergeTarget startLine 20 = the definition line; the declaration is 19).

The merge broken the other way: the declaration is kept BESIDE the definition instead of being replaced by it, so one name is published as two symbols. Caught by clean/signature-definition-merge's expectSymbolCount (`mergeTarget` equals 1) — measured catch, printed by script/m14/tmp/mutant-catch-reasons.ts; the same regression inside the analyzer's own export loop would additionally trip the exports-family invariant, which is why the fixture pins both halves.

THE SAME DEFECT ON THE OTHER END of the row: a resolver that publishes the row's SOURCE in the owner-qualified spelling, `owner::member`, instead of the leaf the analyzer publishes. The half that pins the SOURCE side of the spelling contract, and the half a target-only forbid cannot see.

D13, REVERTED. A friend function DEFINED inside a class body is not a member of that class, so its body's reads belong to the friend and not to the class. The defect this reverts is the one the lane MEASURED on absl/random/uniform_int_distribution.h:81-87, where the enclosing CLASS was published as the owner of a read of a PARAMETER — wrong twice over, because the class has members of the same name, so the edge cannot be told apart from reading those members. The mutant re-owns the friend definition's body's reads to the class, which is the pre-D13 behaviour verbatim.

CP2, REVERTED. A friend DECLARATION — `friend void helper();` — declares someone ELSE's function: it is not a member of the class and it mints no symbol of the class. The pre-CP2 analyzer minted a (private) Method for the inner declaration node, which is the defect CP2 removed. The mutant mints that member symbol again, from the SOURCE (the declaration's own spelling), so the revert is faithful rather than a hardcoded string.

W9, REVERTED — the operator spelling published INSIDE the class's member key space. The Lead's ruling L-2026-10-21-02 is that an operator spelling is not in the published key space of the class's members, and the lane's own measurement is the reason: the class has real members `a` and `b` AND an in-class friend `operator==` whose PARAMETERS are also named `a` and `b`, so publishing the operator as a class member would make `uses param_type -> b` undecidable. The mutant gives the friend operator a class owner and a `contains` edge from the class — the exact shape the ruling forbids.

THE REPLACEMENT FOR THE NO-OP `cpp/last-sig-wins-overrides` (in script/m14/mutate-analyzer.ts), and it is here because the rule is that a no-op's REPLACEMENT TRAVELS WITH IT. THAT MUTANT IS A NO-OP MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: it filters the override rows whose `metadata.reasonCode` is EXACTLY `signature-match` and whose source starts with `Derived.f` — but MEASURED on the current analyzer, the `Derived.f` row's reasonCode is `override-keyword+signature-match` (the `override-keyword+` prefix was added later), so the filter matches NOTHING and the mutant reports 0 -> 0 failures. A no-op is not a pass. This replacement models the SAME defect class at the CURRENT spelling: the virtual registry keeps one signature per method name, so the override of the first-declared base overload is silently dropped when the base also declares an overload of the same name. The filter drops the override row for the first-declared overload — the row the fixture cpp/ctor-and-overload-regressions pins as `overrides Derived.f -> f` with `meta.overriddenOwner: Base`.

The analyzer publishes each row's QUALIFIED SPELLING in `metadata.qualified` — the row's own qualified name, the thing a resolver needs and the thing W4 is about. This mutant drops it from every row, which is what a resolver that reads the leaf only would see. Caught by the fixtures that pin `meta.qualified` (14 pins across the lane's fixtures).

The analyzer publishes the OWNER of an overridden method in `metadata.overriddenOwner` — the base class the override belongs to, and the fact the `overrides` edge's spelling is carried by. Dropping it leaves the override row naming a base that no reader can resolve, which is the shape the cross-file override fixtures pin (34 pins across the lane's fixtures).

`implements` IS ADAPTED SEMANTICS in C++ — a PURE-VIRTUAL CONTRACT (a class declaring `= 0`) is a contract a derived class implements — and the analyzer publishes the fact in `metadata.isPureVirtual` ON THE MEMBER SYMBOL (and `metadata.isAbstract` on the class). Dropping it leaves the `implements` row asserting a relationship the reader cannot check against the contract that justifies it. MEASURED: the first version of this mutant dropped the flag from the RELATIONSHIPS and SURVIVED, because the flag lives on the SYMBOL — the pins are symbol pins, so a relationship-side drop is a NO-OP. It is the symbol-side drop that bites (9 pins across the lane's fixtures).

Every cpp row carries a `metadata.reasonCode` — WHY the row exists (the node type and the evidence class that produced it). Dropping it leaves the row asserting a relationship with no explanation, which is the state the reason-code fixtures exist to prevent (17 pins across the lane's fixtures).

Every cpp row carries a `metadata.evidenceClass` — the evidence class that produced it (`structural`, `import_based`, `usage_contextual`, `reference_qualified`, `inferred`). Flattening it to one constant makes every row claim the same evidence, which is a LIE about the corpus's own evidence and not a loss of detail (15 pins across the lane's fixtures).

M60.P1 regression, ARM A: reverts the parameter TYPE slice from the parameter's NAME node to its DECLARATOR node. A `reference_declarator`'s text is `& name` and its start index points at the `&`, so slicing at the declarator deletes the pointer/ref operator and publishes `const std::string` for `const std::string& name` and `const char` for `const char* format`. Not cosmetic: those are different C++ types that overload differently, and the same slice is the override-matching KEY (buildParamSig), so `virtual void f(Widget&)` and `virtual void f(Widget)` also hashed alike before the fix.

M60.P1 regression, ARM B: drops every DEFAULTED parameter. In this grammar a defaulted parameter is an `optional_parameter_declaration` — a DIFFERENT node type from a required `parameter_declaration` — so a walk that handles only the required one silently loses `double scale = 1.0` while looking correct on every undefaulted signature. The class is corpus-wide and invisible to a name/type pin that happens to sample an all-required signature.

M60.P1 regression, ARM C: publishes a deduced-return function's `auto` instead of the type after the `->`. The pre-fix read took the declaration's `type` field, which for `auto label() const -> std::string` is literally `auto` — a name that resolves to nothing, in the one field whose whole job is to name a type. Trailing return types are not exotic: they are how `decltype(auto)` and every deduced-return function is written.

M60.P1 regression, ARM D: drops `decorators` from every non-callable declaration, keeping it only for functions. `static constexpr int kAxes = 2;` carries exactly as much modifier information as `virtual double area() const = 0;`, so a payload field that answers for one of them and not the other is a field a consumer cannot rely on. A distinct arm from the others because it is a SCOPE restriction, not a wrong value: the function-branch values are all still correct, which is what makes it survive a fixture that only samples methods.

M60.P1 regression, ARM E: removes the one step that looks BELOW the declaration. `override` and `final` are `virtual_specifier` nodes in this grammar, children of the declarator rather than of the declaration, so a scan of the declaration's own tokens finds `virtual` and misses `override` — and `override` is the modifier that answers the question a reader actually has of an override edge. It is also the arm most likely to survive review, because the declaration-level modifiers are all still present.

M60.P1 regression, ARM F: scans only the DECLARATION for modifiers and not its DECLARATOR. A method's trailing `const` and its `override`/`final` `virtual_specifier`s are children of the `function_declarator`, so this arm drops `const` from every const method and every override — while leaving `static`/`virtual`/`explicit` intact, because those DO sit on the declaration. It is the arm most likely to pass review, since the modifiers a reader checks first are all still there, and `const` is on essentially every getter in a C++ corpus, so the loss is large and the signal is small.

D8 regression, arm A: re-publish the trailing annotation. A thread-safety annotation written after a parameter list decorates the declaration in front of it and declares nothing; the grammar recovers it as a second function_definition whose declarator is the macro and whose body is the real method's. Publishing it invents a member of the class — measured as `GTEST_LOCK_EXCLUDED_(mutex_)` with `expandedFrom: "macro-heading"`, 20 sites in one bundled gmock file — and attributes the real body's reads to the macro. Reverted generically: a no-return-type, all-caps function_definition whose invocation continues a declaration publishes nothing.

D8 regression, arm B: the SECOND half of the same defect, which is the one that was not obvious. Even with the phantom symbol suppressed, the stolen BODY is still a separate `compound_statement` node and reaches the macro-declared-body branch on its own — so the body's reads were attributed to the annotation. Reverted generically: the macro-declared-body branch is skipped when the body belongs to a trailing annotation, and the statements are walked with the enclosing owner instead of a macro's.

D8 regression, arm C — the CONTROL, and the one this lane needed most. A test-macro HEADING is the opposite of an annotation: `TEST(Suite, Name) { body }` genuinely defines the function it is named after, and `TEST` is spelled in all caps, so the macro-name test cannot separate the families. Two versions of the D8 rule deleted real headings (every heading following a function declaration, then 20 in one gmock file). This mutant deletes a heading to prove the fixture still fails when the rule over-corrects — a gate that only ever runs in the under-firing direction proves nothing about the direction that costs symbols.

D9 regression, arm A: stop minting the `#define` DECLARATION. A `#define` declares a name whatever its body — the C lane's #901 ruling, which this lane now shares — so the branch publishes function-like macros as `Macro` and object-like ones as `Constant`, sourced from the `preproc_def` node. Dropping it re-opens the measured gap: 3,870 `calls` edges in 82 files that name a macro the SAME file defines and that no published symbol could resolve. Reverted generically: no `preproc_def`/`preproc_function_def` node publishes anything.

D9 regression, arm B — the CONTROL, and the one this change most needed. D9 required REFINING two gated fixtures: `cpp/bare-macro-statements` and `cpp/macro-decorated-specifier` asserted that NO symbol of ANY kind may carry `FMT_END_NAMESPACE`/`EXPORT_API`, which is a coarser proxy than the invariant those files document in their own text (a phantom symbol of kind `variable` minted from specifier recovery). The pins are now kind-scoped, which is strictly more precise but is still a narrowing, and a narrowing that nothing tests is a gate that only half works. This mutant puts the ORIGINAL #915 fabrication back — a `variable` named after the macro — so the refined pin must still catch the defect it was written for. Without this, 'the fixture still passes' would prove only that the refinement was legal, not that it is still true.

D14 regression: collapse a macro-heading symbol's range back to the HEADING node. The fix extends it through the recovered function_definition, because on the measured shape (nlohmann-json tests/src/unit-class_const_iterator.cpp:14-15, where TEST_CASE's opening brace is on its own line) the heading node ends at the invocation while every edge the body emits lands hundreds of lines below. Reverted, the three headings in the fixture publish as 23-23, 37-37 and 45-45 while still owning edges at lines 25/27/28, 39/40 and 47/49/51/53. Reverting the range is enough to fail the fixture: expectSymbolRanges pins all three extents, so this needs no edge assertion to be caught — which is the point, since the defect IS the range rather than the edge set. MEASURED corpus-wide at HEAD: 39,787 macro-heading edges outside their owner's range across 1,076 offending symbols, of 234,111 owner-checkable edges; 0 after the fix.

D15 regression: drop macro-decorated classes back out, restoring what the grammar's recovery does to them. `class GTEST_API_ UnitTestImpl { ... };` is recovered as a function_definition whose specifier names the MACRO and whose real name is a bare sibling, so the specifier has no body of its own and the forward-declaration rule declines it — the class is never published, the bare sibling reads as a function declarator (so the class's own name is published as a FUNCTION), and the members lose their owner (HEAD published `UnitTestImpl` as a function at 27-27 with `value` and `cached_` unowned). This transform removes the class, re-adds the class's own name as a function, and strips its members' owners. `Reporter` goes entirely, since HEAD published no struct spelling at all. MEASURED corpus-wide at HEAD: 93 macro-decorated class declarations, 5 published, 88 lost; after the fix all 93 publish. The fixture's D11 control (`class Widget f();`) is not touched by this transform, which is why it can pass here while the elaborated-return-type shape still holds.

ONTOLOGY revert: drops every `imports` relationship while leaving the `imports[]` payload and the `references` twin alone — the exact state this lane was measured in (0 `imports` relationships over 269,352 on 1,200 roslyn files, 8,941 `references` rows already carrying metadata.isImport). Caught by csharp/import-export-edges, whose 9 `imports` expects all vanish.

ONTOLOGY revert: drops every `exports` relationship and keeps the `exports[]` payload — the shape the r lane's own comment describes ('the exported surface existed in the parse result but in no relationship, so it was absent from graph_usages' exports view and from relations.ts' declaration set'). Caught by csharp/import-export-edges (4 expects) and csharp/export-global-scope (1 expect).

CS-ONT4 revert: drops every `override` edge whose `overriddenMemberKind` is not `method`, which is the pre-fix state exactly — the only branch that pushed an OverrideTask was the method branch, so `public override int P => 1;` produced a symbol, a `contains` edge and a declared-type `references` edge and NO `overrides` edge. Found by the lane's own independent overrides oracle (cs-ont-07: 118 TRUTH-ONLY rows on 250 roslyn files), NOT by a fixture and NOT by the differential, because csharp's `overrides` is excluded from the compared set on both sides — which is why this class could sit under the DERIVATION finding unobserved. LABEL CLASS, and the confusion this language is most likely to fall into: the new `overrides` edges are relabelled `extends`. Both spell a kind of precedence between two declarations of one name, and CSS's own preprocessor DOES have an `extends`-shaped construct — SCSS `@extend .base` — so a lane reasoning from the family rather than from the measurement can pick the wrong word. It is the wrong word twice over: `extends` asserts type-level inheritance between two DIFFERENT names (a `calls`-shaped supertype relation CSS does not have), while `overrides` asserts a later declaration replaces an earlier one of the SAME name. Measured: 0 `@extend` directives and 0 type-declaration nodes in the whole corpus, so an `extends` edge here would name a relation the language never writes. Caught by css/keyframes-redefinition-overrides, which forbids `extends fade -> fade` and requires `overrides`.

FABRICATION CLASS on pass 2's new shape, and the expensive direction. The `--custom-property` redefinition rule is scoped to ONE declaration block, because two declarations of one property inside one block share origin, context, layer, specificity and importance, so CSS Cascade 5 §6.1 ("The last declaration in document order wins") makes the later one replace the earlier one outright. `:root { --x: 1px }` followed by `.dark { --x: 2px }` shares NONE of those: the two apply to different elements and the cascade chooses between them per element. The mutant drops the block scope and keys the rule by property name alone, so every cross-block pair becomes an `overrides` edge asserting a replacement that never happens. This is the class the workstream calls the most expensive mistake available — an edge between two REAL symbols (the lane publishes one `--x` symbol by name-identity, which is exactly why the two blocks are the same node), so no resolution check can catch it. Caught by css/custom-property-redefinition-overrides, whose `forbidRelationships` rows refuse `overrides --scoped -> --scoped` and `overrides --guarded -> --guarded` while requiring the same type for `--twice`, `--thrice` and `--conditional`.

SECOND FABRICATION DIRECTION on the same shape, subtler than the boundary one. `--guarded: 1px !important; --guarded: 2px;` does NOT redefine: CSS Cascade 5 §6.1 sorts IMPORTANCE above document order, so the later declaration LOSES to the important one and the edge would point the wrong way. The mutant drops the equal-importance guard, so every mixed-importance pair in a declaration block becomes an `overrides` edge. Caught by css/custom-property-redefinition-overrides, which forbids `overrides --guarded -> --guarded` while requiring the type for the three equal-importance pairs in the same fixture — so the guard cannot be satisfied by suppressing the whole shape either.

UNDERSHOOT on the same shape, and the one a naive implementation gets. The rule keys on "assigned twice in one block", which is what CSS Cascade 5 §6.1 actually says; it does NOT require the two declarations to be ADJACENT. `:root { --twice: 1px; --between: 2px; --twice: 3px }` still has the second assignment replace the first, because position decides and nothing between them competes. The mutant adds an adjacency requirement, so any interleaved redefinition is silently dropped — the type shrinks toward zero on real stylesheets while every adjacent case still passes. Caught by css/custom-property-redefinition-overrides, which requires `overrides --twice -> --twice` at the line of the THIRD declaration with `supersedesLine` naming the first, across an interleaved `--between`.

REGRESSION GUARD on pass 2's second fix, and the defect class is an ENDPOINT rather than a label. `@media` and `@layer` publish ONE symbol per name, at the first block, so a second block of the same query used to leave the symbol's recorded extent covering only that first block — while every rule of the later block kept a `contains` edge pointing at it. Measured over the whole admitted corpus before the fix: 7,257 of 25,181 `isMediaScope` edges (28.8%) and 40 of 505 `isLayerScope` edges (7.9%) carried a contained rule OUTSIDE the source symbol's line range, e.g. `bootstrap-grid.css` pointing `.col-sm` at L284 through a symbol recorded at L22-L26. The mutant reverts the widening, so every multi-block scope collapses to its first block again. Caught by css/scope-conditions-and-custom-properties, which writes the same `@media` query twice and asserts the containment edge for a rule in the SECOND block. The class matters beyond this lane: a `contains` edge whose endpoint is somewhere its target is not is what makes `bb_impact` on a scope name report the wrong rule set, and no resolution check can see it because the endpoint DOES bind.

UNDERSHOOT, and the exact defect the parse-tree rewrite of this branch fixed. The `isCustomMediaRef` edge used to be recovered from the media query's own TEXT: peel one leading `(` and one trailing `)` off it, then ask whether what was left begins with `--`. That answers `@media (--narrow)` and nothing else, because in `@media screen and (--wide)` nothing is peeled at the front — the string starts with `s` — so the reference is silently LOST even though the grammar hands it over as a `keyword_query` inside a `parenthesized_query`. The mutant reinstates that reach by keeping only the edges whose scope name is ITSELF a single parenthesised `--ident`, which is exactly the set the text version produced. Caught by css/custom-media-in-every-query-shape, whose `expectRelationships` rows pin the composed shape (`@media screen and (--wide) -> --wide`) and the negated shape (`@media not (--c) -> --c`); neither row exists under the old behaviour. The corpus cannot catch this one: `css-ontology-probe.ts` measures 0 `@custom-media` declarations across the whole admitted set, so the branch has no corpus occurrences and a fixture is the only instrument that can fail on it.

FABRICATION DIRECTION on the same branch, and the opposite of the mutant above — a fixture that pins only the positive shapes constrains a type that can be broken in the direction nobody checked. A custom-media reference is a `keyword_query` node, and so is a MEDIA TYPE: `@media print` and `@media speech` are `keyword_query` nodes in the same grammar, distinguished only by the `--` prefix. An implementation that keys on the node type alone therefore turns every media-type query into a reference, and each such edge names a `@media`-scoped rule as depending on a construct that is a device category, not a declaration. The mutant drops the prefix test. Caught by css/custom-media-in-every-query-shape, whose `forbidRelationships` rows refuse `isCustomMediaRef` targeting `print` and `screen`, while the same fixture requires four real references — so the guard cannot be satisfied by suppressing the whole branch.

ENDPOINT CLASS, on the field the lane's `lastPathSegment` pure-String helper produces and on which no css fixture pinned anything until this round. The `imports` edge is sourced from the importing stylesheet's own file name, taken as the LAST `/`-separated path segment, because that is how the store spells a file and how the module is written in the import itself. Two wrong separators produce a wrong source here and both are the same defect: splitting the path on `/` and taking index 0 drops every directory (`themes/scope-conditions-and-custom-properties.css`), and splitting on `.` drops the extension (`scope-conditions-and-custom-properties`). THE FIRST IS NOT REACHABLE FROM THE EDGE ALONE — once the source has been reduced to a basename there is no separator left in it to get wrong — so this mutant injects the second, which is. It is recorded that way rather than quietly, because a mutant suite that only counts survivors would otherwise have let a non-reachable mutant sit in the registry looking like coverage. Caught by css/scope-conditions-and-custom-properties, whose two `imports` rows now pin `from` as well as `target`; before this round every row constrained `target` only, so the mutant would have SURVIVED and the suite would have reported coverage it did not have. The pin was added BECAUSE the mutant was written — the fixture did not fail first and teach us, which is the direction a mutation-first lane works in and the reverse of the one this repo's M13 retrospective was about.

THE REPLACEMENT'S OWN FAILURE MODE, which is why the boundary is read off the tree. `atRulePrelude` used to find the end of an at-rule's prelude with `node.text.indexOf(block.text)` — a substring search from offset 0 of the node's text — so a prelude that CONTAINS the block's own text truncated at the wrong offset and published a scope name cut mid-word. The mutant reproduces the class from the published side: every at-rule scope symbol's name is re-cut at the first `(` in its OWN query text, which is where a text search lands whenever the query text also occurs inside the block (a `@supports (display: grid)` whose body repeats the condition, a `@media` prelude that names a selector the block also uses). Caught by css/custom-media-in-every-query-shape, css/scope-conditions-and-custom-properties and css/declarations-the-corpus-never-uses, all of which pin at-rule scope NAMES containing a parenthesised query — `@media screen and (--wide)`, `@supports (display: grid)`, `@container (min-width: 400px)`. Without this mutant the tree rewrite would have had no pin at all, since a boundary bug that only fires when a prelude repeats its own block text cannot be produced by a hand-written fixture without inventing that file.

FABRICATION CLASS, and the one this lane most nearly shipped by agreeing with a tool. `script/m14/differential.ts --lang css` reports 2 MISSING on the svelte sample, both `imports expected.css -> http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml`, derived from the `@namespace url(...)` lines in `packages/svelte/tests/css/samples/supports-namespace/expected.css`. The cheap way to make that number zero is this mutant: take each `@namespace` declaration the analyzer already publishes and republish its URI as an `imports` edge. The differential would then read 2/2 and every gate would go quiet. The edge is false. A namespace URI is a NAME that a prefixed type selector is compared against; the CSS syntax never dereferences it, so `imports` would assert this stylesheet pulls in an external resource, and `imports` is the relation that drives module resolution and the refactoring advice `bb_migrate` gives. The analyzer's existing edge is `references svg|a -> @namespace svg url(...)`, which says which selector depends on which declaration — strictly more than the file->URI edge the oracle wants. Caught by css/namespace-uri-is-not-an-import, whose `forbidRelationships` rows refuse `imports` targeting either namespace URI, in both the bare and the prefixed spelling. The `@import url("theme.css")` line in that fixture is what makes the refusal mean something: the mutant must still pass the positive `imports` row, so it is the namespace specifically being refused rather than an `imports` branch that never fires.

REGRESSION GUARD on an EXISTING emitted type, and the one the ontology's six questions call LABELLED. `animation: fade` names a `@keyframes` sequence, and the lane emits `uses .spinner -> fade`; the mutant relabels that edge `calls`. `calls` in this codebase means "invokes a callable declared elsewhere", and CSS has no callable to invoke — the whole `calls` question for this language is RULED on a grammar inventory of 103 node types with no function-definition production and 0 `@function` declarations on the tree. So a `calls` edge out of a stylesheet would name a construct the language does not have, and `calls` is the type `bb_migrate` most trusts. Caught by css/keyframes-redefinition-overrides, which forbids `calls .spinner -> fade`.

FABRICATION CLASS, and the guard half of pass 10's `@import` fix. `findImportNameNode` takes a direct `string_value` / `call_expression` child first, and failing that the first such node AT ANY DEPTH whose row equals the `@import` KEYWORD's own row. The row test is load-bearing and the mutant removes it: every quoted span in the file becomes a module the stylesheet imports. The shape it reproduces is measured on the corpus — `Documenter.jl/assets/html/scss/bulma/elements/button.sass` has an `import_statement` node spanning L2..L50 with ELEVEN `string_value` descendants, one at L2 (the real module) and ten at L47 (a `$breakpoints` map's "mobile", "small", "normal", "medium", "large", "tablet-only", ...). An unguarded traversal reaching those ten publishes ten `imports` edges asserting that this partial pulls in ten stylesheets it never names, and `imports` is the type that drives module resolution and the advice `bb_migrate` gives, so the cost lands on refactoring. Caught by css/recovered-import-shape-is-an-import, whose `$map: ( "a-key": 1, "b-key": 2, )` block puts both decoys INSIDE the `import_statement` node that spans L13..L19, and whose `forbidRelationships` rows refuse `imports` targeting `a-key` and `b-key`.

PAYLOAD CLASS on the same edge, and the bug a new branch invites. The recovered path returns a `string_value` NODE, and a node's text still carries its quotes; `unwrapUrl` is what turns `"../utilities/mixins"` into `../utilities/mixins`. A branch that forgets that call publishes the quoted spelling, which is a DIFFERENT string from the one every other language's import target uses and a different graph node from the unquoted one — so the same partial becomes two nodes and the edge binds to neither. The mutant rewrites every `imports` target to its quoted form, which is the shape of that mistake. Caught by css/recovered-import-shape-is-an-import, whose `forbidRelationships` rows refuse the three quoted spellings, and independently by css/namespace-uri-is-not-an-import, whose `expectRelationships` row requires `target: theme.css` unquoted.

The mutant that convicts the pass-11 `references` fix from the OTHER side. `currentSelector` is empty inside a `keyframe_block`, and the fix routes such a read to the enclosing `@keyframes` name instead; a revert to the pre-fix guard (`&& currentSelector`) makes every one of them vanish again. Measured over the admitted corpus that is 845 edges in 265 files, which is why this is a mutant and not a refactor: the corpus cannot see it, so the fixture must. Caught by css/keyframes-read-a-custom-property, whose four `expectRelationships` rows each name a keyframes name as the SOURCE and no other fixture in the lane emits an edge with a keyframes source at all.

The failure mode of naming an owner that CANNOT resolve. A keyframe STOP is not a name anything binds to — `to`, `50%`, `from` are anonymous positions — so an edge sourced from one names an endpoint the store will never resolve, and `bb_impact` on it returns nothing while claiming a dependency. The mutant re-sources every keyframes-owned read from the stop selector instead of the animation name. Caught by css/keyframes-read-a-custom-property, whose `forbidRelationships` rows refuse `references` from `to`, `50%` and `from`, and by nothing else in the lane.

The owner must be the NEAREST enclosing `@keyframes`, and the frame field resets per node rather than carrying (`let nextKeyframeScope = keyframeScope` is a reset, not a `||`). Carrying it would attribute a read inside a LATER keyframes block to the first one, so `@keyframes a { to { opacity: var(--x) } } @keyframes b { to { opacity: var(--y) } }` would emit `a -> --y` as well as `b -> --y` — two edges, one of which names the wrong animation, and the extra edge is a claim about a dependency that does not exist. The mutant makes every keyframes-owned read name a single fixed animation, which is the shape of that mistake. Caught by css/keyframes-read-a-custom-property, whose four rows name FOUR different owners (`slide`, `fade`, `never-declared`, `nested-in-media`) over FOUR different targets.

The pass-13 `contains` (at-rule scope) fix, reverted. `processMedia` builds the scope NAME from the at-rule's own prelude, so `@media A, B { }` publishes `@media A, B`; the pre-fix code handed `findChild` the FIRST query child and published `@media A`. That is not a cosmetic name: two lists differing only after the comma then share a name, and the identity merge folds two different conditions into one scope symbol together with their rules. The mutant restores the first-term name. Caught by css/media-comma-list-is-one-condition, whose two blocks share a first term and differ only after the comma, and by css/custom-media-in-every-query-shape, whose `@media (--a), (--b)` block the old code named `@media (--a)`. Neither fixture is reachable from a corpus number: `validation/m14/tmp/css-media-prelude-equivalence.ts` measures 102 comma lists against 0 `@custom-media` declarations in the admitted corpus, so a fixture is the only instrument that can see this.

The second half of the pass-13 fix, which the name half alone would have left inconsistent. `customMediaRefsInList` unions the reference walk over the statement's DIRECT query children; the pre-fix code called `customMediaRefsIn` on the first query child alone, so for `@media (--a), (--b)` it found `--a` and could not see that `--b` sits in a SIBLING query node. With only the name mutant applied the scope would be named for both declarations while the graph recorded one dependency — the under-description moved from the name to the edges. Caught by css/custom-media-in-every-query-shape, which now asserts BOTH `references` edges from the one comma-list scope, and by nothing else in the lane.

The stylesheet-module symbol reverted, which is the defect the fix removed. An `imports` edge's SOURCE is the importing stylesheet, and without a symbol carrying that name the store's per-file lookup misses and records `source_external` for an edge whose source is the file the reader is already looking at. This is a MISSING-NODE defect rather than a missing-edge one, and that distinction is why it needs its own mutant: every relationship in the fixture is still present and still correct, so a mutant set that only watches edges passes it. MEASURED over the 600-file window (`validation/m14/census/css-incoming-split.ts`): `imports` same-file-resolved edges 58 of 58 -> 0 of 58, and the whole-corpus `imports` source resolution 251 of 251 -> 0 of 251 (`css-parsefile-census-1286.json`, row `imports` srcPublished). Caught by css/stylesheet-is-the-module-symbol, whose `expectSymbols` row requires the basename with kind `module`.

The module symbol published under the FALLBACK name instead of the file's basename. `analyze` computes `importerName = lastPathSegment(filePath) || filePath || "stylesheet"`, and the third disjunct is a placeholder literal that exists so the `imports` edge always has a source string. Publishing the SYMBOL under that literal puts the placeholder into the symbol table, where every consumer reads it as a real name: `keepSymbol` does not reject it, the store indexes it, and a stylesheet whose path yields no basename would silently merge with every other such stylesheet under one node. This is the M60 R7 rule this analyzer already states about the `imports` source — the same defect, one field over — and it is cheap to reintroduce because the literal is three tokens away in the same expression. Caught by css/stylesheet-is-the-module-symbol, whose `forbidSymbols` row refuses a symbol named `stylesheet` while requiring the basename: a mutation to the fallback satisfies neither, so the fixture is red in both directions.

The `imports` target reverted to the verbatim specifier — the defect the fix removed, and the reason one edge had its two ends spelled by two different rules. The source is `lastPathSegment(filePath)` (`layout.css`); the target was `styles/layout.css`. No stylesheet symbol in the store carries a path separator, so the store's `WHERE project_id = ? AND name = ?` lookup can never join them. MEASURED over the 600-file window (`validation/m14/census/css-import-specifier-names.ts`, 58 import edges): 11 edges named a file that exists under the basename with that basename unique in its own repo, and all 11 were unreachable. Re-measured after the fix with `css-incoming-split.ts` at the same window: `imports` byEdge `U4-absent-corpus` 56 -> 33 edges, and the store outcome row `crossFileUnique` 0 -> 6. Caught by css/import-specifier-names-its-target, whose `expectRelationships` require `layout.css`, `theme.css` and `other.scss` while six `forbidRelationships` rows refuse the multi-segment spellings — so a partial fix that recovers only slash-bearing specifiers with a `.css` extension is still red on `other.scss`.

Every specifier reduced to its last segment, with no test for whether that segment names a stylesheet. This is the failure mode the extension test exists to prevent, and it is the dangerous direction of this fix because it makes MORE edges resolve: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Lato:400,400i` becomes `Lato:400,400i`, `@fontsource-variable/figtree/index.css` becomes `index.css`, and each then binds to whatever unrelated same-named file its project happens to hold. An edge that resolves to the wrong stylesheet is worse than one that resolves to nothing, because nothing downstream can tell them apart — `bb_graph`, `bb_impact` and `bb_migrate` all read a resolved edge as a fact. MEASURED in the same 58-edge window: 10 URL edges, 1 package subpath. The two exclusions are also what stop the fix being a fabrication generator at scale: 24 bare package names, and `tailwindcss` in particular DOES collide with a real file in this corpus, so recovering it would resolve to the wrong thing. Caught by css/import-specifier-names-its-target, whose `forbidRelationships` rows refuse `Lato:400,400i`, `figtree/index.css` and `index.css` — an implementation that recovers everything satisfies all eight `expectRelationships` and is caught only by these six.

R1 (3d4d7fa4) regression: a `qualified` name under a `constant_pattern` stops being read, so a switch case naming a declared enum member publishes no edge again. The pre-fix shape is not a guess — it is what the analyzer did for its whole life, because the string 'qualified' appeared NOWHERE in 2,784 lines of it: `mode == M.off` parses as `identifier(M)` plus `selector(.off)` and the DT-F pass saw the selector, while `case M.off:` parses as ONE `qualified` node and nothing read it. Two node shapes, same text, one handled. Recovery measured at the time: 2,405 edges over ProxiCall/lib, 516 naming a symbol declared in the same file, 0 relationships removed, 0 duplicates introduced. The transform deletes every `uses` edge carrying `isConstantPattern` — exactly the surface the fix added — and leaves the expression-shaped edge alone, so the fixture's CONTRAST pin (`sameTextInExpression -> recipientLookup`, already working before the fix) still passes and the mutant can only be caught by the pattern pins.

R2 (7c574834) regression: the type extractors' node allowlist loses `record_type`, so every Dart 3 record type vanishes from the payload again. All three extractors (parameter, return, field) accepted a fixed five-node list — type_identifier, function_type, nullable_type, void_type — and a record fell through every one: `void f((int, String) p)` typed its parameter `dynamic`, and `({int a, String b}) f()` published no return type at all, so the function looked untyped. DARTD6 and DARTD13 could both be right about their mechanism and still lose every record. The transform rewrites any record-shaped parameter or return type back to `dynamic`, restoring the pre-fix degradation exactly. Measured recovery at the time: 27 return types and 1 parameter over 1,294 ProxiCall/lib files, with 0 relationships changed.

reverts the two receiver-head reads (dart/typed-receiver-heads): an ANONYMOUS CLOSURE's own parameter list is handed to `extractParameters` as the body's previous named sibling and then searched for a CHILD list that is not there, and `collectDartLocalTypes` never reads `for_loop_parts` — so a typed closure parameter and a typed for-in variable lose the type the SOURCE writes and `Element.poke`/`Element.id` out of `closures`/`loops` revert to a bare `poke`/`id` carrying `receiverCause: receiverTypeUnknown`. The transform is the pre-fix output, not an erased row: the bare rows are RE-ADDED with the typing-gap cause, so the fixture must be caught by its expectations and its forbids independently. The method-parameter CONTROL (`calls methodParam->Element.poke`) is deliberately untouched — it was typed before the change — so a mutant that reverted the whole receiver pass could not pass for the same reason.

ONE READ of the typed-receiver-heads change: `extractParameters` stops accepting the `formal_parameter_list` it is handed as the body's previous named sibling, so a typed ANONYMOUS CLOSURE parameter loses its type while the METHOD parameter control keeps its own (a local function is unaffected either way — its body's sibling is a real `function_signature`). Kept separate from the for-in mutant because the change is TWO independent reads of the source and a single combined revert cannot show which one a green suite is resting on: this one is caught by `uses closures->Element.id` and `calls closures->Element.poke` together with their forbids of the bare rows.

THE OTHER read of the typed-receiver-heads change: `collectDartLocalTypes` has no `for_loop_parts` branch again, so `for (Element element in xs)` and its `final`/`await for` spellings bind the name and never read the type written beside it. Caught by `calls loops->Element.poke` and its forbid of the bare row — and by the fixture's `equals: 1` count, which is why the three spellings are one pin: a mutant that reverted only the `await for` arm would still leave the count at 1 and be caught only by the expect, so the count is the assertion that all three sites are read.

OVER-READS the source instead of under-reading it: the rule reads the type written INSIDE a Dart 3 record pattern, so `for (final (int n, Element element) in …)` types its binding and the pattern's `element.poke()` stops being bare. This is the DECLINE half of the typed-receiver-heads fixture — the type is in the source and it must still not be read, because DARTGAP1 re-scoped pattern bindings to its own bucket by measurement, not by this rule. Caught by the fixture's `forbidRelationships calls controls->Element.poke`, the row that would move if the scope ever widened; the untyped `var` for-in and the untyped closure parameter are the same claim at two other spellings.

THE COUNT HALF: the dedupe stops collapsing a key that has TWO producers in one file — a typed METHOD parameter's read and a typed CLOSURE parameter's read of the same member in `collapses` are one key and must be one row, so this re-emits the row and `expectRelationshipCount equals: 1` fails with 2. The duplicate carries the SAME line, deliberately: that leaves the `line_number` pin satisfied, so this mutant can only be caught by the count, and the line mutant below can only be caught by the line. Kept as two mutants because arm14's mechanism has two observables and a single mutant could not show which one a green suite was resting on.

THE LINE HALF: the dedupe keeps a LATER producer instead of the first, so `calls threeSites -> Element.poke` — three call sites of one key at three lines — reports a line that is not the first site's. The count is untouched (still one row), which is the whole point: this moved the reported evidence of an edge, and until `dart/dedup-first-producer` there was no pin on WHICH line survives a collapse anywhere in the suite. Real, not theoretical — arm14 measured the same effect on 374 real files (`calls main -> WidgetTester.getSize` surviving at line 3,597 before the change and 448 after).
