ER-D22 regression: each -nifs entry mints a SECOND Function symbol beside the declaration. attrs-er3 pins expectSymbolCount 1 for native, native2 and boot — a duplicate identity is what the pre-ER3 branch was written to do

ER-D28 regression: -export_type entries are exported as FUNCTION exports, so a type export and a function export of the same name/arity become indistinguishable. types-er3 pins kind=type on handle/0 and tree/0

ER-D20 regression: no import is classified external, so the file-dependency engine cannot keep an -import of an OTP module and an -include_lib of a code-path header out of internal resolution (M60/#910 is_external contract). attrs-er3 pins isExternal true for both and false for the project's own -include
-compile becomes a dependency, so `{inline, [helper/1]}` reads as a reference to a module named `inline`. attrs-er3 FORBIDS `references attrs_er3 -> inline` and `-> export_all`

ER-D28 regression: -optional_callbacks emits a reference edge. attrs-er3 FORBIDS `references attrs_er3 -> handle_info`; the attribute declares nothing — the names belong on the module symbol, which is the only place they are true
ER-D19 regression: OTP 28's `maybe … else … end` arms stop counting, which also silently flattens every case/receive/try arm. otp28-er3 pins pick at 3
ER-D18 regression: a comprehension stops counting as a decision point. otp28-er3 pins walk at 2 and patterns-er3 pins comp at 2
ER-D17 regression: andalso/orelse stop counting as branches. record-ops-er2 pins `guarded` at 4 (base 1 + two if-arms + one andalso)

ER-D26 regression: one symbol per fun_decl, which is what the pinned grammar's per-clause fun_decl shape invites. behaviour-otp pins handle_req/2 with clauseCount 2 as ONE symbol; the census measured 18,444 fun_decls for 18,409 clauses, i.e. the grammar gives every clause its own node

ER-D25 regression: `?MODULE() -> …` stops resolving to the module's own function, so 79 corpus function definitions disappear. edge-cases-er3 pins the edge_cases_er3/0 symbol, the `-export([?MODULE/0])` entry and `calls edge_cases_er3 -> logger`
a record field's TYPE stops naming types, so `-record(r, {f :: token()})` loses `references r -> token`. types-er3 pins `references state -> token`; otp28-er3 pins `references box -> integer`
ER-D4/ER-D16 regression: a record named inside a TYPE is read as a construction. types-er3 FORBIDS `instantiates wrapped -> state`; the record's edge there is a type dependency

ER-D36 regression: counts a BARE unquoted atom in type syntax as a type dependency again. In Erlang `-type day() :: monday | tuesday.` declares the ATOMS monday and tuesday — you must write `monday()` to apply a type — so every such edge is fabricated, resolving to a same-named type or record property elsewhere in the file. This is the M12 false positive that started the ER3 wave: the differential went 1.000 -> 0.784 with 19 of them, two of them this exact shape (`job -> id`, `job -> kind`, the map keys of a map type). types-er3 FORBIDS `handle -> ok`, `handle -> error` and `payload -> undefined` while still REQUIRING the applied `binary()`, `request()` and `reply()`, so the mutant has to be selective to survive

ER-D37 regression: a `-nifs` entry with no Erlang clause is dropped instead of published, so every call to a NIF dangles with nothing in the graph saying a function was declared. The pre-fix code asserted "a NIF always has an Erlang-visible stub"; the compiler accepts `-nifs([n/1])` with no `n/1` anywhere in the file, so the assertion is false. imports-and-try REQUIRES nif_one/0 and nif_two/1 AND their `contains` edges at the -nifs line, so removing the symbols alone is not enough to be caught
ER-D15 regression: a second -module overwrites the first, so every module-scoped edge follows the wrong owner. Measured in the pre-ER3 code, where the attribute was assigned unconditionally

ER-D35 regression: treats EVERY macro in remote-module position as `?MODULE` and substitutes this file's module, inventing a self-call that is nowhere in the source. Measured on otp/lib/debugger/test/line_number_SUITE.erl and otp/lib/dialyzer/test/r9c_SUITE_data/src/inets/httpd_acceptor.erl, where `?FILE_MODULE:acceptor(A,B,C,D)` was reported as `httpd_acceptor:acceptor`; 922 fabricated edges over the corpus. macro-module-er3 FORBIDS the self-call and the bare leaf, while dispatch-er3 keeps the legitimate `?MODULE` self-dispatch pinned

ER-D34 regression: reverts `-module(?MACRO)` to requiring a bare atom under the attribute, so a module that names itself through a macro emits NO module symbol and the file falls back to being owned by its path. Measured on otp/lib/kernel/test/file_SUITE.erl (`-module(?FILE_SUITE).`), the only such file in the 4,326-file corpus; the attribute carries a macro_call_expr, never an atom. modname-macro-er3 REQUIRES the module symbol and its macro reference

ER-D34 regression, the subtle half: mints the module symbol under the MACRO's own name (MODNAME) instead of what it expands to (modname_macro_er3). Every consumer of a module symbol — exports, imports, cross-module calls — would then look for a module no compile can produce. modname-macro-er3 pins the module name AND meta.expandsTo

ER-D33 regression: `contains` carries the CONSTRUCT's line (range.startLine) instead of the NAME's line. Found by the 400-file corpus draw, missed by the 150-file one: otp/lib/snmp/src/manager/snmpm_net_if.erl defines worker/4 in two -ifdef/-else branches, so the -define( keyword sits on 208 and 219 while the macro names are on 209 and 220. line-owner-er3 FORBIDS the construct lines and REQUIRES the name lines for a macro, a function-like macro, a record and a type

ER-D32 regression: reverts the owner fallback for MODULES-scope declarations to the bare pre-pass module name, so in a module-less include fragment (no -module at all - OTP's own merl examples are written that way) macros lose their owner entirely while the function beside them keeps the file-path owner. fragment-er3 REQUIRES the macro's contains edge, which only exists when the macro is owned

ER-D38 regression: derives edges from a file the grammar could not read. Not every Erlang file is Erlang to this grammar — wx's api_gen sources are code-GENERATION TEMPLATES (`<<EXPORT:SortItems sortItems/2 SortItems:EXPORT>>`) and OTP's pre-R16 `-module(Name, Params)` is unparseable — and what comes back is a run of top-level ERROR nodes with loose call/atom fragments between them. Everything derivable from that wreckage describes structure the source does not have. Caught by the full-corpus dual lens as 55 analyzer-only edges in wxListCtrl.erl alone (`calls wxe_util:get_cbId@31` and thirty more, line numbers that are error recovery rather than source). grammar-damaged-er3 FORBIDS the recoverable call and the recoverable symbol and REQUIRES zero of each

ER-D32's edge half: `currentSource` falls back to the module name alone instead of the file path, so in a module-less include fragment a FILE-SCOPE edge has no source and pushRel drops it silently — no error, no counter. Found on otp/lib/stdlib/test/epp_SUITE_data/mac2.erl, which is four `-define` blocks and one `-plupp({?p, ?'p', ?P, ?'P'})` with no module and no function: the analyzer published the four macro constants and their `contains` edges (the macros exist) and published nothing saying they are USED. fragment-file-scope-er3 REQUIRES both file-scope macro references

ER-D39 regression: every `-define` is published as kind=constant, the state before the audit split it. A function-like macro (`-define(SCALE(X), X*2)`) claims to be a value, so the store's LSP identity list cannot tell a macro from a constant and `macro` — one of the 25 kinds in SymbolKind, emitted by 8 analyzers — is emitted by no Erlang symbol at all. export-import-macro-er3 pins SCALE as kind=macro and LIMIT as kind=constant, so dropping the split is caught on both halves of the line.

ER-D40 regression: `-export`/`-export_type` reaches the store as ExportInfo only, so no `exports` relationship exists and the module's public surface is indistinguishable from mere membership (`contains`). 16 analyzers emit this label; without it the type is stored and compared against nothing. export-import-macro-er3 pins one `exports` edge per `fa` in each attribute.

ER-D41 regression: `-import(Mod, [f/a])` emits only `references`, so the module-dependency pass that reads `imports` (brain_import rows, dependencies.ts:27-28, relied on precisely because resolved_symbol_id is often null) cannot see an Erlang import at all. 19 analyzers emit `imports`. The mutant removes the dependency and keeps the mention, which is the honest pre-fix state: the fact was recorded under a label nothing read.

PRE-FIX (FS-D2): a `type X with …` is F#'s only way to add members to a type declared elsewhere, so it is not a declaration of X. The grammar wraps every extension in a `type_definition`, and the branch minted a second Class symbol named after the extended type. Measured: 54 duplicate type symbols per 400 real files, every one a `type_definition` + `type_extension` pair at the same line. Reverted by re-publishing a symbol for each the analyzer itself marked `isTypeExtension` — read off the result's own metadata, so the mutant cannot silently stop matching if a fixture changes. The pre-fix extension ALSO produced `contains X -> X` (the containment pass emitted an edge for every symbol with an owner), so a faithful revert re-adds both: a first draft re-published the symbol alone and SURVIVED, because the fixture's forbid rows pin the EDGE. Caught by fsharp/type-extension-and-containment, which pins ONE `Foo` with both the declaration's and the extension's members owned by it, and forbids the six self-edges naming all three sources of the FS-D3 class.

PRE-FIX (FS-D3): `contains` was emitted for every symbol with an owner, so a name could contain itself. Measured: 368 self-edges per 400 real files from three distinct sources — a DU case named after its own type (305; `type TypeProviderDesignation = TypeProviderDesignation of string` is a real, common F# spelling), a member named after its own type (3: `E.E`, `MatchClause.Pattern`, `Map.Map`), and the type_extension of FS-D2. The refusal belongs at COMPOSITION, where the labels are composed, because the DU case genuinely IS contained by its union — suppressing the label instead would lose a real fact. Reverted by re-adding every dropped self-edge. Caught by fsharp/type-extension-and-containment, whose six forbid rows name all three sources.

PRE-FIX (FS-D4): the R9 declared-type reference graph was absent from this lane entirely. script/m60/declared-type-refs-census.ts measured `absent` WITH THE CONTROL PRESENT — the snippet parses, the holder symbol is walked, and the lane emitted no type reference of any kind. Thirteen lanes emit it; rust's own R13 header calls it a family standard. An absent capability emits nothing, so no per-edge oracle can adjudicate it, which is why it survived: every gate the lane had asked whether an edge that EXISTS is right. Reverted by dropping every `references` edge marked `declared_type`. Caught by fsharp/declared-type-graph (all seven positions) and fsharp/call-ownership (the class-field, parameter, local and return positions).

PRE-FIX (FS-D6): an `identifier_pattern` in this grammar spans the ENTIRE left-hand side of a binding, so `let f (a: string) : string = …` published the symbol `f (a: string) : string`. Measured: 60 such symbols per 400 real files — 37 with a curried argument list, 23 with a generic argument in the return type — none joinable by a consumer; script/m14/tmp/fs019-adjudicate-loss.ts counts the removed names by the character that disqualifies them (57 by a parameter list, 16 by a generic argument, 9 by a space, 8 otherwise). Reverted by renaming every function/variable/method symbol to the whole text of its binding's left-hand side, which is what the identifier_pattern's own text is. A first draft guarded the revert with 'only if a signature-shaped name is already present' — which made the mutant PERMANENTLY VACUOUS, since the fixed analyzer never produces one; a vacuous mutant is a green that means nothing, and the probe that found it is script/m14/tmp/fs023-mutant-probe.ts (whose own first version called four LIVE mutants vacuous, because it compared counts on a map-shaped transform). Caught by fsharp/name-surface, whose forbids name the four exact pre-fix strings and whose control bindings (`plain`, `curried`, `lambdaArg`, `counter`) exist because a first draft of the FIX that also redirected the plain-identifier case regressed them and the A/B reported them as dropped symbols.

PRE-FIX (FS-D7): an `object_expression` published a Class symbol and never opened a scope for it, so in an F# SCRIPT — no namespace, no module, an empty enclosing scope — every member of every object expression came out with NO owner. Measured on the second corpora: elmish docs/docs/subscription.fsx lines 71/144/803/833, suave examples/WebSocket/Program.fs:181, fsharp-data HtmlNode.fs:123 and 206. Reverted by removing the owner AND its containment edge from every member of an object expression — the edge is derived from ownerName, so a revert that cleared only the owner is not a state the pre-fix analyzer could produce; the first draft did exactly that and SURVIVED, because the fixture pins the edge. Caught by fsharp/name-surface, which expects `contains new System.IDisposable -> Dispose` and forbids the scope from outliving the object expression (`contains Fixture.Names -> after` is the live risk: a scope that does not pop captures the next binding).

FS-D2 REGRESSION GUARD, and the only mutant whose job is to fail if a bug this round once shipped returns. An F# SIGNATURE file forward-declares a type and then defines it — `type Surface` / `type Surface = member this.Real = 1` — and the definition is the one carrying the members. A first draft of the publication rule applied one-symbol-per-name to every type, kept the forward declaration and dropped the definition: script/m14/tmp/fs018-compare-dumps.ts reported 30 dropped `type_definition` symbols across 15 corpus files (fsiaux.fs, TypedTree.fsi, TaggedCollections.fsi, sformat.fsi) before the rule shipped, and the fix was to scope the dedupe to EXTENSIONS — the one place the duplication is a defect. Reverted by dropping every symbol marked `isForwardDeclaration` and the containment edge into it, which is what the draft did. Caught by fsharp/type-extension-and-containment, which expects `contains Fixture.Extensions -> Surface` at BOTH line 72 and line 74 and expects the member `Real` owned by Surface.

PRE-FIX (FS-D8): the export list was 'every non-variable symbol', so a record field, a method and an object expression's member were published as importable units no F# `open` can bind, and an `internal` or `private` declaration was published with `visibility: public`. Two independent facts, and the fixture runner's own export invariant is what caught them — `export(s) […] do not resolve to a top-level symbol (membership rides Contains)` and `duplicate export name(s) ["Surface"]`. Reverted by re-running the pre-fix rule verbatim, because a first draft rewrote only `visibility` and could not change the invariant's verdicts, so the mutant was VACUOUS. Caught by fsharp/declared-type-graph (whose `Bad<'T>` carries `val mutable` members and an `inherit Object()`) and fsharp/name-surface (whose object-expression members are type-owned).

PRE-FIX (FS-D13): the 'a computed property getter emits no calls' contract was applied to the WHOLE member. It is inherited from the C# family and is about an EXPRESSION-bodied property, which in C# has no second body for code to live in. F#'s `with get, set` does: the accessor is a `property_accessor` node carrying its own `set` token, and the setter body executes. Reverted by dropping every `calls` edge whose source publishes a `declared_type` on its own PARAMETER — which is the shape a setter's parameter produces, read off the result rather than from a name list, so the mutant cannot silently stop matching if the fixture changes. Caught by fsharp/call-ownership, which expects `calls Probe -> reset` AND forbids `calls Computed -> Length`; the forbid is what stops the fix being read as 'properties emit calls'.

PRE-FIX (FS-D12): a `default` implementation of an abstract member publishes no SYMBOL — that dedup is correct and is exactly why the abstract signature is the canonical one — but its BODY belongs to that member, and the arm passed the enclosing owner through unchanged. Inside a class the enclosing owner is undefined, so every call in every `default` implementation was dropped: 731 of 817 MISSING `calls` rows per 120 real files, found by the lane's own truth oracle. Reverted by re-attributing every call whose source also has a `member_signature` of the same name in the file — the exact set of `default` implementations, derived from the result rather than from a name list. Caught by fsharp/call-ownership, which expects `calls Describe -> describeWith` and `calls Area -> computeArea`.

PRE-FIX (FS-D11): `typeof<T>` and `unbox<T>` are EXPRESSIONS that carry a type argument, not positions where a type is WRITTEN. `typeof<TypeInThisAssembly>.Assembly.Location` depends on a runtime value, and a `declared_type` edge claims the opposite. It first appeared as an UNEXPLAINED row in the lane's own differential — the two sides agreed to emit the edge and disagreed on its SOURCE, which is the tell that both were reading a position neither should have taken. Two attempts at the discriminator measured nothing before the differential forced a third: the grammar spells the query as a `typed_expression` whose `long_identifier_or_op` child reads `typeof` — a SIBLING of the type, not its parent. Reverted by re-adding a `declared_type` edge for every declared type attributed to an ARGUMENTLESS binding, which is the shape a top-level `let x = typeof<T>.…` produces. Caught by fsharp/call-ownership, whose forbids name `quoted -> Foo` and `unboxed -> int`, with `annotated : Bar` as the control that a real written type in the same position still emits.

PRE-FIX (FS-D9): the R10 SPELLING rule — 'a qualified type USE is published under the name the lane would publish for that type as a symbol' — was not implemented, so `implements` and `extends` targets carried the full dotted path (`System.IDisposable`), which joins to no symbol. R10 is the family rule, applied to ten lanes; fsharp was never asked. Measured: 13 dotted `implements` and 3 dotted `extends` targets per 400 real files, found because the lane's own truth oracle applies the rule independently and the differential reported the disagreement. Reverted by re-expanding every `implements`/`extends` target through its own `metadata.qualifiedType`. The `open X` `references` rows are deliberately NOT touched: a module PATH is legitimately dotted and its leaf is not the module, so R10 does not apply to it. Caught by fsharp/name-surface, which expects the leaf targets `IDisposable` and `IComparable`.

PRE-FIX (FS-D14): an object expression's interface name was read as the FIRST `long_identifier` descendant. That is correct exactly when the name is unqualified; a qualified name is NESTED in this grammar — `object_expression > typed_expression > dot_expression > long_identifier_or_op > long_identifier` — so the first such node is the first SEGMENT. `{ new System.Collections.Generic.IEqualityComparer<T> with … }` published `new System` and `implements -> System`, a target that resolves to no symbol. Found by the differential in the most useful way available: the lane's truth side read the SECOND segment (`Collections`), so two implementations independently picked different segments of one name. Reverted by re-expanding the published name and the `implements` target to the first segment of the qualified form, using the result's own `metadata.qualifiedType` rather than a name list — which also makes the mutant fail if the qualified form is ever absent, rather than silently matching nothing. Caught by fsharp/name-surface, which forbids `implements -> System` and `implements -> Collections` alongside the correct leaf row.

PRE-FIX (FS-D17): the source of an `open` was `wherever the walk happened to be`, and in this grammar an `open` is a SIBLING of the file's `module` declaration rather than a child of it — so a scope stack maintained by walking down the tree is empty when the walk reaches one. The rule that produced the answers was position, and position is not a property of the program: `AssemblyCheck.fs` (`open` at line 3, `module` at 10) was sourced to the module because the walk had entered it, and `docs/fcs/project.fsx` (same shape) was sourced to `Global` because the walk had not. Two files, one rule, two answers. Reverted by re-sourcing every open-path `references` edge to `Global`. The fix is a pre-pass over the file's declared scope, gated on there being exactly ONE top-level module/namespace and on nothing EXECUTING above it — the second condition is what keeps a script's top-level imports out of its first module, and the extra `module M` / `module N` in project.fsx are inside triple-quoted strings, so counting module nodes alone is not enough (script/m14/tmp/fs036-top-level.ts). Caught by the oracle, which is where both of the disagreeing files were adjudicated.

PRE-FIX (FS-D29): `let rec f … and g …` is ONE `function_or_value_defn` holding both clauses, and two things read the FIRST left-hand side. The symbol publication minted only `f` — so `g` did not exist at all — and the declared-type attribution named the group by its first clause, so `g`'s parameter and return types were published as `f -> …`. Measured on TypedTreeOps.Attributes.fs: `visitEntity -> Entity`, `-> Val` and `-> TypedTreeNode` all published as `visitVal -> …`, in a corpus written almost entirely in this shape; and 24 rows in Symbols.fs for the same reason. Nothing downstream could tell, because `visitVal` IS a published symbol and the edges resolved. Reverted by attributing every declared-type row to the LAST function-or-variable symbol in the result — the pre-fix shape, where one name carries a whole group. Caught by fsharp/declared-type-graph, whose mutual group at lines 73-77 pins four rows that split by OWNER: `groupFirst -> GroupDep`, `-> GroupSecond` and `groupSecond -> GroupSecondDep`, `-> GroupFirst`.

A defect in the lane's own TRUTH ORACLE, reverted here because a differential finds bugs on both sides and a mutant is the only way a truth-side bug stays fixed. The oracle refused EVERY label's self-edge, on the reasoning that a self-edge is a statement about the graph rather than the code. That is true for `contains` and FALSE for `calls`: `let rec f x = … f (x-1) …` really does call itself, and refusing the edge deletes a true fact about the program. Measured: 668 UNEXPLAINED rows per 200 real files, every one of them a recursive call the analyzer was RIGHT to emit. The analyzer's own refusal is already per-label (see the composition site); this mutant restores the blanket version on the ANALYZER's output so the fixture that pins `calls loop -> loop` — a true recursive call that must survive — goes red. Caught by fsharp/call-ownership, whose last forbid row states the two rules are per-label on purpose.

M60 ontology lane: ER-D41's shape in F#. `src/intelligence/analysis/dependencies.ts` reads `imports` relationship edges for file->file module dependencies, relying on them precisely because `brain_import.resolved_symbol_id` is routinely null — 19 analyzers emit `imports`, and F# recorded `open X` under `references` alone, so an `open FSharp.Compiler.Diagnostic` was stored under a label that reader never looks at. Reverted here by dropping every `imports` edge the analyzer emits, which is the honest pre-fix state: the mention survives and the dependency does not. Caught by fsharp/import-and-use, whose five `imports` rows (two `open`, one `open type`, `#r`, `#I`, `#load`) go missing while its two `references` rows stay green — so the mutant is caught by the ABSENCE of the dependency and not by any change to the mention.

M60 ontology lane: the `#r`/`#load`/`#I` rule reads the directive's keyword off the tree and accepts three of the six keywords `fsi_directive_decl` covers. Accepting the NODE TYPE instead emits an import for `#time "on"`, `#help` and `#quit`, which are REPL controls touching no resource outside the file — a fabricated dependency, the most expensive mistake available, because a fake dependency is counted as a fabrication by the oracle and poisons bb_graph, bb_impact and bb_migrate, where it becomes wrong refactoring advice. `#time` is the load-bearing case and not a contrived one: it CARRIES a string (`#time "on"`), so a rule that keyed on 'has a string argument' would emit the edge too, and only the keyword test refuses it. The two targets are F#'s two documented `#time` arguments. THIS IS AN INJECTION, NOT A BYTE-FAITHFUL REVERT, and the reason is stated rather than papered over: the pre-fix rule's extra edges leave NO trace in a result the analyzer refused to produce — no symbol, no relationship, no ImportInfo row — so a transform over the result cannot recover them, and a revert written against the source would be a text match, which is the instrument this project has twice measured to be wrong. What it asserts is exactly the defect: does the suite go red when an `imports` edge exists that names no resource? Caught by fsharp/import-and-use, whose forbid row for target `on` exists for this and nothing else.

M60 ontology lane, and a REGRESSION guard for a bug this lane's own round introduced and then removed. `[<return: Struct>]` and `[<assembly: CompilationRepresentation(…)>]` carry an attribute `target` field; the rule skips it by asking the tree for the field name at each child index. The pre-fix version skipped it by OBJECT IDENTITY (`c === attrTarget`), which does not hold — web-tree-sitter rebuilds the Node wrapper on each accessor call, so the comparison was false for the very child it meant to skip, and the variance keyword became the dependency. Measured: 11 `uses` edges in a 200-file draw whose target was the literal string `return`. Without this mutant, a rule that was wrong once is free to be wrong again, and the failure is invisible downstream because a fabricated target resolves to nothing while a real one resolves to a symbol. Caught by fsharp/import-and-use, whose forbid rows for `return` and `assembly` exist for this and nothing else.

M60 ontology lane pass 2, and a REGRESSION guard for the defect this lane's own pass 1 shipped. `override` is not a statement about a BASE CLASS: F# has no separate keyword for an interface member, so `interface I with override this.M() = …` implements `I.M` and the pre-fix rule — which read the `override` TOKEN alone — emitted `overrides Owner.M -> M` when the type had no `inherit` at all (a member that overrides itself, a target binding to nothing) and `overrides Owner.M -> Base.M` when it also inherited (an interface implementation attributed to a base-class member). Measured over the whole 6,619-file corpus by validation/m14/fixtures/fsharp/ontology-probe.ts, probes A1 (the population) and A2 (the subset with no base type to resolve). The mutant reverts the TARGET RESOLUTION rather than the edge: it rewrites each `interface_member_implementation` edge's target to the member's bare name, which is the pre-fix answer for the no-`inherit` case and the sharpest possible fabrication for the rest. Caught by fsharp/override-target, whose three forbid rows pin each of the three wrong answers — including `Guarded.Speak -> Animal.Speak`, where the wrong target names a member that REALLY EXISTS in the base class, which is why the defect survived a corpus census: a fabricated edge that resolves is indistinguishable from a correct one by name alone.

M60 ontology lane pass 2. `calls` was gated on `fnName.length > 1`, which no property of the program justifies: by the time the branch runs, the grammar has already said the callee is a NAME node. The gate removed every call to a ONE-LETTER function, of which instrument B counts 5,313 over the 6,619-file corpus in 735 files — 2.2% of the label against its 246,327 full-extent edges — and the dropped population is better connected than the emitted one (32.4% in-file resolution on a 120-file draw against 22.2%). The mutant drops the edges a one-character target carries, which is the honest pre-fix state: the application is in the tree and nothing is published about it. Caught by fsharp/one-char-calls, whose `composed -> f` row exists for this and nothing else. It is a REGRESSION guard in the strict sense — the gate was in the lane since M12 and no fixture asserted its absence, which is why 5,313 real calls could sit unread behind a green suite.

M60 ontology lane pass 2, and the largest single `calls` gap this lane ever shipped. The lane's doc claimed pipe `a |> List.map` reads as a call, and it read one only when the pipeline sat in CALLEE position (`f (x |> g)`); a `let` whose BODY is the pipeline — the shape F# is actually written in — produced no edge at all. Measured on a 300-file corpus draw: 1,043 bare `|>` infix nodes with a NAME on the right, against 580 read in callee position, so ~11% of the corpus's calls were missing from the label. `script/m14/fsharp-truth-oracle.ts` has no `infix_expression` branch either, which is why the differential never reported it: both sides said nothing, so nothing disagreed. The mutant drops the pipeline edges the analyzer now emits. Caught by fsharp/one-char-calls, whose `applyBoth -> triple` row (metadata `isPipelineCall`) exists for this and nothing else, and whose three forbid rows — composition `>>`, a lambda on the right of a pipe, and `x = y` — are what stop a from-scratch implementation of the rule from passing by emitting far more than it should.

The reason a target carries is decided AFTER the walk, from the FINISHED published set, because the two halves of the question are answered at different times: the KIND of name is known when the edge is emitted, whether THIS FILE declares it is not — a type declared further down the file is still this file's declaration, and a mid-walk membership test would call it external. M60 ontology lane pass 7, FS-P7-1's SOURCE half. A `contains` edge names its parent by IDENTITY when the file has exactly one symbol of that name, by its own name when the parent is a top-level unit (which IS its own name), and by the bare name when two declarations share it with different identities — the last case is 30.4% of the draw's 58,298 `contains` edges, and the first draft of the classification called EVERY module-scoped edge `ambiguous-owner-name` because `publish` mints no fqn for an unowned symbol, which is a claim about the corpus that is false. PRE-FIX (FS-P9): `type A = … and B = …` is ONE `type_definition` node holding a clause body per type, and the analyzer read the declaration from the NODE — so the group was named after its FIRST clause, every later clause was published nowhere, and every later clause's members were published under the first name. Measured on the 3,000-file draw (.tmp-probe/fs-p10-groups.mts, arm rows-pass13-meta.ndjson): 79 groups in 67 files, 182 clauses after a first, 161 of those names published nowhere — while the members were not missing at all but ATTACHED WRONGLY, which is the half a missing-name count cannot see: `ConcatBuilder.GroupOwn` is a published symbol, so a containment edge or a call landing on it RESOLVED and nothing downstream could tell it named the wrong type. The fix re-dispatches each clause through the same type branch as a marked walk frame (`asTypeUnit`), so the kind classifier, record fields, DU/enum cases, interface implementations, `extends` edges, member scoping and containment composition are one implementation for both shapes. Reverted here by collapsing each mutual group to its first clause: the later clause's symbol is DROPPED, its members keep their spans but take the first clause's owner and fqn, and every edge endpoint that named the group's later clause is rewritten to the first — which is exactly the pre-fix shape (a resolved edge naming a declaration the source did not mean). The group is identified in the OUTPUT by the only signal the output has: two type-kind symbols with the SAME owner whose declaration lines are adjacent, which is what an `and` clause is once the `and` token is gone. Caught by fsharp/mutual-type-group, whose four shapes pin an OWNER each and whose two `expectRelationshipCount` rows pin the totals a per-row expect cannot state.

FS-P16/17 — the PROJECT-INDEX refinement, reverted. The analyzer reads `context.projectIndex` (built once per run, shipped with every batch) and turns the classes that mean 'not this file' into classes that say WHICH 'not this file': `bare-external` -> `in-project-name`, `external-type` -> `in-project-type`, `external-type-or-module` -> `in-project-type-or-module`, `external-namespace` -> `in-project-namespace`, `base-member-external` -> `base-member-in-project`, `interface-member-external` -> `interface-member-in-project`. The last two classes added are the FS-P17 channels (a module owner and a namespace path), and they are in this one map because the defect they revert is the same defect: an analyzer that never reads the index. The pre-fix state is exactly an analyzer that never reads the index, which is what this transform restores — the classes go back, and the markers the refinement writes (`projectIndexRefined`, `baseInProjectLacksMember`) go with them, because a run that never refined cannot have written them. Measured price of the rule it reverts: 32,778 of the 179,481 edges whose class said 'not this file' get a sharper reason on the lane's 3,000-file draw, and the population is named per class in `docs/analyzers/fsharp.md` pass 16. Caught by fsharp/fs-p10-project/fs-p10-client, whose positive rows assert the refined classes and whose FORBID rows name the pre-fix ones — a fixture that asserted only the positives would be satisfied by a run that emitted both, which is why both halves exist. The index is not a guess: with no index the analyzer is byte-for-byte its old self, so this mutant is also the pin on that property.

THE R3 REMEDY (2026-10-22), REVERTED: a `#load` directive is a TEXTUAL INCLUDE — the named file is compiled as part of THIS compilation unit, shares this file's single scope, imports nothing, and cannot be resolved as a separate module — so it is a `part_of` row, not an `imports` row. Before the remedy the analyzer read the directive's keyword and published ALL THREE of `#r`/`#load`/`#I` as `imports` (measured over the whole admitted population: 838 `#r` sites, 99 `#I` sites, 236 `#load` sites in 135 files), and `#r` and `#I` are still `imports` — they name an assembly and an include path. The defect this mutant injects is EXACTLY that: the `#load` row is published under the old label, so ONE CONSTRUCT CARRIES TWO LABELS, and a dependency graph that reads both sees a file coupling twice and cannot tell which of the two is the file coupling. THE MUTANT REVERTS THE LABEL AND NOT THE TARGET SPELLING, and the reason is stated rather than papered over: the pre-fix row's target was the RAW SPECIFIER (`Other.fsx`), a string the post-fix row does not contain (it carries the PROJECT-RELATIVE PATH the directive resolves to), so a transform over the result cannot recover it — the same reason the `repl-control-directive-imports-a-resource` mutant is an injection rather than a byte-faithful revert. What it asserts is the defect itself: does the suite go red when a `#load` also reads as an import? Caught by fsharp/part-of-load/host, whose forbid row for the `imports` shape exists for this and nothing else, and by fsharp/import-and-use, whose `part_of` row for `#load` cannot be satisfied by an `imports` row.

THE R3 REMEDY'S DIRECTION, REVERTED: the `part_of` contract says the DIRECTION IS THE DIRECTIVE'S OWN — the source is the file carrying the directive, the target is what it names, and every row carries `metadata.partRole` (src/ast/types.ts:170-190). F# has only ONE of DART's TWO FORMS: there is no `part of` in F#, so EVERY F# row is the host that INCLUDES the part and the role is `library`. A rule that could not tell the two ends apart would publish the included part as the source and the host as the target, and `partRole: "part"` on a host file is the same fact with the sign flipped. The mutant injects EXACTLY that: the role is flipped to `part`, which is the whole of the claim. Caught by fsharp/part-of-load/host, whose forbid row for `partRole: "part"` exists for this and nothing else.

PRE-FIX (2026-10-02 ontology round): the lane published an `exports: ExportInfo[]` array and NO `exports` relationship, so `bb_graph` could not answer what a package makes available. MEASURED as a real construct first — the Go spec's capitalized-identifier rule is a CONVENTION, so the ontology gate's grammar inventory is blind to it and probe B1 on the tree counts it instead. Caught by go/exports-spec, which expects five `exports` edges from the package symbol.

PRE-FIX: `collectGoPromotedMethods` computed that an outer method shadows a promoted one and DISCARDED the promoted method without recording the displacement, so no `overrides` edge existed although the analyzer held the evidence. Same defect shape as bash's omitted `overrides`. Caught by go/override-promotion, which expects `Wrapper.Report -> Shape.Report` and `Wrapper.Name -> Shape.Name`.

Method shadowing published on the `extends` label — the nearest neighbour, since the embedding itself is already an `extends` edge and a shadow is a relation between the two types. This is the label confusion the ontology asks about directly (Part 1 q4): the edge would read as inheritance while the fact is displacement. Caught by go/override-promotion, whose expectation names the `overrides` label and whose `extends` pin is scoped to `Wrapper -> Shape`.

The `overrides` endpoints published as the bare method leaf (`Report -> Report`) instead of the family's `Receiver.Method` qualified spelling. Go method names are not package-scope names — `Report` is declared on Shape, Wrapper and Counter in one file — so the unqualified form cannot name which declaration shadows which, and it collides with the `uses`/`contains` leaf surface. Caught by go/override-promotion, whose expectations name `Wrapper.Report` and `Shape.Report`.

The name-only shadow match replaced with a signature-compatible-only one — the shape the analyzer's own promotion dedupe uses for interface satisfaction. Both are defensible rules; only one is Go's selector rule. `Wrapper.Name()` hides a promoted `Shape.Name(string)` with a DIFFERENT signature, and Go selects Wrapper's for `w.Name()`, so a signature-only match under-reports the relationship by exactly the hiding cases. Caught by go/override-promotion, which pins `Wrapper.Name -> Shape.Name` and forbids the promoted-only `Wrapper.Area -> Shape.Area`.

The `exports` source set to the FILE path instead of the package symbol. An `imports` edge legitimately names a module path as its source, and the two sit in the same phase of `analyze()` — so the wrong source is one identifier away, and it makes every export edge unattributable to a module. Caught by go/exports-spec, whose expectations pin `source: "exports"` for all five edges.

THE MUTANT FOR A DEFECT THAT WAS LIVE, not a shape this lane once had. `exports` published for a type declared INSIDE a function body — `exports cobra -> UserCompletionTypeHelper` for `type UserCompletionTypeHelper func(...)` at cobra/completions_test.go:2946. It happened because the edge read the PHASE-5 `exports` ARRAY, whose predicate is `!ownerName`, and GO38 deliberately publishes a function-local type as a SYMBOL (a local var/const is not a symbol, but a local TYPE is, because the declared-type pass attributes that type's field types to it). The symbol carries no ownerName, so the array accepted it, and the edge published `exportForm: "capitalized_package_scope_name"` on a declaration that is not at package scope at all. Go does not export it: the name has no reach beyond the function that declares it. Caught by go/exports-spec, whose `scopeBoundary` body declares `type localUnit struct{ n int }` and whose expectations FORBID `exports -> localUnit` while still REQUIRING the `contains localUnit -> n` edge, so the mutant cannot be satisfied by deleting the symbol.

The exported-ness test made case-INSENSITIVE, so `helper` and `modeTable` publish `exports` edges. Go's rule is not 'is it a name' but 'does its FIRST CHARACTER begin an upper-case Unicode letter'; a predicate that stops discriminating cannot tell an exported identifier from an unexported one, and the edge then claims a package publishes something an importer cannot name. Caught by go/exports-spec, which forbids `exports -> helper` and `exports -> modeTable`.

ERROR RECOVERY: the walk STOPS at the first recovery node instead of bypassing it. `n.type === "ERROR" || n.isMissing` is the contract — report the region, skip it, keep publishing. Stopping instead means a document with one unreadable region publishes its module and the elements ABOVE the error and nothing below, and because the module still publishes the file still reads as analysed. A silent truncation is the defect class here, and it is invisible to every other gate in the lane because nothing counts symbols-per-file against a floor. Caught by html/error-recovery, whose fixture places the ERROR region in the MIDDLE of the document specifically so the half-after-the-error case is the one being tested.

PRE-FIX (M14 / R3, the call-shaped heritage): `class X extends Base.extend(M)` puts the BASE and the MIXIN at OPPOSITE depths — the base is the member call's RECEIVER and the mixin is its ARGUMENT — and the analyzer's lookup pair read only the heritage's DIRECT named children, so it found neither and published NO edge for the class at all. Measured over the whole admitted population: 76 call-shaped clauses (74 member-form, 2 identifier-form) of which the pre-remedy lookup found 0, and 802 of 2,572 heritage clauses (31.2 %) published no edge. The remedy reads the heritage's direct named child, and if it is a `call_expression` it takes the RECEIVER as the base and the ARGUMENTS as mixins (member form) or the CALLEE as the mixin and the first ARGUMENT as the base (plain form). The role assignment is the whole of the rule, and this mutant breaks it in the direction that is hardest to see: it publishes the BASE as a mixin as well, so `class X extends Base.extend(M)` yields `mixes_in X -> Base` beside `mixes_in X -> M` and `extends X -> Base`. Every such row is a false edge — it says the class composes its own supertype into itself — and it is invisible in a count, because the row COUNT is unchanged. Reverted here by DUPLICATING the base as a mixin row, which is the pre-remedy shape's closest reachable form: the transform layer receives the analyzer's RESULT and no parse tree, so the base is recovered from the `extends` row the remedy published and re-published under `mixes_in` with the same `isMixin` metadata. Caught by javascript/call-shaped-heritage-mixins, whose seven FORBID rows name exactly these false edges (`ApplicationRoute -> Route` is never a mixin, `ApplicationRoute -> WithBlockingActions` is never the base, `RedwoodRecord -> Core` is never a mixin, `RedwoodRecord -> ValidationMixin` is never the base) and whose twelve EXPECT rows keep the correct assignment passing — so a fix that published nothing at all would fail the expect rows rather than pass vacuously.

PRE-FIX (M14 / R3, the shape guard's other side): the remedy's discriminator is that the heritage's own expression is a CALL — a call in heritage position is a class-producing expression BY CONSTRUCTION, because the language requires the heritage to evaluate to a constructor or the class is a runtime error, while a call in ARGUMENT position is not. The rule therefore never fires on a plain heritage: `class Derived extends PlainBase {}` publishes `extends` and NOTHING else, and a rule that fired on it would publish `mixes_in Derived -> PlainBase` — a class that composes its own supertype into itself, on every class in the corpus. This mutant is the inverse of the previous one and is what proves the rule is SHAPE-gated rather than merely present: it publishes a `mixes_in` row for EVERY plain `extends` row, so the fixture's positive controls (`class PlainBase {} class PlainDerived extends PlainBase {}`) become fabrications while the correct rows are untouched. Caught by javascript/call-shaped-heritage-mixins, whose forbid row names `PlainDerived -> PlainBase` as a mixin, and whose expect rows keep the shape-(A) and shape-(B) rows passing.

M14 ontology regression: the duplicate check is scoped to the FILE instead of the OBJECT, so the same key in two different objects reads as a redefinition. A JSON key is unique only within its object, and this is the permissive direction: 120,174 occurrences across 7,679 files against 21 genuine duplicates, so the mutant is worth about 5,700 false edges. Caught by json/SameKeyDifferentObjects, whose forbids exist for exactly this mutant.

M14 ontology regression: the `overrides` edge is emitted but `overridesLine` is zeroed, and since both declarations share a name AND a qualified path the prior line is the only thing that distinguishes them — the edge then asserts a replacement without saying what was replaced. Caught by json/DuplicateKey's `meta.overridesLine` pin.

M14 ontology regression: `overrides` reverts to bare-name endpoints, violating the lane's own contract row that every relationship type emits QUALIFIED PATHS on both ends. Measured over the whole admitted population, 22 of 22 targets and 8 of 22 sources stop being paths, and 2 of 22 sources become name-ambiguous. The suite had three other `overrides` mutants and none tested endpoint FORM, so the change passed 16/16 and 24/24 with nothing objecting. Caught by json/DuplicateKey, whose `overrides` pins AND `forbidRelationships` were both migrated to the path form.

M14 ontology regression: every edge loses its site line, restoring the measured pre-M60 state in which `line_number` occurred ZERO times in the analyzer and every json edge in the index was stored with a NULL line while symbols carried `range` throughout.

M60 regression, MEASURED AND FIXED THIS LANE: the module-prefix strip is a fixed `slice(rootName.length + 1)`, which assumes the character at `rootName.length` is the dot separating a module from its first key. In a document whose TOP LEVEL is an array that character is `[`, so the `+1` ate it and `mod[0].tags[0]` published the name `0].tags[0]` — a `]` with no `[` before it, a spelling no keyed form (`Statement[0]`) and no element form (`rows[0][0]`) can produce. Over a 514-file stride sample of the 2,569 admitted corpus documents whose top level is an array: 17,803 such names in 215 of 514 files, 14.8% of the 120,464-symbol population; after the fix 0, with the 17,803 reappearing as the bracket form and the other three spelling buckets and the total symbol count unchanged to the digit. Measured to be SPELLING-ONLY and not a graph defect: edge count, both-ends resolution (120,464 of 120,464), containment soundness (120,464 of 120,464) and declared-owner agreement (85,670 of 85,670) are byte-identical on both sides of the fix, and the lane's own differential reports the same 363,344 contains edges covered with 0 unexplained either way — the oracle reads qualified PATHS, so it is structurally blind to a defect that lives only in the symbol NAME. That blindness is why this mutant exists. Caught by json/TopLevelArray.

JUL-14 REVERT: every `overrides` relationship is dropped, which is the pre-M60 state of this lane in its entirety. The analyzer's file header DECLINED the type on the grounds that julia has multiple dispatch rather than overriding, and nothing measured that claim: julia's method table holds one entry per (name, signature) pair, so a second declaration of the SAME pair REPLACES the first — julia prints `WARNING: Method definition f(Int) … overwritten at line 40` under `--warn-overwrite=yes`. Measured over the 971 admitted corpus files: 417 redefinition declarations across 109 files, of which 130 across 51 files are unconditional and therefore publishable. `script/m14/ontology-coverage-gate.ts`'s header records the bash instance of this same failure (BD8b). Caught by the two `overrides` rows in `method-redefinition-overrides` — a fixture authored from the measurement, not from the code.

JUL-15 REVERT: `isUnconditionalPosition`'s short-circuit test is disabled, so a redeclaration inside `if`/`else`, `try`/`catch`, a ternary, a `&&`/`||` right operand, or generated code publishes an `overrides` edge for a replacement that never happens. This is not hypothetical — it is what the lane shipped for one measurement round, because the operator of a `binary_expression` is a NAMED child in this grammar, so the operand list is [left, operator, right] and the first version compared index 1 against the declaration's node id and never matched. Measured over 971 admitted files: 11,549 `&&` binary_expressions, exactly 1 with a declaration node on the right (`julia/JuliaSyntax/src/core/parse_stream.jl:316`, `VERSION < v"1.11.0-DEV.753" && function ParseStream(io::IOBuffer; version=VERSION)`), plus 287 of the 417 corpus redefinition declarations sitting in a conditional or generated position — 287 edges that would be counted `unexplained` by the oracle and would make a real method's absence look like a caller. Written off the SOURCE TEXT because the pre-fix output cannot be reconstructed from the post-fix result: the result carries no record of which declaration was refused, which is the whole content of this mutation. Caught by the `guarded` and `toplevel_only` forbid rows in `method-redefinition-overrides`.

JUL-16 REVERT: the `overrides` pre-pass stops refusing LOCAL BINDINGS and stops carrying the enclosing scope in its key, so two closures in different function bodies collide into one "method". This is not a hypothetical: an earlier revision of this lane published 14 fabricated edges of exactly this shape before the fix. `julia/JuliaLowering/src/desugaring.jl` declares `wrap(asgn) = …` at line 153 inside `tuple_to_assignments` and again at line 324 inside a different function; `julia/base/range.jl` declares `throwbool(r) = …` at lines 488 and 496, inside two different inner constructors of `OneTo`. Inside a function body a short-form definition binds a LOCAL variable holding a closure — it adds no method and displaces nothing — so each of those 14 edges asserted a replacement between functions with no relationship. Two of them also named a `property` and a `constant` as the overridden method (`julia/test/core.jl:4441` -> `foo`, `:5489` -> `bar`), which is the tell: a field and a binding are not methods. Written off the SOURCE TEXT because the post-fix result cannot express this revert — it carries no record of the declarations the guard refused, which is the entire content of the mutation. Caught by the `wrap` forbid row in `method-redefinition-overrides`.

JUL-17 REVERT: the `overrides` signature key drops the `where` clause, so two methods of the same generic function whose ARGUMENT LISTS agree but whose type-variable BOUNDS differ collide. Julia keys the method table on the fully-specialised signature, so `f(x) where {T<:SignedInt}` and `f(x) where {T<:UnsignedInt}` are two live methods and neither replaces the other; publishing a replacement between them is the same falsehood the lane's own file header declined to tell about this type. Three corpus pairs were publishing exactly that edge: `julia/base/checked.jl:138-139` (`add_with_overflow`, `{T<:SignedInt}` vs `{T<:UnsignedInt}`), `julia/base/math.jl:834` and `:838` (`min`, `{T<:AbstractFloat}` vs `{T<:IEEEFloat}`), and `julia/test/testhelpers/Furlongs.jl:21-22` (`Furlong{p}`, `where {p,q}` vs `where {T,p,q}`). The cause is positional: the clause hangs off the assignment's LEFT-HAND SIDE, and the key was taken from the callable after `unwrapWhere` had descended past it. Written off the SOURCE TEXT, because the post-fix result records the clause and the revert is its removal — a transform that cannot see the source would have to re-derive the whole key. Caught by the `bounded` rows in `method-redefinition-overrides`: the `{T<:UnsignedInt}` declaration must produce no edge, and without the clause it does.

JUL-18 REVERT: the `overrides` pre-pass key drops the scope's DECLARATION LINE, so two modules that share a name are one scope and a declaration in the second reads as replacing one in the first. Julia treats them as two modules with two method tables. Corpus shape: `julia/test/deprecation_exec.jl` declares `module Src` at line 325 inside `DeprecatedReexportTest` and again at line 358 inside `DeprecatedShadowTest`, each holding a `newg() = 1` at lines 329 and 364. Keyed on the name alone the edge is a fabricated replacement between two unrelated bindings. This mutant exists because the FIX for it did not work at first and the fixtures could not see that: the scope NAME was threaded down the pre-pass while its line reset to 0 at every frame, so every key came out `name@0` and the change was indistinguishable from no change. A lane with one module in its fixture has no way to catch that; the census caught it by reading the source of every edge the lane published. Caught by the `same` forbid row in `method-redefinition-overrides`.

JUL-1 REVERT: a qualified callee collapses to its LAST SEGMENT, which is what the analyzer did before `fieldPath` kept the whole path. Measured over 400 corpus files: 1,352 bare segments appear behind a qualified path and 72 of them are reachable by MORE THAN ONE distinct path — `parse` alone is `Meta.parse`, `Base.parse`, `TOML.parse` and `Dates.parse`, and `bitcast` is `Base.bitcast`, `Core.bitcast` and `Intrinsics.bitcast`. Collapsing fuses unrelated functions into one node, and a fused node makes every edge into and out of it a statement about the wrong function. Caught by the `Base.show` symbol and by modules-and-scope.

JUL-2 REVERT: relationships sourced from the file scope are dropped, which is the pre-`GLOBAL_SCOPE` shape (`if (scope)` guarding every emit). Measured over 295 corpus files: 71.9% of Julia files have NO module block, and 46 of those emitted ZERO call edges while holding 8,478 `call_expression`s between them — a script calling a dozen functions indexed as a file containing nothing. Caught by the `global -calls-> println` assertion in modules-and-scope.

JUL-3 REVERT: `activeScope` is never restored on an exit frame, so it DRIFTS FORWARD and the last declaration to advance it owns every later sibling. Reverted here by re-attributing every relationship to the last symbol declared at or before its line — which is precisely the behaviour the missing restore produced. On the fixture it moves `describe`'s body onto `Area`, the previous function: `Area -calls-> string@17`, `Area -calls-> typeof@17`. Caught by dispatch-and-hierarchy's `Geom -contains-> describe` and by the `describe` symbol's ownership.

JUL-4 REVERT: a declaration's own left-hand side is walked as an invocation, so every short-form function calls itself — `f(x) = …` DEFINES f and Julia does not invoke it there. Measured across the 200-file corpus: 2,502 such false self-calls, the largest single source of wrong edges in the lane. Caught by the `calls` forbids on Area, scaled and perimeter in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

JUL-5 REVERT: `export X` fabricates a `function` symbol for X. An export MARKS a binding, it does not declare one, and Julia allows the export to precede the declaration. Dedup could not merge it because its key is `kind:owner:name` and the kinds differed, so a real `class:Circle` sat beside a second, wrongly-kinded `Circle`. Caught by the `Circle`/`Square` symbol kinds in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

JUL-6 REVERT: a type's OWN `type_head` is read as a reference, so every struct published a reference to itself — `Shapes -references-> Circle`, a declaration stating itself. The head names the type being declared. Caught by nothing in isolation (a self-reference is a weak signal), which is why this mutant is kept: it is the shape the ancestor-aware guard in `withinTypeHead` exists to prevent, and the guard's parent-only version passed the non-generic fixture case while missing `Circle{T} <: Shape`.

JUL-7 REVERT: the walk descends into a struct's type parameters, so `struct Circle{T<:Real} <: Shape` published `Circle <: Real`. `T<:Real` bounds a PARAMETER; it says nothing about Circle's supertype. A parameter list is a wall, not a road. Caught by the `Circle -extends-> Shape` and `Square -extends-> Shape` assertions — a fabricated `extends Real` leaves those intact, so the defect is visible as an EXTRA edge rather than a missing one.

JUL-8 REVERT: every `extends` edge is dropped, reproducing the state where `<:` was invisible because `binary_expression`'s operator is a NAMED child at index 1 — so `pos(node,1)` returned the operator instead of the right operand and an anonymous-child scan found nothing. Zero `extends` over a corpus with thousands, on files that parse with zero ERROR nodes. Caught by both `extends` assertions in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

JUL-19 REVERT: a `<:` CHAIN is read from `left.text`, so `LB <: A <: Mid` publishes ONE edge whose SOURCE is the fragment `LB <: A` and whose target is `Mid`, instead of the two adjacent links `LB -> A` and `A -> Mid`. A source fragment is not a symbol and resolves to nothing, and the upper link is absent entirely. MEASURED over the whole 1,985-file population by `direct-oracle-check.ts` before the fix: 25 of the 25 unexplained `extends` rows carried a fragment source (`LB <: X`, `X <: f()`, `S <: V`) or a doubled target (`UB.UB`), and the two sides agreed because the oracle read `left.text` too — a defect shared by both sides is invisible to a comparison, which is the whole reason this fixture pins BOTH implications: the two adjacent edges must exist AND a fragment source must not. Found generically off the source text because the post-fix result carries no record of the fragment it used to spell. Caught by `extends-shapes`: its two POSITIVE 2 assertions go missing and its `source: "LB <: A"` forbid row matches the fabricated edge.

JUL-9 REVERT: a type is published under its SUPERTYPE's name. `struct Circle{T<:Real} <: Shape` makes the head a `binary_expression` whose first identifier anywhere in the subtree is `Shape`, so one `class:Shape` carried `contains -> radius` and the real `Circle` was absent — name and supertype swapped by the same mistake. Caught by the `Circle` and `Square` class symbols in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

JUL-10 REVERT: a call reached through `ccall`/`@ccall` is marked as a Julia binding call. The call is real; the claim that its target is a JULIA FUNCTION is not — `strlen` and `jl_issorted` are C symbols that do not exist in Julia's namespace. Caught by all three `meta.isForeignCall` assertions in macros-and-foreign.

JUL-11 REVERT: a generic method's declaration is dropped. `function scaled{T<:Real}(s, k)` has callee children `parametrized_type_expression` + `argument_list`, which `calleeName` did not handle, so Julia's most characteristic construct — a parametric method — was invisible to the lane whose job is to notice that. Caught by the `scaled` symbol in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

JUL-12 REVERT: a function carrying a RETURN-TYPE annotation publishes under the return type. `function scaled{T<:Real}(s::Shape, k::T)::Float64` makes the signature a `typed_expression` whose siblings are the callable and the return type, so an identifier scan found `Float64` first and `scaled` was lost. Third instance of the same class in this lane: scan for a name before unwrapping the wrapper around it. Caught by the `scaled` symbol and `Geom -contains-> scaled`.

JUL-13 REVERT: `f(x)::T = …` is not recognised as a declaration. A return-type annotation puts a `typed_expression` on the assignment's left, so the short-form handler's `call_expression` test failed. `x::Int = 5` is also a `typed_expression`, so the wrapper is unwrapped only when it wraps a CALL. Caught by the `perimeter` symbol in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

REVERT: `declaredTypes` is filled DURING the walk, so a call to a type declared LATER in the file is a plain `calls` instead of `instantiates`. The pre-fix code consulted the set mid-walk; the comment on the variable already claimed the opposite ('consulted afterwards, so a type declared later in the file still counts'), which is why it survived review — the code said one thing and the comment the other, and the comment was believed. Found by the F5 `instantiates` oracle: `Compiler/test/EAUtils.jl` calls `GetEscapeCache()` on line 52 and declares it on line 90. Reverted generically by demoting every `instantiates` edge whose line precedes the type's own declaration.

REVERT: a `where` clause's upper bound is a subtype edge from the type PARAMETER, and the emit was guarded by `scope` even though `scope` is not that edge's source. Copy-pasted from the `contains` cases, where the scope IS the source and the guard is the point — so it suppressed a valid edge wherever the bound appeared at FILE SCOPE, which is 71.9% of Julia files. Found by the F5 `extends` oracle: `base/rational.jl` publishes `T extends AbstractFloat` and `base/hashing.jl` `UTF8Units extends AbstractString`, neither of which the analyzer had. Reverted by dropping the `isWhereBound` edges, which is the pre-fix observable.

REVERT: the `where`-bound scan looks only at the where_expression's DIRECT children, so the braced spelling `where {T<:Real}` is missed while the bare `where T<:Real` is found. Julia people write the braced form, so the common shape produced no `T extends Real` at all. Found because this mutant SURVIVED its first form: a fixture whose `where` bound was invisible to the analyzer could not catch the defect that hid it, and a fixture and an analyzer agreeing on nothing is not a test. Caught by the `T extends Real` assertion in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

REVERT: an `imports` edge's source is the declaration doing the importing, not the file root. This mutant rewrites every `imports` source to `root` and is the REVERT of the exact distinction this lane's own `imports` RULED on: the ruling's overturn condition was 'a julia `imports` relationship row that is not an import-site artifact — a row whose source is the importing declaration rather than the literal `root`'. Emitting `imports` at all was therefore read as refuting the ruling, and the fix that satisfied the condition was mistaken for a violation of it. Measured over the 971 admitted corpus files, 446 of 1,502 `imports` edges carry a real module symbol as their source and 595 carry the file scope; collapsing the two asserts that `module M` depends on packages it never named. Caught by the four `imports` assertions and two `forbidRelationships` in `imports-and-exports`.

REVERT: every `imports` relationship is dropped while the `ImportInfo[]` channel keeps filling, which is the pre-M60 state of this lane. The lane recorded the construct on the payload and declined to publish it as an edge, then RULED it non-applicable on the grounds that `RelationshipType.Imports` serializes to `brain_import` and the repo treats `ImportInfo[]` as the import surface — a convention read as a constraint, since `real-python-analyzer.ts:979`, `real-lua-analyzer.ts:569`, `real-yaml-analyzer.ts:1017`, `real-nim-analyzer.ts:1064` and `real-typescript-analyzer.ts:5509` all emit the relationship through the same string. The construct is not rare in julia: 1,675 `import_statement`/`using_statement` nodes across 504 of the 971 admitted files. Caught by the `imports` assertions in `imports-and-exports`.

REVERT: every `exports` relationship is dropped while the `ExportInfo[]` channel keeps filling. The ruling this reverts demanded 'an `exports` relationship count above the `ExportInfo` count for the same corpus' — a threshold that emitting one row per `ExportInfo` entry cannot exceed, so the only way to satisfy it was an edge that was WRONG. `real-python-analyzer.ts:1166` emits both channels from one `__all__` walk. Measured: 308 `export_statement`/`public_statement` nodes across 152 of the 971 admitted files, publishing 1,770 export names. Caught by the `exports` assertions in `imports-and-exports`.

REVERT: an `exports` edge's source is the module doing the exporting. This mutant rewrites every `exports` source to `root`, which is the collapse the `imports` source mutant performs in the other direction: it makes a module's published surface indistinguishable from a file's, so `bb_impact` on a module reports every re-export of every module in the corpus as its own dependents. Measured: 962 of 1,770 `exports` edges carry a real module symbol as their source and 783 carry the file scope, because 71.9% of julia corpus files open no module at all and julia's `public`/`export` are legal at file scope in `Main`. Caught by the `exports` assertions and the two `exports` `forbidRelationships` in `imports-and-exports`.

JUL-16 REVERT: `using A, B` publishes ONE `imports` edge and calls the second module an item of the first. `importTargets()` walked the statement's named children IN ORDER carrying a `pending` variable, and one branch read "a bare identifier when something is already pending, with no items yet, and a different name — that is an ITEM of the pending target"; that branch cannot tell a second MODULE from an item of the first. This mutant reinstates the collapse by keeping only the FIRST `imports` edge per (source, statement line) pair, which is what the state machine produced for a multi-module statement.

MEASURED, not asserted: `script/m14/oracles/julia-imports.ts` — an independent derivation sharing no rule, key set or resolver with the analyzer — found 167 of 440 derived import edges MISSING on a 200-file draw, 38% of the type, and the two- and three-path statement shapes are the second and third most common in the corpus (`validation/m14/fixtures/julia/import-export-shapes.ts`: 32 two-path and 12 three-path statements in a 400-file draw). `DataFrames.jl/src/DataFrames.jl:3-19` is ONE `using` naming 17 modules, of which the analyzer published 1.

Caught by the `Compat` and `Logging` `imports` assertions in `imports-and-exports`.

JUL-17 REVERT: `import A as B` publishes nothing. The `import_alias` branch was gated on a `pending` that a statement whose ONLY named child is an `import_alias` never had, so the whole statement was silently dropped — on `StaticArrays.jl/ext/StaticArraysChainRulesCoreExt.jl`, which writes `import ChainRulesCore as CRC`.

This mutant drops every `imports` edge whose metadata records the aliased form, which is the shape the gate produced. It is a separate defect from the multi-module collapse because the fix for one does not fix the other: a stateless per-child walk that classifies `import_alias` recovers both, and a fixture that pinned only the first would leave the second able to regress silently.

Caught by the `ChainRulesCore` `imports` assertion in `imports-and-exports`.

JUL-18 REVERT: a `public_statement` whose FIRST NAMED child is an `ERROR` still publishes its `exports` edges. `public` and `export` are CONTEXTUAL KEYWORDS in julia — keywords only when a name list follows — so `public = expr` declares a local variable, and the production grammar emits a `public_statement` for it anyway.

MEASURED: 49 of the corpus's 3,570 import/export statements carry an ERROR descendant, and in exactly 2 the STATEMENT NODE is wrong rather than one part of it. Both published fabricated edges: `Documenter.jl/src/expander_pipeline.jl:632` published `exports` rows for the local `fields`, the local `private` and a bare `:`, and `julia/stdlib/REPL/src/docview.jl:408` published one for `binding`, a FUNCTION PARAMETER of `summarize`. A fabricated export is a fake dependency: it is counted `unexplained` by every oracle and becomes wrong refactoring advice in `bb_impact`.

The refusal is "first named child is an ERROR" and NOT "contains an ERROR", because the other 47 are legitimate julia the grammar cannot fully parse (`import .Base.Math.@horner`, in julia's own stdlib) and refusing those would trade 45 real edges for 2 fabricated ones.

WHY IT READS `source` AND NOT THE RESULT. The refusal's whole effect is that the result carries NO trace of the misparsed statement, so a result-only revert would have to hardcode the names it publishes — and a hardcoded name stops matching the moment a fixture is renamed, which is the failure `Mutant.transform`'s `source` parameter exists to prevent. This one re-derives them from the file's own text with a character test, which is what the pre-fix walk effectively did when it returned one string per named child of the misparsed node.

Caught by the `fields` and `select_probe` `exports` `forbidRelationships` in `imports-and-exports` — both names ARE declared in that fixture, so the edges RESOLVE and are merely FALSE, which is the shape no resolution check can catch.

JUL-20 REVERT: a CALL-OVERLOAD definition is named after its own BINDING. `(m::Model)(x) = …` adds a method to Model's call table and declares no binding `m`; the analyzer already refused the plain form, but `unwrapWhere` walks THROUGH `typed_expression`, so `(t::Type{Model} where X)(x) = …` unwrapped past the pattern to the binding and published `function t`, `contains M -> t` and a `decorates t -> inline` row. 423 call-overload sites exist corpus-wide. Caught by the `m`/`t` forbid rows and the `Model.m` / `CallableShapes.t` forbid edges in `callable-shapes`.

JUL-21 REVERT: a SPLICED member is read through to its receiver. `(Base.$fJ)(x::Rational{BigInt}, …)` in `julia/base/gmp.jl` names its overloaded function through a loop variable, and the paren guard saw a `field_expression` rather than an interpolation, so `fieldPath` published the RECEIVER: `contains MPQ -> Base`, a module named as a member of another module. Caught by the `Base`/`fJ` forbid rows (`forbidSymbols` and `forbidRelationships`) in `callable-shapes`.

JUL-22 REVERT: a PARAMETRIC ALIAS declares nothing. `Dims{N} = NTuple{N,Int}` puts a `parametrized_type_expression` on the assignment's left, which is neither a call (a short-form method) nor a plain binding, so the assignment case skipped it — 43 sites corpus-wide (`Base.Dims`, `Base.AbstractVecOrTuple`, `Flux._ParallelONE`, `StaticArrays.SizedMatrix`) published no symbol and no `contains` row while the truth oracle derived all 43. Caught by the `Dims` expectSymbol and the `CallableShapes.Dims` expectRelationship in `callable-shapes`.

An export edge is filed as `references` — its neighbouring type in the ontology, and the one the import edges already use, so the mistake is a plausible copy-paste rather than a slip. `references` asserts that a declaration NAMES a type; `exports` asserts that a file PUBLISHES a name, and a consumer answering "what does this file offer" reads only the latter. Caught by kotlin/exports-visibility, which pins seven `exports` edges from `(file)`.

The export edge keeps its type and endpoints but loses the payload that says WHICH fact published the name (`via`: an explicit `public` versus kotlin's public-by-default), the resolved `visibility`, the `symbolKind`, and the `fileLevel` flag that tells the store the source is the file. Without `fileLevel` the store does not rewrite `source_external` to the project-relative path, so every kotlin export row lands naming `(file)` instead of a path — the edge exists and identifies no file. Caught by kotlin/exports-visibility, which pins `meta.via` and `meta.fileLevel` on individual edges rather than only counting them.

Membership widens to every owner-bearing symbol — the pre-KAD-MR3-K1 `ownerKind === Class` hole that exported every member of every class. Membership of a member rides `contains` (the store resolves `contains` structurally, by the edge's own line, and `exports` by name), so exporting members both double-counts them and inflates every export row with names no consumer can import directly. Caught by kotlin/exports-visibility's forbid rows on `member`, `visible` and `hidden`.

The edge's source becomes the FILE'S PACKAGE instead of `(file)`, which reads as a better identity. It cannot survive the store: parallel-indexer.ts:3453 drops an `exports` edge whose source is a lowercase dotted name, exactly as `org.jetbrains.kotlin.config` is, so every kotlin export row would be deleted at insert time and the type would report as emitted at zero rows stored. This is the defect class the analyzer cannot detect by looking at its own output, which is why it needs a pin rather than a probe. Caught by kotlin/exports-visibility's `from: (file)` pins and its forbid row on the package name.
