The wrapper is a grouping paren and must stay transparent for FINDING arguments. Reproduces the 2.0.0-side loss. Caught by perl/import-argument-items.

PERL-MR4: CODE IS NOT NAMES, for a call's arguments. `use feature (sprintf(":%vd", $^V))` recorded [":%vd"] -- sprintf's FORMAT STRING, whose `%v` is a version conversion, while the bundle name itself is decided at runtime. This was the last disagreement between the two grammars in the whole 5,774-file corpus, and it was introduced by this milestone's own reachability fix: making the wrapper transparent is what let the walk reach into the sprintf at all. Caught by perl/import-argument-items.

PERL-MR15: a base that IS in the companion and does not declare the method must WITHDRAW the guess. Measured over 5,774 corpus files, 6,111 of 8,085 overrides edges are exactly this case -- the base is in the project and says otherwise -- so keeping them is 75.6% of the label being false. This is what no gate could see: the differential asks whether every edge is EXPLAINABLE from the tree, not whether it is TRUE, and a first-parent guess is perfectly explainable. The mutation RE-ADDS an edge for every method symbol that has none, which is the shape a broken withdrawal guard produces; the forbid row is target-agnostic so it catches the edge whatever target the guard invents. Caught by perl/override-companion-resolve, whose `Remote::Silent` sibling exists only so that 'present but declares nothing' is decidable.

PERL-MR15: a base OUTSIDE the project cannot be settled by any index, and absence of knowledge is not knowledge of absence. Promoting that guess above the 0.7 patterns threshold publishes 347 corpus edges -- 4.3% -- as confident when the source proves nothing. This is PERL-MR14's original defect (conflating 'no companion opinion' with 'the base does not declare it') reappearing on the other side of the fix. Caught by perl/override-companion-resolve's `MR15::Unknown` forbid row.

M14.6 regression: a companion index that has never heard of a base SILENTLY DELETES that class's override edges instead of leaving them as guesses. The guard read `else if (!context?.overrideCompanion)` -- whether a companion OBJECT was supplied, not whether it had an opinion about THIS base -- so passing any companion at all silenced the first-parent guess for every uncovered base. Measured on a 120-file draw per corpus: 2,235 guessed edges, and 1,928 of them disappeared while every gate stayed green. A companion is a PARTIAL view by construction (a sample, a subset, an incremental index, one worker's share), and 'I have never heard of this base' is not 'this base does not declare the method'. Caught by perl/override-companion, whose two `overrides` rows are the per-file default this mutant removes. The python lane already reads it correctly (`else if (!overrideCompanion?.has(base))`).

M14.6 regression: a callee that is written as CODE is published as a NAME again. `$self->${\( EXPR \)}` is perl's 'call the method this expression computes' -- the grammar puts the whole expression in the `method` field, so the lane published arbitrary source text as a method name: measured `calls -> DemolishAll->new` (Moo/Object.pm:56, a `function` field holding compound text) and `calls -> ${\( $tc->can('coercion')||sub { ... } )}` (Moo/Role.pm:224). A target that is not written in the file cannot be verified by the line oracle, so it is a fabricated target rather than a weaker claim. 19 such edges removed from a 14-file draw. Caught by the fixture's relationship pins, and by the oracle's Tier A, which asks the SOURCE for the name.

drops every `exports` edge — the php/define-exports pin. The defect class is the one the whole workstream exists to catch: a type that is EMITTED by the source and fires on 49 of 4,642 corpus files can still be lost in one filter, and the loss is invisible to every other type's gate because the other nine are untouched.

publishes a `define()` that sits INSIDE a function body as a file export (`global -> LAZY_ONLY`) — the scope defect. The corpus has 11 such calls, so this mutant fabricates 11 edges asserting the file publishes a name whose publication depends on a function running. Caught by php/define-exports' forbidRelationships: a function-body `define()` is not a file publication.

also files a `define()`d name under `contains` (`global -> CLOOGLE_DB_HOST`) — the labelling defect. A `define()`d name resolves against the GLOBAL scope and no node in the file contains it, so a `contains` edge says the file owns a global. It is the specific confusion this contract has to hold: `DECLARED_CONST` (a namespace-scoped `const`) IS carried by `contains`, and the two look alike.

reverts the callee-resolution fix: drops every `exports` edge whose callee was the FULLY QUALIFIED `\define`, which is exactly what the bare-name-only rule did before 2026-10-08. Written GENERICALLY off the edge's own `metadata.calleeShape` rather than a hardcoded target name, for the reason recorded above the owner mutants — a name-hardcoded filter silently stops matching and then reports a survive as a pass. Caught by php/define-exports' `expectRelationships` on `AUTO_PREPEND_STYLE`; the population it costs is 1 edge, and it is a publication PHP guarantees unconditionally (`\define` is fully qualified, so there is no namespace lookup and no fallback for the rule to be wrong about), in phpunit's `tests/end-to-end/generic/_files/auto_prepend_file.php` — a file whose whole purpose is that the constant is globally visible.

strips `metadata.owner` from every edge — the state of this lane before the change, reproduced faithfully rather than described. The receiver node was on hand at all six member-position emission sites and discarded, so `$this->render()`, `self::render()`, `parent::render()` and `Widget::render()` all published the bare target `render` and were mutually indistinguishable; `render` is a method on many classes, so the reverse walk picked one declaration by a rule nobody chose. Caught by php/receiver-owner's `meta.owner` rows.

fills in the ABSENT owner with the enclosing scope — the tempting wrong answer, and the only direction in this set that is silently harmful. A member-position edge's source is the enclosing METHOD (an edge reads `calls -> build`, `uses -> __construct`), so the result's own symbol table maps it to the class it is written in, and that class is exactly what gets attached to receivers that state no owner: `$obj->m()` (a local variable whose class is whatever was assigned), `$this->svc->m()` (a chain whose type is the PROPERTY's), and `parent::m()` in a class with no declared base. Every fabricated owner names a real class that really has a method with that name, so the edge RESOLVES and the graph looks healthy — which is why a wrong owner is worse than a missing one. Caught by php/receiver-owner's three `meta.owner: null` rows.

publishes the owner as the FULLY-QUALIFIED path (`\Fixture\ReceiverOwner\Qualified`) rather than the leaf name every other row in this lane publishes. Targets are bare names everywhere else — `leafName` in processObjectCreation, the `name` field of the scoped/member calls — so the qualified form would not join against the `ownerName` on the symbol side and would change what every downstream consumer sees. On graphql a qualified publish measured -75% unresolved, so it is not a strawman; it is the alternative this rule had to reject on evidence. Caught by php/receiver-owner, whose `onlyViaAbsolutePath` row has no unqualified twin to satisfy it (a fixture row matches with some(), so the qualified form alone is what pins the reduction).

re-instates the name-only symbol drop (`self`/`parent` refused without reference to kind or owner) at the result level, exactly as `keepSymbol` did before the fix. Relationships are left untouched, which is the defect's whole danger: the analyzer keeps emitting `contains Holder -> parent` while the member it names is gone, so the lane's only orphan endpoint is a store-vs-analyzer divergence rather than a missing edge — a shape no per-edge gate on any other type can see. Caught by php/keyword-member-names, whose five expectSymbols rows are the property, constant and method forms of both names.

the over-broad fix: a `parent`/`self` declaration with no owner (the class, interface, trait, enum, namespace or top-level function the language really does reserve) is published. It is the direction that looks like an improvement — the projection stops deleting anything — and it is wrong for a reason the symbol table would hide: a bare `parent` joins every `parent::` and `$this->parent` edge at once, so a keyword illegally in a type position becomes a resolution candidate for a member. Caught by php/keyword-member-names' two forbidSymbols rows, which name a `parent`/`self` symbol whose ownerName is absent.

the PRE-FIX state, reproduced faithfully: every declaration the recovery-escape published is removed again, and so are the `contains` edges that only exist because it published them. That is what the analyzer did on `FSharp.Formatting/.../php/markdown.php` — 20 real class members (doLists, processListItems, makeCodeSpan, prepareItalicsAndBold, formParagraphs, encodeAttribute, encodeAmpsAndAngles, encodeEmailAddress, handleSpanToken, …) were invisible because recovery nested them inside the method before them, while the corpus kept emitting 19 `calls` edges naming them. Caught by php/recovery-swallowed-members, whose four member rows sit BELOW the damaged statement on purpose: a fix that recovered the first declaration and stopped would pass every row above and fail `callsSwallowed`.

the reading the fixture REJECTS: a recovered declaration is published as a GLOBAL FUNCTION (kind `function`, no owner) and its containment edge is dropped, because a function owned by a class is not a shape this lane publishes. It is tempting for a reason worth stating — a `function` inside a body really does become a global in PHP when the enclosing code runs, and `collectPhpFileScope` already registers nested named functions as file-scope function values — but publication must describe the SOURCE, and the source writes these functions in the class body between members. Caught by php/recovery-swallowed-members' three `forbidSymbols` rows (`ownerName: null`, the top-level absent-or-null convention) and, independently, by its `expectSymbols` `kind: method` rows — two channels, because a mutant that cleared the owner but kept the kind would otherwise survive.

HALF THE FIX, the failure the paired skip exists to prevent: the recovered declarations are published, and the damaged method's body walk still reaches their subtrees, so every call and read inside them is emitted TWICE — once under the member that contains it and once under the method recovery nested it in. Reproduced from the result's own line ranges: for each recovered declaration, every call/read whose line falls inside it is re-emitted under the smallest enclosing callable, which on this fixture is `damaged`. This is the mutant that says the two halves are one change: `php/drop-recovered-members` would still be caught if the skip alone were removed, and `php/publish-recovered-members-as-global-functions` would be caught if only the kind were wrong — NEITHER notices a duplicated edge, because a fixture's `expectRelationships` matches at least one. Caught by php/recovery-swallowed-members' `expectRelationshipCount`: `calls swallowedB -> swallowedA` must be EXACTLY one and `calls damaged -> swallowedB` exactly ZERO.

THE PRE-FIX STATE, faithfully: every nested named function disappears from the store and so do the `contains` edges that give it an owner. Not a hypothetical — it is what all 5,094 admitted files produced before this round, where the only trace of the declaration was an edge SOURCED AT its name (Slim's two `references testProcessRequest -> ...`) or calling it (`calls useHelper -> nestedHelper`). Written off `metadata.nestedIn`, the marker the pass itself sets, so the revert stays faithful to whatever the fixture looks like. Caught by php/nested-named-functions' `expectSymbols`, `expectSymbolCount` and the two `contains` rows.

THE REJECTED READING the source vetoes: a nested function published as a METHOD of the class whose method declared it. Reproduced generically off the result — the enclosing class is found by looking up the callable the symbol names in `metadata.nestedIn` in the symbol table and taking ITS owner, which is exactly how a reader would resolve it, so no class name is hardcoded. The symbol becomes a member that the source does not declare, and the store gains a `contains NestedHost -> nestedHelper` edge a consumer would use to resolve an inherited call. Caught by php/nested-named-functions' `forbidSymbols` row (ownerName NestedHost) and by its `expectSymbols` row (ownerName must be the namespace).

THE SECOND REJECTED READING: the nested function is published, its `contains` edge is kept, but it carries NO owner. In a namespaced file every top-level function is owned by its namespace, so this makes two function symbols in ONE file follow two ownership rules — and PHP's global-table name for the declaration is `Fixture\NestedFunctions\innerValue`, not `innerValue`, so an ownerless symbol is a name no caller can spell. It is also the state a reader would land on by treating "nested" as "file-level but unattached". Caught by the fixture's `forbidSymbols` row with `ownerName: null` and by its `expectSymbols` ownerName.

THE DAMAGE GUARD REMOVED. The pass skips a declaration whose body parent `hasError`, because those 22 markdown.php declarations are class members the parser could not close the body over — MEMBERS, published as members by the recovery escape. Remove the guard and they are published a SECOND time as namespace-owned globals, which is the reading that would make one declaration both a member and a global. Reproduced off the escape's own marker: every symbol with `metadata.recoveredFromBody` gains a namespace-owned twin in the same file, plus the containment edge that follows. This is a FABRICATION, not a gap, and it was published at 0.95 with `evidenceClass: structural` — indistinguishable from a real override to every downstream consumer, which is the worst way to be wrong. It was PRE-EXISTING: the same-file prescan collected every `method` symbol regardless of modifiers, so `class A { private function p(){} } class B extends A { private function p(){} }` published `B.p -> A.p` long before this round. SAME-FILE ONLY, and that is the rule's actual scope rather than a limit of the mutant. PS23 REVERT: the docstring walk skips blank lines while searching upward, so a FILE BANNER becomes the documentation of whichever declaration comes first. PS2/PS15 REVERT: a repeated declaration earns a SECOND containment edge while the symbol dedupes to one, so a `contains` edge names a target the file does not declare. PS19 REVERT: an invocation-operator command's target is the RAW text, so `& $sb` publishes `calls -> $sb` — a name no symbol can have, because a variable is stored stripped. PS-A2 REVERT: a class's interface list publishes no `implements` edge. The class header cannot say which base is a class and which are interfaces — PowerShell resolves that at runtime — so the grammar's positional shape is the only information there is. Caught by class-inherit-psa2's `implements Circle -> IShape` row and by its `implements == 1` count, which is the half that survives a fix that keeps the row but also emits the base class as an interface.

Caught by class-inherit-psa2's two `calls -> interface` / `calls -> IShape` forbid rows and its `interface` forbidSymbol row.

This is the defect the FIX introduced, recorded as a mutant rather than quietly corrected, because it is the reason the fixture puts a class after an interface and pins three `contains IShape -> <class>` forbid rows: scoping without an exit is not a narrower fix, it is a different defect, and it was invisible until a file exercised the order. The first version of the fix leaked exactly this way and the measured damage was `contains IShape -> Shape`, `-> Circle` and `-> Square`. Caught by class-inherit-psa2's three forbid rows.

PS-A3 REVERT, the mistake this work made: `isComObject` is derived from the CONSTRUCTED NAME containing a dot rather than from the FLAG that was used. A dotted .NET type name and a COM ProgID look alike and mean different things, so `-TypeName System.Text.StringBuilder` — a managed type — is published as a COM object. This is recorded as a mutant rather than quietly corrected because it is the more interesting half of the finding: the fix that closed a real gap introduced a different one, and the two metadata rows in new-object-psa3 are the only thing that distinguishes them. Caught by that fixture's `Shell.Application` row expecting `isComObject: true` AND its `System.Text.StringBuilder` row expecting the flag to be ABSENT.

PS-A4 REVERT: a variable passed as a command ARGUMENT is not read. The largest of the five defects the F9 completeness audit found, and the most consequential: `Write-Host $a` published the call edge and no `uses` at all, so every variable handed to a cmdlet was invisible in the graph while the same variable interpolated in a string was read. Measured rather than estimated — reading command arguments took the corpora from 114,096 to 129,259 relationships across 760 files, and a line-level check over all 25,023 variable-reference edges then read 100.00% justified.

Scoped to the `isArgumentReference` marker rather than deleting every variable read, because an argument read and an interpolation read are the same row shape (`uses` + `isVariableReference`); without the marker a mutant for this defect would silently revert three others. That is the same standard the PS9 entry in this file already states — a mutant that cannot be attributed faithfully is not written. Caught by variable-reads-psa4's argument rows and its `uses == 9` count.

PS-A4 REVERT: a BRACED variable keeps its braces, so `${a}` and `$a` become two different symbols. Measured on a probe: `$a = 1` declared `a`, and a string containing `${a}` published `uses -> {a}` — a read naming a symbol nothing declares, so the reference was lost rather than merely misspelled. The braced spelling is how PowerShell writes a variable whose name would otherwise run into adjacent text, so it is not rare. Caught by variable-reads-psa4's `braced` rows and its `{braced}` forbidSymbol, which pins the DECLARATION side too because the name reaches the graph two ways.

PS-A4 REVERT: an EXPANDABLE HERE-STRING is not interpolated. A here-string published no read at all while the identical text in a double-quoted string did, because `expandable_here_string_literal` is a different node type from `expandable_string_literal` and only the latter was in the switch. The second half of the defect was a LINE off-by-one with the line break and the sigil inside the target: the grammar gives the interpolation a span starting at the end of the previous line (`variable [6,8]-[7,8]` for a `$message` written on line 7), so the edge was published one line high. Caught by variable-reads-psa4's two here-string rows, whose line numbers ARE the assertion.

PS-A4 REVERT: a SPLAT keeps its `@`, so `@name` and `$name` become two different symbols. The grammar models `@name` as a `variable` node whose text carries NO sigil, so the dollar-strip did nothing to it and `New-PSOptions @OptionsArguments` published `uses -> @OptionsArguments`. Found by the line-level check, where the splat rows were the one real defect hiding among its false negatives. Caught by variable-reads-psa4's splat row and its `@splatArgs` forbidSymbol.

PS-A4 REVERT: a DYNAMIC method target is published as a call to a sigil-bearing name. `$type::$method()` wrote `calls -> $method`, which is wrong twice: a variable is stored stripped, so `$method` is a name no symbol can have, and the source says the method is CHOSEN AT RUNTIME, so calling a method named `$method` asserts a fact the code does not contain. The correct edge is a `uses` of the variable holding the name. Found on ConstrainedLanguageRestriction.Tests.ps1:513 — the last row of the line-level check's residue, at which point it read 100.00%. Caught by variable-reads-psa4's `isDynamicMethodTarget` row and its `calls -> $method` forbid row.

PS-A4 REVERT: an INCREMENT or DECREMENT publishes no read of its operand. All four types were in the F9 audit's "the analyzer never names it" set, and probing them confirmed every one emitted nothing, so `$count++` left the graph with a declaration and no read. Keyed on `isCounterUpdate` so the revert is attributable to this defect alone; the increment and the compound-assignment reads are separate rows with separate markers and separate mutants. Caught by variable-reads-psa4's four counter rows.

PS-A4 REVERT: a COMPOUND assignment publishes no read of its left side. `$total += 1` is a read of `$total` and a write to it; the write is the declaration, and the read was nowhere, so a variable the graph could see being created had a use it could not. The operator is the whole distinction — a plain `=` gains no read edge, which is what the count row pins. Caught by variable-reads-psa4's two compound rows and their `assignmentOperator` metadata.

PS-A4 REVERT, the half-defect: a PREFIX counter update is missed because the operand is found by a direct-child lookup. `$count++` puts its variable directly under the increment node, but `++$count` nests it as `pre_increment_expression > unary_expression > variable`, so a direct lookup finds the postfix pair and silently misses the prefix pair. That is the same shape of miss as `sub_expression` (PS16) and `left_assignment_expression` (PS2), and it is invisible in a count — two of four sites missing reads as an error count looks like a partial success. Caught by variable-reads-psa4's two `isPostfix: false` rows, which fail on their own if the prefix forms are the ones dropped.

PS-A4 REVERT, the RULING half: a scope-qualified READ is suppressed again, because the read path reuses PS8's DECLARATION guard. Measured on the F5 non-test sample: 7 rows from Sign-Package.ps1 expecting `uses -> env:Temp` and `uses -> {env:ProgramFiles(x86)}`, with the analyzer publishing nothing for either.

This reverses part of an existing ruling, which is why it is pinned as a decision and not as a defect fix. PS8's own text is about declarations — "a scope-qualified name (`$global:x`) is never a local declaration" — and that still stands: `$env:FOO = 'x'` declares no symbol, which the fixture pins as a forbidSymbol. What changed is only that a READ is a dependency on something outside the file, of the same kind as a `calls -> Write-Host` target, which is equally unresolvable. The scope prefix is KEPT on the target so it can never collide with a project variable.

Needs owner confirmation: it is a change to a standing lane ruling, taken on the evidence of an independent oracle plus the reasoning, and recorded as a decision for that reason.

PS-A4 REVERT: every relationship's EVIDENCE TIER is dropped, and `overrides` is relabelled `structural`. The tier is how the edge was derived, which is analyzer knowledge, and the one relationship in this lane that is genuinely INFERRED is `overrides` — PowerShell has no `override` keyword, so it is a name match between a subclass member and the base's declared member set. Calling it `structural` overstates the evidence, which is the whole reason a tier exists.

Emitted centrally in `addRel` rather than per call site, so no call site can forget it, with the caller's metadata spread LAST so a call site may still override. The SPEC gate's section D requires two DISTINCT tiers pinned, so collapsing them all to one is caught there as well as here.

PS23 REVERT: no `imports` edge is published, and the module dependency is carried by `references` alone. This is the pre-fix shape verbatim — `addImport` filled `imports[]` for all four PowerShell import forms (`Import-Module`, `using module`, `using namespace`, `#requires -Module`) and published one `references` row, so the ontology's `imports` type was EMITTED 0 TIMES across the whole corpus. `script/m60/powershell-surface-measure.ts:223` derives its `absent` list as `ONTOLOGY.filter(k => !kinds[k])` and `:243` prints it as the types 'all implemented + gated'; a type with zero edges corpus-wide is in that list for every draw, so the parenthetical asserted `imports` was implemented while `grep -c 'RelationshipType.Imports' src/ast/real-powershell-analyzer.ts` returned 0. Keyed on the TYPE rather than on a module name or a fixture, so it reverts the whole kind wherever it is emitted. Caught by imports-psb12's eleven `imports` rows and its `imports == 6` count; the count matters because a `forbid` alone would not notice a type that vanished, and the eleven rows matter because a count alone would not name the target.

PS23 REVERT, the half that is easy to ship by accident: the `imports` edge keeps its type and every row count stays right, but its evidence TIER becomes `usage_contextual`. The edge now claims it was derived from a node's POSITION, which is the opposite of where an import comes from. `usage_contextual` is defined in this lane as 'settled by what the construct means', a true statement about `New-Object -ComObject Shell.Application` and a false one about `#requires -Module Pester`. Honesty contract §4 makes the tier a countable fact rather than a label, so a wrong tier on a whole type is a defect even when the edge itself is real.

IT IS AIMED AT `evidenceClassFor`'s `if (isImport) return "import_based"` LINE, and the journey to that target is the record. The first two attempts aimed at a `case ASTEngine.RelationshipType.Imports:` added to the switch beside the `References` case, and BOTH SURVIVED — once while the two shared a fallthrough return, and once after they were split into separate cases with separate returns. Both mutants changed a line no edge's tier depended on, because `isImport` is true for every `imports` edge `addImport` emits and the function returns before the switch is reached. Reading a survivor as 'the fixtures do not check the tier' would have been wrong twice: the fixtures checked it and the tier had a different home. The `Imports` case was then DELETED as an L2 dead branch and the tier is decided, and tested, at the one line that actually decides it. Caught by imports-psb12's `meta.evidenceClass: "import_based"` constraint on all six `imports` rows.

PS23 REVERT, the other direction, and the reason this wave did not REPLACE the `references` edge: the module dependency is published as `imports` only. That is the shape a lane reaches by 'fixing' the missing type with a rename, and it is a regression rather than a repair — bash emits both channels for `source ./x.sh` (`imports` for module resolution, `references` for a general dependency edge) and the store's M60/#910 file-level seam keys on the `references` row's `metadata.fileLevel`. Removing the `references` edge would leave the module dependency present in the graph and invisible to every consumer that reads the channel the lane already published. Caught by imports-psb12's `references` row on `Pester` with `meta.import: true`, and by its `references == 7` count.

PS24 REVERT, the COMMA LIST: at most one module name per `#requires` declaration. That is the pre-PS24 reader verbatim — `extractRequiresValue` scanned forward from the flag and stopped at the first space, tab or comma, so `#requires -Modules CimCmdlets, PSReadLine` published `CimCmdlets` and dropped `PSReadLine`, which the file genuinely declares and which therefore did not appear in `imports[]` or in the graph at all. Measured over the 1,092-file admitted corpus: ONE occurrence of a comma-separated `#requires` module list — `#Requires -Modules PSScriptAnalyzer, PSSA-PSCustomUseLiteralPath` at `ansible/test/lib/ansible_test/_util/controller/sanity/pslint/pslint.ps1:2` — so `PSSA-PSCustomUseLiteralPath` was a declared dependency the lane read and dropped. The one resolution rule the header argues for at length: a DOTTED name in protobuf is written fully qualified, so `extend google.protobuf.MessageOptions` inside `package a` means the GLOBAL google.protobuf.MessageOptions. The pre-fix fallback prefixed the package to every unresolved reference and so produced `a.google.protobuf.MessageOptions`, a type that exists in no file. Reverted by prefixing the package to any `uses` target that is dotted and does not already carry the package prefix — the result's own `metadata.protoPackage` supplies the package, so the transform stays valid on any fixture. Caught by protobuf/payload-and-ontology, whose `User.created` row pins `uses -> google.protobuf.Timestamp` at the absolute spelling.

A leading dot in a protobuf type reference means ABSOLUTE: `.google.protobuf.Timestamp` names the global type whatever the enclosing package is, and stripping the dot and resolving from the innermost scope outward lands on `demo.v1.google.protobuf.Timestamp`. This is the half of the resolution contract the dotted-fallback mutant does not exercise, and it is separate from it: fixing one leaves the other live. Reverted by re-prefixing the package onto any `uses` target that is neither package-qualified nor a name the file itself declares — the analyzer records `metadata.protoPackage`, and the declared set is rebuilt from the result's own symbols, so the transform does not depend on a fixture's names. Caught by protobuf/absolute-and-scope-resolution, whose `.demo.v1.Role` and `Outer.Inner` rows pin the absolute case and the scope walk independently.

A protobuf reference resolves from the INNERMOST enclosing scope outward, so inside `Outer`, the name `Inner` is `Outer.Inner` and not the top-level `Inner` — a shape protobuf permits precisely because two scopes may declare the same leaf name. The pre-fix resolver compared only the last dot segment against a package-prefixed concatenation and produced `demo.v1.Auth.demo.v1.User`, a name in no file; the fix compares whole ids along the scope chain. Reverted by moving every `uses` edge off a NESTED declaration onto the top-level declaration of the same leaf name where one exists, which is the defect this rule exists to prevent expressed in its other direction: a resolver that starts its walk at the outermost scope instead of the innermost. Caught by protobuf/absolute-and-scope-resolution, whose `Outer.inner` and `Outer.Deepest.inner` rows both pin the NESTED `Outer.Inner` while a top-level `Inner` is declared in the same file, so an analyzer that reached either would fail.

A `type` node holding no `message_or_enum_type` child is a scalar KEYWORD — `string`, `int32`, `bytes` — and there is no declaration of it anywhere, so a `uses` edge onto one points at nothing. The analyzer decides this by construction rather than from a hardcoded scalar list, which is what makes an unrecognised scalar safe. Reverted by giving every `property` the analyzer marked `metadata.scalar` a `uses` edge onto its own `metadata.type`. This is the fabrication defect the workstream calls the most expensive one available, because an edge onto a non-symbol poisons bb_graph, bb_impact and bb_migrate. Caught by protobuf/payload-and-ontology, whose forbid rows name `uses -> string` for both a plain field and a map value.

A map field's KEY type is a scalar by specification — the grammar admits no other kind there — so the key is never a reference, while the VALUE is an ordinary type reference and does produce an edge. Treating the two alike publishes an edge onto a keyword. Reverted by emitting a second `uses` edge from every `isMap` property onto its `metadata.mapKey`. Caught by protobuf/payload-and-ontology, whose map forbid row pins the absence for a `map<string, string>` field; the value edge is pinned by the same fixture, so the pair cannot be satisfied by dropping both.

An rpc names a request AND a response, and the grammar gives both the same node type with no field name, so they are told apart by position. Emitting one edge per rpc records half the fact and makes `Login -> User` indistinguishable from an rpc whose response differs. Reverted by dropping every `uses` edge tagged `role: rpcResponse`. Caught by protobuf/payload-and-ontology, whose `expectRelationshipCount` pins `equals: 2` for a request and response that are the SAME type — a suite that only checked presence would report a pass here, which is why the count row exists.

A oneof's fields belong to the MESSAGE, not to the oneof: the field number lives in the message's own space and `msg.field` is how every protobuf tool names it. Grouping is a different relation from ownership, so the grouping travels as `metadata.oneof` and `contains` means ownership only. Reverted by re-owning every `union`-flagged field to its oneof and moving the `contains` edge with it — which is exactly the pre-fix shape, and it also manufactures the second `contains` edge the header argues against. Caught by protobuf/payload-and-ontology, which pins `contains User -> User.email` AND forbids `contains User.contact -> User.email`, so neither half alone passes.

`extend Foo { … }` adds fields to a type this file does NOT declare, so the block is not a declaration and publishing a symbol for it is a fabricated type: a phantom that then becomes the source of a fabricated containment edge and a second, disagreeing copy of a type that already has an owner in the file that declares it. The analyzer emits no block symbol for this reason. Reverted by minting one `class` symbol per `viaExtension` member's owner that the file does not itself declare, and a `contains` edge from the phantom to each of that owner's members — the pre-fix shape. Caught by protobuf/extend-and-group, which forbids the phantom symbol name outright and pins the total symbol count, so neither half of the fabrication can be satisfied by removing only the edge.

A proto2 `group` declares a nested type AND a field of the same name in the same message, so on a bare `owner.name` id the two collide and the `uses` edge that should run field→type loops a symbol onto itself. The fix disambiguates the second id with a `#<kind>` suffix and PUBLISHES the resolved id on `metadata.id`, so a consumer re-deriving `ownerName + "." + name` cannot reconstruct the wrong one. Reverted by rewriting every `#`-disambiguated id back to its bare form, which restores both the collision and the self-edge. Caught by protobuf/extend-and-group, which pins two DISTINCT symbols for the group, the `uses` edge between them, and forbids the self-edge.

`import public` is a re-export: this file's importers reach the imported declarations THROUGH it, which is a fact about the module graph and not derivable from the path. The modifier is an anonymous token child, read off the tree, because matching the declaration's text for an `import public` prefix is a parser in disguise and misfires on any grammar change. Reverted by dropping `metadata.modifier` from every import. Caught by protobuf/imports-and-editions, which pins `public`, `weak` and the editions `option` import form, and forbids an import with no modifier claiming one.

`stream` is an anonymous sibling immediately BEFORE the type it qualifies, so client- and server-streaming are read off the tree. The pre-fix version tested the rpc's text for `(stream`, which is a text scan AND wrong on `option (x) = "stream(1)"` — a quoted value that mentions the keyword. Reverted by forcing both streaming flags false on every rpc. Caught by protobuf/streaming-and-forward-refs, which pins one client-streaming, one server-streaming and one bidirectional rpc, and forbids the flags on a unary rpc — a suite pinning only the positive cases would pass an analyzer that set every flag true.

`reserved` records field numbers and names a schema has RETIRED, and `extensions` records where other files may add members. Both are what makes a migration audit possible, and both are facts about the schema rather than about a declaration, so they attach to the owning message's metadata — the scope the specification gives them — or to the file at file scope. Reverted by stripping both lists. Caught by protobuf/extend-and-group, which pins the message-level ranges, the message-level reserved NAMES and the file-scope list separately, so a rule that moved one to the other scope would fail too.

The resolved id is published as `metadata.id` rather than left to be re-derived, because a consumer that rebuilds `ownerName + "." + name` reconstructs the WRONG id for a proto2 group and for any damaged input — which is how the corpus probe first reported 28 phantom duplicate ids and 48 phantom unresolved endpoints. Reverted by deleting `metadata.id` from every symbol. Caught by protobuf/extend-and-group, whose group rows are keyed on the two distinct ids, and by protobuf/payload-and-ontology's endpoint rows.

A REGRESSION guard for a defect this lane measured and fixed, not a revert of a pre-fix draft. Protobuf resolves a type name through nested scopes, and only TYPES are in that namespace; a field declares no type. The resolver accepted every declaration, so an ordinary field whose NAME equals the type it names answered its own type reference: `message Extra { repeated IPAMStatus IPAMStatus = 1; }` published the field as `pkg.Extra.IPAMStatus` moments before emitting its edge, the innermost scope candidate matched the field, and the edge became `pkg.Extra.IPAMStatus -> pkg.Extra.IPAMStatus`. Measured: 9 self-edges over 606 corpus files — docker/daemon/cluster/convert/netextra/extra.proto:12 and 8 under docker/vendor/github.com/moby/buildkit (api/types/worker.proto:13-14, frontend/gateway/pb/gateway.proto:173/193/197, solver/pb/ops.proto:117/120/317). A self-edge is the shape a fabricated edge takes when two declarations collide on one id, so bb_graph, bb_impact and bb_migrate would each read it as a field whose type is itself. Reverted by resolving against EVERY declaration again — the result's own symbol table gives the containing message of each `property`, and a `uses` edge from that property onto an id with the same leaf name is moved onto it. Caught by protobuf/absolute-and-scope-resolution, whose `SelfNamed.Inner` row pins the top-level type and whose forbid row pins the ABSENCE of the self-edge; the `SelfNamed.shadow` row is the control, since it has no collision for this defect to exploit.

A dependency graph for a schema language that cannot answer `which file does this type come from` is missing the one edge a consumer needs most, and its absence is invisible to a differential because the oracle was written after the same ruling. Measured before this lane's change: 1,117 `import` nodes across 392 of 606 corpus files were recorded into `result.imports` and emitted as NO edge at all. Reverted by dropping every `imports` relationship while leaving the `imports[]` array intact, which is exactly the pre-fix state — the array was already correct, so this mutant is faithful rather than a wholesale deletion. Caught by protobuf/imports-and-editions, which pins all three non-public forms including the editions feature import.

`import public` is a RE-EXPORT: this file's own importers reach the imported declarations through it. Recorded as a plain import it becomes an ordinary dependency, the re-export fact is lost, and a consumer asking which of two files importing the same path republishes it gets the same answer for both. Measured: 4 occurrences in 4 files (pb-reference/src/google/protobuf/{cpp_options,json_options,unittest_import,unittest_import_lite}.proto). Reverted by relabelling every `exports` edge as `imports` and dropping its `viaPublicImport` marker — the shape an analyzer that knew about imports but not re-exports produces. Caught by protobuf/imports-and-editions, which pins an `exports` row AND forbids the `imports` row for the same target, so relabelling alone cannot satisfy it.

The SOURCE of a module edge is the importing file and the TARGET is the path as written. Taking the basename of the IMPORTED path for the source — which a first draft of this change did, before the suite caught it — makes a file appear to depend on ITSELF: `import public "common/v1/types.proto"` became `types.proto -> common/v1/types.proto`, an edge whose two endpoints name the same module, which bb_graph reads as a self-dependency and bb_impact reads as a cycle. Reverted by re-sourcing every module edge onto the basename of its own target. Caught by protobuf/imports-and-editions, whose forbid row names the self-import shape explicitly.

Every edge this analyzer emits is read off the parse tree — a declaration node, a named child, an anonymous sibling token, a position — so its tier is `structural`, or `import_based` for an import. Measured before this lane's change: 40,562 of 40,562 production edges carried NO `evidenceClass`, so the honesty contract's requirement that a heuristic be COUNTABLE had nothing to count and the graph panel had to infer a tier from the confidence value instead. Reverted by deleting the key from every edge. Caught by protobuf/imports-and-editions, whose rows pin `meta.evidenceClass` on both a `contains` edge and an `imports` edge — the two different tiers, so an analyzer that stamped one constant on everything would fail as well.

Every relationship this analyzer emits is a parse FACT — a declaration node, a named child, a position — so the honest confidence is 1.0 and nothing lands under the 0.7 threshold the contract reserves for name-match guesses. Reverted by writing 0.5 on every edge, which is the shape a heuristic guess would take and which the contract requires to be countable. Caught by protobuf/streaming-and-forward-refs, whose every relationship row carries `confidenceMin: 0.9` — a fixture that asserted no confidence would pass this mutant, and then the workstream's heuristic-ratio question would have no answer for this lane.

The `overrides` rule pass 1 did not have. What protobuf can express as an override is a field SLOT restated: two declarations in one message claiming the same number. This mutant reverts the rule to the reading pass 1's own probe used — 'a name declared twice in one scope' — which is the reading that fires on a name collision that replaces nothing, because the two claims occupy different slots. Reverted by dropping every `overrides` edge whose two endpoints carry DIFFERENT `metadata.fieldNumber`s, i.e. keeping only the name-and-number shape and deleting the slot shape. That is the pre-fix state: `string legacy = 7; int64 modern = 7;` restates slot 7 under a fresh name and the edge disappears, while `string dup = 3; bool dup = 3;` survives, so the corpus count of 1 that pass 1 measured was a coincidence of one syntax-highlighting fixture rather than a measurement of the construct. Caught by protobuf/slot-and-grouping, whose `Slot.modern -> Slot.legacy` row requires the slot shape. Its `Twin` forbid rows are the other half: they fail an analyzer whose rule is 'a repeated NAME', which is the mutant the fixture exists to keep out.

The `overrides` edge's `line_number` must be the SOURCE's line, because `line_number` is what `bb_graph` and the store's relId key on. The walk is a LIFO stack and reaches siblings in reverse document order, so the declaration being ADDED when the collision is noticed is usually the EARLIER one — this is measured, not hypothetical: the first version of the rule reported the override of slot 7 at line 26, which is `legacy`, the declaration being overridden, while the source `modern` is line 27. Reverted by rewriting each `overrides` edge's line to the LOWER of its two endpoints' lines, which is the same wrong answer for a forward-declared pair and cannot be told apart from the correct one by an assertion that does not read the source. Caught by protobuf/slot-and-grouping, whose two `overrides` rows pin line 27 and line 36 — the sources — and whose forbid rows name the same two symbol pairs, so an edge with the right endpoints and the wrong line still fails.

`metadata.oneof` is how a oneof's grouping travels, since `contains` means ownership only and there is deliberately no edge from the oneof to its fields. It carried the oneof's BARE name, which cannot address a oneof: two messages in one file may each declare `oneof body`, and a consumer grouping fields by that string merges two unrelated discriminated unions. Measured over the corpus before the change: 423 of 1,121 oneof fields (37.73%) sat under a bare name declared by more than one owner — `oneof attrs` in 7 different messages of boundary's session_recording.proto alone. Reverted by truncating every `metadata.oneof` to its last dotted segment, rebuilt from the result's own symbols rather than from a fixture name. Caught by protobuf/slot-and-grouping, which declares `oneof body` in two messages and requires the two fields' keys to be the two RESOLVED ids — an analyzer emitting the bare name fails both rows, and neither row can be satisfied by emitting nothing.

`viaExtension` was carried on the extension field's SYMBOL and not on the EDGE that adds it to the extended type, so a consumer reading `google.protobuf.MessageOptions -contains-> audit_ticket` could not tell a field added by an `extend` block in another file from one declared in MessageOptions' own body — and this analyzer's own header claimed the edge carried it, which made the header false. Measured over the corpus before the change: 0 of the extension-derived `contains` edges carried `viaExtension`. Reverted by deleting the key from every edge whose metadata has it, leaving the symbol's copy intact — the exact pre-fix shape, in which the two are not derived from each other and the flag can drift. Caught by protobuf/extend-and-group, whose two rows now require `meta.viaExtension` ON THE EDGE. The same fixture's plain-field rows in protobuf/payload-and-ontology forbid the flag there, so stamping it on every edge fails as well.

`import public "x.proto"` is BOTH a dependency and a re-export: `protoc` records it as a `FileDescriptorProto` dependency like any other, with `public_dependency` naming its index. Pass 1 emitted `exports` alone, pinned the absence of `imports` with a fixture forbid, and the fixture's stated reason — that emitting both 'would double the module's inbound dependency and lose the re-export fact entirely' — is wrong on both halves: nothing is doubled, because the pair went from ZERO `imports` edges to one, and the re-export fact is what the `exports` edge carries. Reverted by dropping every `imports` edge that also appears as an `exports` edge on the same source and target, which is exactly the pre-fix state. Caught by protobuf/imports-and-editions, whose public-import rows now REQUIRE both labels, so neither reading satisfies the fixture alone.

Pass 16 measured that the `imports`/`exports` SOURCE resolved against published ids at 0 of 1,561 + 4 edges, and that 967 of 1,565 (61.8%) hung off a basename another corpus file also uses. The source is now the file's own `package` namespace, which the analyzer already publishes. This mutant is the pre-pass-16 state, reproduced GENERICALLY: any `imports`/`exports` edge whose `metadata.moduleOwner` is `package` has its source replaced by `path.basename(metadata.filePath)`. Caught by protobuf/imports-and-editions and protobuf/ancestor-scope-resolution, whose module-edge rows name the package as the source, and by protobuf/module-edge-source-fallback, which pins the other arm so the transform cannot be satisfied by always emitting a basename either.

The same rule read `pkg` without checking it, which is what happens to a file declaring no `package`: 11 of 821 corpus files, carrying 5 of the 1,561 `imports` edges. The edge is published with the EMPTY STRING as its source, which is an endpoint the index cannot hold and the graph cannot walk from. Reverted generically: any `imports`/`exports` edge whose `metadata.moduleOwner` is `basename` — which is exactly the set of edges whose file declared no package — has its source emptied. Caught by protobuf/module-edge-source-fallback, whose fallback row names the basename and whose `forbidRelationships` carries `{type: "imports", from: ""}` for this shape. No other fixture can catch it: all ten other protobuf fixtures declare a package.

`metadata.moduleOwner` is the only thing that tells a consumer whether an unresolvable module-edge source is a file that declares no package — an external-by-necessity endpoint — or a name the analyzer simply failed to publish. Without it the two are indistinguishable, which is the same confusion this lane separates everywhere else (an external package versus a declaration it failed to publish). Reverted by deleting the key from every edge that carries it. Caught by protobuf/module-edge-source-fallback, which asserts `meta.moduleOwner: "basename"` on its fallback row, and by protobuf/imports-and-editions and protobuf/ancestor-scope-resolution, which assert it on the package arm.

A relative DOTTED type name is resolved through the package's ANCESTOR scopes, because protobuf's rule is C++ name lookup over every enclosing scope and not only the package subtree. The pre-fix behaviour was to emit such a name exactly as written, which is the shape of all 431 corpus edges that named an id no file publishes: `resources.scopes.v1.ScopeInfo` where the declaration is `controller.api.resources.scopes.v1.ScopeInfo`. This transform rewrites a target back to the name as written ONLY where the walk moved ALONG a shared ancestor path — the target's package shares a leading segment with the source's own package but is not equal to it, which is the corpus shape and is what makes the transform fire on the row under test and not on the guard's row. Caught by protobuf/ancestor-scope-resolution, which requires the ancestor-resolved id and forbids the name as written as well as the package-prefixed reading. Nothing is dropped, so a transform that emitted no edge at all would fail the same three rows.

The ancestor walk accepts a candidate only when the matched import directory is not a proper SUFFIX of a more specific candidate's directory, and that condition is what a `-I` root ABOVE the package looks like. Dropping it was measured at 7 wrong corpus ids: docker vendors containerd, whose `api/types/platform.proto` declares `package containerd.types;` and is imported as `types/platform.proto`, so a guardless walk answers `types.Platform` where `protoc` answers `containerd.types.Platform`. This transform reproduces the guardless answer for the ONE shape the guard exists for — a reference whose package is a SINGLE segment, so every ancestor candidate is strictly longer and `types` is a proper suffix of all of them — and fires on nothing else. Caught by protobuf/ancestor-scope-resolution alone, and by exactly two of its rows: the `Shifted` requirement (`types.Platform`) goes missing and the innermost-candidate forbid (`corp.api.resources.accounts.v1.types.Platform`) appears instead. Measured rather than described: the walk reaches the MOST SPECIFIC ancestor first, so the id it asserts is that one and not `corp.types.Platform` — which is a second forbid row in the fixture, added so the chain ORDER is pinned independently of the guard. The ancestor-walk row is untouched by this mutant, which is what separates it from the mutant above.

A type written inside an `extend` block is resolved from where the block is WRITTEN, because `extend` opens no scope: the extended type is where the block's members GO, not a scope their types are looked up in. `Ctx` therefore carries `scope` (the lexical position) separately from `owner` (the extended type), and the `extend` case inherits `ctx.scope` unchanged. This transform reinstates the single value by re-pointing the SCOPE at the OWNER for every symbol whose owner is an extended type — i.e. the pre-fix behaviour — which is exactly the defect class: a field inside `extend google.protobuf.FieldOptions` had `google.protobuf.FieldOptions` handed to the resolver as its scope, every candidate derived from it fell outside the package subtree and was dropped, and a reference to a type nested in the enclosing messages resolved to nothing.

MEASURED end to end, by two independent instruments and not by argument. Corpus-wide, this transform moves 6 of 13,275 `uses` targets and adds and removes no edge. `protoc` 36.2, run as an oracle over the corpus (`script/m14/tmp/protobuf/probe/protoc-oracle.py`), reads exactly those 6 as disagreements and nothing else: WRONG-NAME 47 before, 42 after, on 11,250 judged edges, with 5 verdict flips and 0 new ones. Each flip is a case where `protoc` names a nested declaration the pre-fix analyzer could not see — `proto2_unittest.ComplexOptionType2.ComplexOptionType4`, `proto2_unittest.TestExtensionOrderings2.TestExtensionOrderings3`, `edition_unittest.TestExtensionOrderings2.TestExtensionOrderings3`, `proto2_unittest.TestNestedExtension.OptionalGroup_extension` and `edition_unittest.TestNestedExtension.OptionalGroup_extension`. The 6th moved edge is in `unittest_delimited.proto`, where `protoc` reports two declarations under one owner-qualified name and the oracle records INDISTINCTUISHABLE rather than guessing; read by hand from `protoc`'s descriptor it answers `editions_unittest.LengthPrefixed`, which is the post-fix emitted name.

Caught by protobuf/nested-extend-scope, whose two rows are the two directions: ROW 1 (a block nested inside the type it names) loses `nse.demo.Nest.Leaf` and regains the forbidden `nse.demo.Leaf`; ROW 2 (a FILE-SCOPE block with two declarations named `Twin`) loses `nse.demo.Twin` and regains the forbidden `nse.demo.Dual.Twin`. ROW 2 is what stops this mutant from being satisfiable by 'always prefer the innermost declaration', and ROW 3 (an ordinary field resolving to the nested type) is the control neither direction may break. Ownership is asserted on both extension members, so a transform that moved the resolution scope by also moving ownership would fail on a `contains` row rather than pass.

The resolved id is published on the symbol through TWO channels — `qualifiedName` (the one pool-worker's projection carries into `brain_symbol.qualified_name`, which is the column `resolveRelationships` strategy 1 matches a relationship's target against) and `metadata.qualifiedName` (the one a fixture can assert, because `run-fixtures.ts`'s `CONSTRAINT_KEY_ALLOWLIST` carries no `qualifiedName`). This transform deletes both, which is the pre-fix state. It reverts the RULE rather than one line: the two assignments are the same value on the two channels a consumer can reach, and reverting one alone would be a mutant of a line while the rule stayed published. Measured cost of the pre-fix state, end to end through the real indexer and the real store over 40 reference `.proto` files (script/m14/tmp/protobuf/probe/store-binding.mts, two runs each): 0 of 3,075 analyzer edges were PROVABLY the declaration the edge named, against 2,977 of 3,075 with it — and `contains` 0 of 2,565 against 2,563, `uses` 0 of 489 against 414. A fixture cannot see the store binding, so it pins the published value on both channels and the probe carries the store half.

A proto2 `group` declared inside an `extend` block has its TYPE declared at the BLOCK'S OWN SCOPE; only its FIELD belongs to the extendee. `Ctx` carries `scope` (the lexical position) separately from `owner` (the extendee), and the group's type takes `scope`. This transform reinstates the single value by re-pointing a group's TYPE at the EXTENDEE — the pre-fix behaviour — which is a fabricated declaration: `optional group GroupField = 121` written in a file-scope `extend TestAllTypesProto2` in `pb-reference/src/google/protobuf/test_messages_proto2.proto` produced a nested type `protobuf_test_messages.proto2.TestAllTypesProto2.GroupField`, which `protoc` 36.2's descriptor does not contain anywhere. The extension is recorded in the descriptor's top-level `extension` list with `type_name = .protobuf_test_messages.proto2.GroupField`, so the type is a FILE-SCOPE message and the extendee owns only the field.

MEASURED end to end by `protoc`'s descriptor as an oracle over the corpus (script/m14/tmp/protobuf/probe/protoc-descriptor-oracle.py, 821 files, 781 compiled), not by argument: `contains` agreement 36,017 of 37,042 judged with this mutant against 36,022 of 37,042 without it, and the oracle's `unexplained` bucket — the rows its stated rules cannot account for, which is the number that has to be zero — reads 7 with this mutant and 0 without it. The 7 are: the two phantom group TYPES (`…TestAllTypesProto2.GroupField`, `proto2_unittest.ComplexOpt6`), the three group MEMBERS published under them, and the two extension FIELD rows that cannot be matched because the type they name was never published at the scope protoc gives it. 7 corpus `contains` edges move, 0 are added, 0 are removed.

Caught by protobuf/group-in-extend-scope, whose three rows are the three directions. ROW 1 (a file-scope `extend`) loses `gie.demo.Hoisted` and regains the forbidden `gie.demo.Target.Hoisted` groupType row — the corpus defect's shape. ROW 2 (an `extend` nested inside a MESSAGE) loses `gie.demo.Outer.Inner` and regains the forbidden `gie.demo.Outer.Holder.Inner`, which is what stops the rule being satisfiable by 'always hoist to the package' — the companion mutant below is that rule. ROW 3 (a group already inside its owner) is the control in the other direction and is byte-identical in both arms. The field->type `uses` edge is asserted too, because a transform that moved the type's owner while leaving the `uses` target alone would produce one right edge and one wrong one.

The COMPANION to `protobuf/group-type-owned-by-the-extendee`, and the reason the fixture has three rows rather than one. Re-hoisting every group's type to the FILE's package satisfies `protobuf/group-type-owned-by-the-extendee`'s corpus evidence — both corpus groups with a misplaced type are inside a file-scope `extend` block, so 'always the package' produces the same 36,022 of 37,042 and the same `unexplained` 0 on this corpus — and is wrong for a group declared inside an `extend` block that is itself nested in a message.

protobuf resolves that case to the ENCLOSING MESSAGE's scope. `protoc` 36.2 on `validation/m14/fixtures/protobuf/group-in-extend-scope.proto` reports, for an `extend Holder` block written inside `message Outer`, the nested message `gie.demo.Outer.Inner` and the in-message extension `inner` with `extendee = .gie.demo.Outer.Holder` and `type_name = .gie.demo.Outer.Inner` — so hoisting to the package would publish `gie.demo.Inner`, which protoc does not define. The corpus contains no such case: measured over all 821 files, every one of the 8 groups sits either directly in a message body or in a file-scope `extend`, so this defect is INVISIBLE to the corpus oracle and is caught only by the fixture. That is the honest reason a fixture exists alongside a corpus oracle, and it is stated here because the alternative — quoting the corpus number as though it covered this — would be the same mistake in a different place.

Caught by protobuf/group-in-extend-scope ROW 2, which loses `gie.demo.Outer.Inner` and regains the explicitly forbidden `gie.demo -> gie.demo.Outer.Inner` groupType row. ROW 1 (file scope) and ROW 3 (already inside its owner) are unaffected by this mutant, which is what makes ROW 2 load-bearing rather than decorative.

MEASURED, and this is the number that makes the fixture necessary: the corpus contains 10 `groupType` edges, of which 2 sit in a file-scope `extend` block (their type's owner is the package), 8 sit directly in a message body (their type's owner is that message), and 0 sit in an `extend` block nested inside a message. So this mutant produces the same 36,022 of 37,042 and the same `unexplained` 0 as the correct analyzer on every file in the corpus, while being wrong on every group written in an in-message `extend` block. It is also caught by protobuf/extend-and-group, whose groups live in message bodies and are therefore over-hoisted by it — so two fixtures catch it and one corpus does not.

An extension member's PUBLISHED ID is built from the block's own enclosing declaration chain plus the member's own name. The EXTENDEE is a separate descriptor field (`extendee`), never part of the name, so an id carrying it is a name no compiler defines. This transform reinstates the single value by re-building every extension member's id from the EXTENDED TYPE that the `contains` edge already names as its source — the pre-pass-21 behaviour, reproduced generically from the analyzer's own `metadata.viaExtension` flag and its `contains` edges, so editing a fixture cannot silently stop it matching.

It leaves the `contains` edge's SOURCE and the symbol's `ownerName` alone: membership is unchanged and `contains` means membership, so only the edge's TARGET is re-pointed along with the id. That is what makes the mutant SELF-CONSISTENT — a mutant whose edges dangled would fail every fixture for the wrong reason and prove nothing about this rule. A group's FIELD moves with the other members, because its published id is the member id plus the `#property` disambiguator and its `contains` edge carries `viaExtension` like any other extension member's. A group's TYPE does NOT move, and the mutant does not pretend otherwise: that id already took the block's own scope before pass 21 (it is the same value the sibling mutant `protobuf/group-type-owned-by-the-extendee` reinstates a violation of), so pass 21 left it alone and reverting pass 21 leaves it alone too.

MEASURED by `protoc` as the discriminator, not by argument. Pass 20 reported 50 colliding ids within one repository as a bare count; `script/m14/protobuf-classb-protoc-adjudication.mts` ran libprotoc 35.1 over those 50 and read its own duplicate-symbol diagnostic: 41 REJECTED the set (a corpus fact — no compilation unit holds both files, so the id is correct in each), 4 inconclusive (an unresolved import, so the compiler never reached the check), and 5 ACCEPTED it. Those 5 are one symbol the analyzer published as two, and every one is an extension member, in one repository: `google.protobuf.FeatureSet.test` (`unittest_features.proto:32` declares `test = 9999` in package `pb`; `unittest_custom_features.proto:14` declares `test = 9995` in package `custom_features`), `google.protobuf.FieldOptions.field_opt1`, `google.protobuf.FileOptions.file_opt1` and `google.protobuf.MessageOptions.message_opt1` between `unittest_custom_options.proto` and `unittest_custom_options_unlinked.proto`, and `google.protobuf.MessageOptions.custom_option_lifetimes_message` between `unittest_custom_options.proto` and `unittest_features.proto`. Re-running that same probe over the same 842 files with this analyzer at HEAD reads 50 rows and 5 ACCEPTED, and with the fix reads 45 rows and 0 ACCEPTED, with 38,876 distinct published ids before and 38,881 after: the five removed rows are exactly the five protoc accepted, and no row was added. Read back from `protoc`'s descriptor on the fixtures, the names it defines are `ext.v1.extra`, `ext.v1.counts`, `ext.v1.audit_ticket`, `gie.demo.Hoisted`, `gie.demo.Outer.Inner`, `nse.demo.which_twin` and `nse.demo.Nest.Leaf.leaf_ref` — every one the span this transform reverts.

Caught by three fixtures, and each is load-bearing. protobuf/extend-and-group loses `ext.v1.extra` and regains the forbidden `ext.v1.Container.extra`, so an analyzer that hoists only to the PACKAGE cannot pass by accident. protobuf/group-in-extend-scope loses `gie.demo.Hoisted#property` and regains the forbidden `gie.demo.Target.Hoisted#property`; its ROW 2 is the guard, so the rule cannot be satisfied by 'always the file's package'. protobuf/nested-extend-scope covers the third depth — a block nested inside the type whose name it references — losing `nse.demo.Nest.Leaf.leaf_ref` and `nse.demo.which_twin`. The `uses` rows matter as much as the `contains` ones: a transform that moved the member id but left the field->type edge alone would produce one right edge and one wrong one.

Prefixes the file's own `package` onto a DOTTED type name whenever the import-directory guard declines — the defect the analyzer avoids by construction, reproduced here so the refusal has a regression test rather than being an unexamined gap.

`resolveViaImports` returns the name AS WRITTEN when no enclosing scope's candidate directory is one this file imports, because that is the only honest outcome: the import path is relative to an include root the analyzer is never told, so path and package are independent and the path is not evidence about any package name. The tempting repair is to fall back on the package-relative reading that UNQUALIFIED names already get.

Measured over all 842 on-disk corpus files, that fallback would be wrong on every dotted name the guard declines, and it is wrong in a way no fixture can miss: it produces a fully-qualified-looking id that no file anywhere publishes. `extend google.protobuf.MessageOptions` inside `package a` would become `a.google.protobuf.MessageOptions`, which the language cannot declare.

The corpus shapes it breaks, from script/m14/protobuf-ambiguity-split.mts over 842 files and 13,024 `uses` edges: 42 edges on 12 distinct targets whose leaf IS declared under a different id — `common.EnterpriseMeta`, `common.RaftIndex`, `common.Locality`, `types.Platform`, `types.Metric`, `NodeSpec.Membership`, `connect.IssuedCert`, `connect.CARoots`, `config.Config`, `common.QueryMeta`, `status.Status`, `NodeSpec.Availability` — plus 4 edges whose leaf is declared nowhere. PY-24 REVERT: `__all__` is treated as export METADATA only, so an `__all__` assigned in a CLASS body publishes exports and never becomes a class member. `__all__` is in that class's `__dict__` like any other assignment, so this drops a real `contains` edge — the corpus row `contains CythonDotParallel -> __all__` at cython/Cython/Shadow.py, which was the last missing relationship left in the whole python corpus. Caught by python/class-dunder-all-is-not-exports. NOTE ON WHAT THIS MUTANT CANNOT EXPRESS: the revert had a second half — publishing `exports module -> alpha/beta` for names inside a class `__all__` — and that half is NOT reproducible here. It is an ABSENCE of scope information in the result: once the gate is correct, nothing in `r` records which `__all__` literals were skipped, so a result-shaped transform cannot re-add them. Reconstructing them from fixture strings is what the `dunder-all-tuple-ignored` comment above records as having produced a no-op that reported 0 -> 0 and read as a survivor. The false-exports half is therefore covered ONLY by the fixture's three forbid rows, which is the honest split: a mutant that cannot be written without guessing names is a mutant that proves nothing.

The EAGER side of the binding-scope line: a class-body variable binding is suppressed outright, not only when a lambda or comprehension encloses it. Every Property carrying `isClassVariable` is dropped along with its `contains` edge, so no class body publishes a member at all. This is the direction a fix for the lambda-parameter fabrication is most likely to overshoot into — 'stop publishing names bound in a scope' is one step from 'stop publishing names bound in a class body' — and the two differ on every real member: `walrus_direct` IS a class attribute in python, verified with `vars()`, as are `via_lambda` and `from_comprehension`. Caught by python/lambda-scope-is-not-class-scope, whose positives were read out of CPython rather than asserted, which is the only reason this line has both directions pinned: the fabrication side by FORBID rows and the over-suppression side by positive rows. A fixture carrying only one of the two would accept half the possible fixes. Stated honestly: the faithful revert of the scope guard itself cannot be written here, because the guard asks a question about the TREE and a ParseResult does not carry one. A no-op reporting 0 -> 0 would have looked like a survivor while modelling nothing, which is the trap three earlier mutants in this lane fell into.

PY-7 REVERT, the subtle half: the companion index IS read, the base IS resolved from it, and then the answer is published as if nothing had been learned — every override the index confirmed is demoted from its verified confidence to the 0.5 `first-parent-guess`. The EDGE is still right, so no membership comparison notices: only the number a reader weighs it by changes. Caught by python/companion-index/comp-child, whose `Redirect.send -> Mixin.send` row carries `confidenceMin: 0.9` precisely so a demotion fails it. Why it is worth a mutant when the obvious reverts already exist: dropping the companion read altogether and dropping its RESULT are different defects with different consequences. The first changes the edge SET — and a set comparison catches it immediately. The second leaves the edge set byte-for-byte intact and corrupts only the ranking, which is the failure a graph consumer cannot detect by looking at WHAT is there. 855 corpus edges sit in exactly this state today, and the census that found them had to compare confidences rather than members to see it at all.

PY-14 REVERT: `exports` is read only from a `list` literal, so `__all__ = ("a", "b")` publishes nothing. The tuple spelling is ordinary older python, and measured over 400 pinned corpus files: 16 `__all__` assignments, 13 lists and 3 tuples that produced no edge at all — 19% of a module's declared public surface invisible for a reason that has nothing to do with the author. Caught by python/module-all-exports, whose first `__all__` is a TUPLE, so a lane that reads only lists satisfies every other expectation in the file and misses these three.

PY-15 REVERT: ONE marker root is removed from the detection table while the rest of the table stays exactly as declared, so the surface still reports itself alive and still passes every reachability check — the defect the table's own comment warns about ('a marker that stops matching is a visible deletion here and not a silent loss of detection') made invisible by making it small. This is the shape the coverage census found in the wild rather than a shape invented for the harness: 7 of 9 declared roots fired ZERO times across 3,271 corpus files, and nothing in the suite noticed, because reachability had been reported as coverage. The transform drops the LAST declared root from `frameworkPatterns` and re-picks the primary from what remains, which is the pre-census table minus its newest row. Caught by python/framework-marker-coverage, whose `detectedFrameworks` row is an EXACT ORDERED list, and by python/framework-surface-pins.

PY-13 REVERT: the module scope is the filename stem VERBATIM, so `my-module.py` publishes the scope `my-module` — not a valid python identifier, not typeable, and not a name a symbol could carry. Found by writing the PY-12 fixture: the harness refused to match the expected `from` because the analyzer spelled the module with a hyphen in it. Caught by python/module-all-exports, whose file is `module-all-exports.py` and whose every export edge must be sourced from `module_all_exports` — the unnormalised spelling matches nothing.

PY-4 REVERT: a statement with no enclosing function or class attributes its relationships to the LITERAL STRING "global" — a python KEYWORD used as a scope name. Three things were wrong at once: it is not a name anything can be navigated to (the M60 R7 class, the same one markdown hit when an empty ATX heading published a symbol named `#`); it is absent from the indexer's GENERIC_SOURCE_NAMES (`unknown, SCSS_FILE_SCOPE, window, exports, default, GlobalScope`), the list of names the store knows are synthetic scopes, so python's took a path no other lane's takes; and it contradicted the same analyzer's own `imports` edges in the same file, which already used the module stem. Caught by python/module-all-exports, whose expected `from` is the module name — a lane spelling the scope `global` cannot match it.

REVERT of the first genuine analyzer defect the independent oracle found: a class written in a CLASS BODY loses its owner again, so no `contains` is derived for it. `Outer.Inner` resolves in python with no lookup machinery, so the nesting is containment rather than a lexical coincidence, and the pre-fix state was 66 `contains` edges the tree supports and the lane did not emit, across 24 corpus files including `_Multipart._Part` in `urllib/parse.py`. The transform drops `ownerName`/`ownerKind` from class symbols whose metadata says `isNestedClass`, which is the pre-fix state exactly. Caught by python/nested-class-containment, whose `contains Outer -> Inner` row is the fix and whose FORBID row — `contains Outer -> Local`, a class in a METHOD — is what stops the eager version from passing: the mutant models the lazy side, the forbid models the eager side, and a change that gets the containment without the guard satisfies one and fails the other.

REVERT of the fourth genuine analyzer defect, and the most damaging of the four: a class VARIABLE on a base is made indistinguishable from a METHOD, so the name-keyed match finds it and the lane publishes an override that overrides nothing — at 0.95, with no `reasonCode`, which reads as a verified fact. `class Base: attr = None` beside `class Derived(Base): def attr(self)` published `Derived.attr -> Base.attr`. There is no method on Base to override: `Base.attr` is the value `None`, which CPython's own `ast` reports as `attr(var)` against `attr(def)`.

The transform PROMOTES the variable's SYMBOL KIND rather than clearing a flag, and that distinction is the whole lesson of writing it: a first version cleared `isClassVariable` in metadata and reported `0 -> 0` — a survivor — because the fix reads `kind`, not that flag. A mutant has to move the field the resolution actually consults. Reproducing the pre-fix observable means reproducing the pre-fix *indistinguishability*, not editing the nearest metadata.

Caught by python/class-variable-is-not-overridden, whose three positives are the half that must survive: a fix that stopped matching on name at all would pass every forbid in that fixture and lose real overrides. In the corpus this was 20 fabricated VERIFIED edges in `Cython/Compiler/Nodes.py`, where Cython declares class state at class level so nearly every method shares a name with a variable on its base.

The class-member OWNER is dropped from every symbol. Nothing in the analyzer fails when this happens — the result still parses, still extracts every symbol, and still emits every `overrides` edge with its correct `Owner.method` source string. The damage is one layer down, in the store: `parallel-indexer.ts` builds `nameToSymbol` with TWO keys per symbol, `name` and `${s.scope || s.ownerName}.${name}`, and the owner-qualified key is the one that makes an `overrides` source resolve to the RIGHT method when several classes in a file declare the same name. Strip `ownerName` and every one of those edges falls back to a bare leaf lookup, which is first-wins. This is the surviving half of the retracted PY-3: the dependency is real and it is load-bearing, so the pin has to be checked rather than assumed. Caught by the `contains` derivation, which reads the same field — which is the honest reason this mutant is caught at all, and worth stating plainly rather than discovering later that the override path itself is unpinned.

PY-6 REVERT: the relationship dedup key goes back to (type, source, target) with NO LINE, which is STRICTLY COARSER than the store's own (source, type, target, line) key. Python makes this idiomatic rather than exotic because the canonical property is a getter/setter pair: both `def`s are real declarations and both published as symbols (measured: L50 and L54 in ansible's `_collection_config.py`), and ONE `contains` edge was emitted — so the setter was unreachable from its class and bb_graph/bb_impact could not reach it. 6 missing `contains` over 120 corpus files before the fix, 0 after. The transform is the pre-fix key exactly: keep the FIRST edge for a (type, source, target) triple and drop the rest, which is what a coarser key does. Caught by python/external-override's sibling shape and by any fixture with two same-named members; the assertion that matters is the EDGE COUNT, not a name, because two symbols sharing a name is the whole defect.

PY-11 REVERT: an uppercase callee that is not a class declared in THIS file produces NO relationship at all, instead of a `calls` edge.
