A payload-only revert is invisible to every count-based gate in the repository, which is why it needs one of its own. Caught by natspec-sol16's five `docstring` pins.

SOL-16 REVERT, the bug the fixture was written for: attach documentation PER COMMENT instead of per RUN, so only the LAST comment of a run survives. This is not hypothetical — it was the first implementation, and it published `library Docs` as documented by `@author Someone` while silently dropping the `@title` and `@notice` above it, i.e. two lines kept out of every three, on every documented declaration in the corpus. Caught by natspec-sol16's exact `docstring` for `Docs` and `SLOT`.

SOL-16 REVERT, the second bug the fixture was written for: do not clear the run anchor after a flush, so a TRAILING comment run at the end of a parent reuses the previous declaration as its target. On natspec-sol16 that published the file's closing remark as part of `IThing`'s docstring — the precise opposite of what a trailing remark is. Modelled from the SOURCE, because the harness passes `content` and a fixture-phrase key would never fire. Caught by natspec-sol16's exact `docstring` for `IThing`. (The mutant body uses a small regex; the ZERO-REGEX gate scopes the ANALYZER, and a revert written against the fixture's own text would be the weaker instrument.)

SOL-17 REVERT: stop publishing applied modifiers on the `decorators` field. 188 corpus symbols over 40 distinct modifier names stop carrying them; no relationship changes, because the `calls` edge for an applied modifier is emitted by the `modifier_invocation` case and is untouched. Caught by modifiers-sol17's four `decorators` pins.

SOL-17 REVERT, the over-collection direction: publish EVERY modifier declared anywhere in the file as a decorator on EVERY function. This is the failure mode of reading modifiers from the enclosing contract instead of from the function's own header, and it is the reason modifiers-sol17 pins `single` as exactly `["onlyOwner"]` — `single` applies one modifier while three are in scope, so this turn would make the fixture fail rather than quietly widen. Caught by modifiers-sol17's `single` and `paired` pins.

SOL-16's audit find: revert the `using_alias` case to looking for DIRECT `identifier` children. The grammar nests the name as `using_alias (user_defined_type (identifier)) (user_definable_operator)`, so the direct-child search is empty for every input and the branch had NEVER fired — 4 `using_alias` nodes in the corpus, all in contracts/account/utils/draft-ERC7579Utils.sol, and 0 edges. Found by a per-case emit census, the same signature as the `revert_statement` dead branch.

SOL-15 REVERT, the payload half: strip `calleeKind` from every `calls` edge. No COUNT changes — 4,331 edges stay 4,331 and every kind's edge count stays put — so nothing but the gate can notice. What is lost is the one field that says whether a callee is a symbol at all, and with it the difference between `abi.encode` (a language namespace), a custom error, and a member declared in another file. That difference is the whole content of the 1,849-row unresolved figure. Caught by call-resolution-sol15's four `meta.calleeKind` pins.

SOL-15 REVERT, the RULE half: report every call as `external`. This is the classifier as it behaves when resolution never runs — and it is what the lane effectively shipped before SOL-15, except that the field did not exist then, so a consumer could not even tell resolution had been skipped. With the field present and flat, the four kinds collapse to one and every count stays identical. Caught by call-resolution-sol15's three `meta.calleeKind` forbids — which is where the closure-order bug WOULD have been caught, had the fixture existed when the bug was written.

SOL-15 REVERT, the never-fired branch: revert the `revert_statement` case to its original form, which tested `node.namedChild(0).type === "identifier"` and was therefore FALSE for every possible input, because the grammar puts an `expression` wrapper there for `revert Boom(1)`, `revert Solo` and `revert("x")` alike. That is 453 custom-error call edges over the 389-file corpus that this lane did not emit AT ALL, and no gate noticed — the kind had a case in the source, so it read as covered. Caught by call-resolution-sol15's `boom -> Boom` row and its `errorRevert` forbid.

IMPORT REVERT, the annotation half. `imports` is not a relationship kind in this product: an import is a `references` edge carrying `metadata.import: true` (the settled convention, the same reason PowerShell PS-7 used it), so the ANNOTATION is what distinguishes an import from any other reference. Stripping it leaves the edge type intact and the meaning gone — 899 edges over the 389-file corpus would stop being imports while every count stayed identical. Caught by all-kinds-sol's two import rows' `meta.import` pins and its `references equals 4`.

IMPORT REVERT, the MEASURED ZERO. `import * as Utils from "./Utils.sol"` produced NO edge while a braced import produced one per name — two import statements yielded one edge, because the reader only looked for a plain import name and the namespace form has only an ALIAS. The edge that was missing is the one naming the local binding, the only name the importing file can use. Caught by all-kinds-sol's `references … -> Utils` row and its `expectImports`, and by the `references equals 4` count, which a rule that handled only two of the three import forms would make 3.

F9 REVERT: the plausible-name gate stops refusing a target containing a path separator, so a bare `import "./Bare.sol";` grows a `references` edge naming the path. That edge can never resolve to a stored symbol, and — the reason F9 exists — it would sit at ZERO `unknownTargets` for exactly as long as it existed, because the metric asks whether a target MATCHES a symbol and a name matching nothing is no more detectable than a name matching something. Measured on a sibling lane: malformed here-string targets sat at 0 unknown indefinitely. The correct state is that a bare import binds no name and so contributes an `imports` payload row and no edge. Caught by all-kinds-sol's `forbidRelationships` row naming the path. The first draft of this transform went the WRONG WAY — it removed path-targeting edges, which is the opposite of a revert of the gate and therefore a no-op, because the gate working means there are none to remove. A revert has to ADD what the gate suppresses.

The `imports` edge is derived from ONE property the analyzer records on it: `metadata.psqlInclude === true`, which only `processPsqlMetaCommand` sets and only for a command word in {i, ir} whose argument is a literal .sql/.psql/.dump path. The obvious wrong implementation emits an import for every `psql_meta_command` node — 143 of them over the 1,460-file census, of which 121 are `\echo`, `\set`, `\gexec`, `\if`, `\endif`, `\gset` and `\pset`, none of which names a file. Reverted by promoting every `psql_meta_command`-derived include to an import regardless of its command: a faithful revert has to invent the metadata the fixed analyzer would not have written, so it is expressed by reading the SOURCE for a backslash directive at a line the analyzer recorded no import on, and emitting the edge the pre-fix code would have produced. Caught by sql/sqld13-ontology-types, whose forbidRelationships name the `\echo` line and whose expectRelationshipCount pins `imports` at 3.

`\i :varname` includes a file whose NAME is computed by an earlier `\set`, and the variable's value lives in another statement. An implementation that trusts the argument text would publish `imports global->:varname`, a target no file declares and no consumer can resolve - a fabricated edge whose only content is the variable's name. The fixed analyzer counts those in `ambiguity.includeNonLiteral` and emits nothing; this revert turns that counter into an edge, so it is faithful in both directions and self-limiting: the edge count FOLLOWS the counter, so a corpus that never writes `\i :var` yields a no-op mutant rather than a fabricated count. The three regression rows in sqld13 exist for this mutant and the fixture labels them as belonging to the REGRESSION population rather than the corpus (measured: 0 of the census corpus's 22 includes look like this). Caught by sql/sqld13-ontology-types, whose forbidImports and forbidRelationships name `:d13_script_var` and `d13_no_suffix`.

The `overrides` edge requires all three of: a replaceable declaration kind (function, procedure, view, materialized view - `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` is a syntax error in PostgreSQL), a name this file ALREADY declared of that kind, and an explicit `OR REPLACE` on the later declaration. The measurements that forced each clause: 20 same-kind re-declarations carry no `OR REPLACE` and PostgreSQL rejects those outright; and Hasura's `10_to_11.sql` declares `CREATE FUNCTION hdb_catalog.hdb_schema_update_event_notifier()` at line 7 and `CREATE TRIGGER hdb_schema_update_event_notifier` at line 25 - the same NAME, two different objects, which a name-keyed probe called a redefinition (43 function / 22 table / 13 view events, before the leaf AND the kind were taken into account). Reverted by publishing an override for every name the file declares under two or more KINDS, which is the name-keyed probe's own contribution. Caught by sql/sqld13-ontology-types, whose `d13_twin` table and `d13_twin` trigger share a name and whose forbidRelationships name `overrides global->d13_twin`.

An `instantiates` edge is emitted only for a `cast` whose `custom_type` FIELD names the type AND whose value side is a CONSTRUCTOR - a `ROW(...)` invocation, or a `list`/`array` node. Every other cast to a named type converts a value that already exists: `nextval('s')::integer`, `col::my_enum`, `null::some_enum`. Measured over the 1,460-file census: 4,406 `cast` nodes, of which the construction-shaped ones against a declared type are 20, against a type no file declares 67 (`::row`, `::struct`, `::geometry` - DuckDB inline type specifications and extension types, none of them a project declaration), and the rest conversions. Reverted by publishing an instantiation for every DECLARED type the file does not already construct, which is the shape an implementation reaches for when it treats a type's mere existence as a construction site. Caught by sql/sqld13-ontology-types, whose `d13_never_built` is declared and never constructed and whose forbidRelationships name `instantiates global->d13_never_built`.

The wired grammar cannot represent `CREATE TABLE c (LIKE p INCLUDING ALL)`: it parses the `LIKE p` pair as `column_definition name:(identifier "LIKE") custom_type:(object_reference "p")`, which the analyzer read as a column named `LIKE` whose type is the source table. Measured 6 such phantom columns corpus-wide in 2 files, each with a fabricated `sqlType`, and the same shape makes `ALTER TABLE c INHERIT p` a column named `INHERIT`. The guard is keyed on the name AND on the node being an unquoted `identifier`, because a quoted `"like"` column arrives as a `literal` and is legal. Reverted by re-publishing each suppressed column: read off the analyzer's OWN `ambiguity.reservedNameSymbolsSuppressed` counter so the revert cannot silently stop matching. Caught by sql/sqld13-ontology-types, whose forbidSymbols name `LIKE` and whose expectSymbolCount pins it at 0 while requiring the quoted `like` column to survive at 1.

`processConstraint` reads a constraint's name from the identifier after `keyword_constraint`. With no `CONSTRAINT` keyword it falls back to `directChild(node, "identifier")`, which exists for MySQL's `UNIQUE KEY <name> (cols)` where the name IS a direct identifier. An unnamed FOREIGN KEY also has direct identifier children and they are the REFERENCED table's columns, so the fallback published `constant:<other table's column>` owned by the referencing table. Oracle-validated over the corpus (validation/m14/fixtures/sql/pass3-phantom-constraint.mts, which decides with a parse-tree walk and not with the name heuristic, because phpMyAdmin's `UNIQUE KEY `db_name` (`db_name`,`table_name`)` is a REAL index named after one of its own columns): 53 phantom declarations in 22 files before the fix, 0 after. The fix is the ORDER — MySQL's name PRECEDES `ordered_columns`, the foreign key's referenced columns FOLLOW it. This mutant reverts the order test by republishing, for every unnamed constraint, the LAST direct identifier rather than the first one before the column list, which is the shape the pre-fix code read. Caught by sql/sqld15-pass3-adversarial, whose forbidSymbols name `d15_fk_ref` and `d15_fk_ref2` as `constant` under `d15_fk_src` and whose forbidRelationships name the containment edge that would follow one of them.

The relationship dedup key is (type, source, target) plus `metadata.memberKind`. A column and an index can share a name under one table - `CREATE TABLE t (scope_id int)` beside `CREATE INDEX scope_id ON t (...)` is legal, and phpMyAdmin writes `UNIQUE KEY `db_name` (`db_name`,`table_name`)` - so the two `contains` edges are DIFFERENT facts that a (type,source,target) key collapses to one, silently deleting the index's containment edge. Measured: 100 of 11,305 `contains` edges named two declarations that share a name AND an owner before `memberKind` joined the key. This mutant reverts the key by deleting `metadata.memberKind` from every `contains` edge, which both restores the collapse (the two edges become indistinguishable and one is dropped by the runner's own dedup) and removes the disambiguator a consumer needs. Caught by sql/sqld15-pass3-adversarial, whose expectRelationshipCount pins the same-name pairs at 2 edges and whose expectRelationships require `meta.memberKind` on both.

`contains` edges are emitted from TWO places: `createSymbol`, and explicit calls for the paths where `createSymbol` returns early without emitting. Both must carry `metadata.memberKind`, because the dedup key now includes it - and when only `createSymbol` carried it, EVERY ordinary containment edge was stored TWICE, once with the key and once without, which is the same defect as the mutant above pointed the other way. This mutant deletes `memberKind` from the edges that did NOT come from `createSymbol`, i.e. the ones whose payload lacks nothing else distinctive: it re-adds a second, unlabelled copy of every containment edge whose target is declared under a different owner than the edge source, which is the shape both emission sites produce. Caught by sql/sqld15-pass3-adversarial's `expectRelationshipCount` rows pinning ordinary containment at exactly 1 edge (`d15_plain -> d15_plain_id`, `d15_fk_src -> d15_fk_col`), which is the assertion a double-emission cannot pass.

`processDo` exists, its body is three real calls (`processQueryDependencies`, `processCalls`, `addPattern`), and it was UNREACHABLE: its only caller sat in `dispatchDeclaration`, which runs for `DECLARATION_NODES` only, and `do_statement` is not a declaration - it declares nothing. A source-derivation count of which relationship types an analyzer can construct would have counted `calls` from a DO block as constructible; it produced nothing. Measured on single statements: `DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM f(1); END $$;` published no `calls` edge, and `DO $$ BEGIN SELECT id FROM t; END $$;` published no `Anonymous Procedural Block` pattern. Settled corpus-wide by validation/m14/fixtures/sql/pass3-invocation-why.mts: 742 qualified invocations on the tree, 449 emitted as `calls` before this round. This mutant reads the analyzer's OWN `metadata.patterns`: the dead dispatch is exactly the absence of `"Anonymous Procedural Block"`, so the revert deletes every `calls` edge whose callee the file does not declare as a symbol - the set only the DO path produces, because every other `calls global -> X` path in the fixtures has X declared in the same file. No source scanning: a first version of this mutant scanned the text for `DO $`, and it SURVIVED, because the fixture's own comments quote `DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM f(1); END $$;` and the scanner matched the prose before the code. Caught by sql/sqld15-pass3-adversarial, whose three `calls global -> d15_do_*` rows and whose `calls` count of 4 all fail without the dispatch.

An `ALTER TABLE t ALTER COLUMN c SET DEFAULT app.f()` puts an `invocation` in a grammar-mandated expression slot and produced no edge: `alter_table` is neither a query nor a declaration, and `processAlterTable` returns early when the statement adds no column - which is exactly this shape. `hasura-engine/server/src-rsr/migrations/41_to_42.sql` writes `SET DEFAULT hdb_catalog.gen_hasura_uuid()` five times in one file. Of the 14 qualified invocations the corpus probe could not explain away before this round, 8 were this shape. This mutant deletes the `calls` edges whose SOURCE is a table the file also declares, which is the observable consequence of never reading the ALTER's expression slots - every `calls` edge with a table as its source comes from that path, because a table is not something any other route sources a call to. Character scans only, no regex: the table names come from the analyzer's OWN symbol list, not from re-parsing the `ALTER TABLE` text. Caught by sql/sqld15-pass3-adversarial, whose `calls d15_alter_target -> d15_alter_default` row fails without it.

`markDeclaration` and `createSymbol`'s identity key on a node's ABSOLUTE file position, `node.startIndex + state.slice.byteOffset`. Keyed on the raw `startIndex` - which is what the file did before this round - a declaration recovered from a re-parsed SLICE (the statement resync pass, or the EXECUTE-literal pass) collides with whatever the main pass already consumed at the same SLICE-LOCAL offset. Measured both ways: 161 intra-file duplicate symbols (identical kind, name and range emitted twice) across 10 corpus files before the fix and 0 after, which is the same defect seen from the other side; and the moment the dedup guard became load-bearing while the key was still slice-local, sql/sqld11 lost `quoted_name` - the table its `EXECUTE 'CREATE TABLE "quoted''name" ...'` literal declares. This mutant reverts the OBSERVABLE consequence: it deletes every symbol the file declares ONLY inside an `EXECUTE '...'` literal, which is exactly the set a slice-local key loses. Caught by sql/sqld11-execute-literal, whose `quoted_name` row is the pin.

`processStatement` calls `markDeclaration` and IGNORES the answer, so the declaration sweep — which walks every declaration in the tree, including the ones the root walk already dispatched — ran `dispatchDeclaration` a second time for every top-level declaration. Nothing in the graph doubled because `symbolKeys` and `relationshipsByKey` deduplicate, but the work did, and so did every counter once counters existed: one `ROW(1,2)::t` construction reported `instantiationsEmitted: 2` and one `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION f` pair reported `overridesEmitted: 3`, all from the same single edge. Reverted by re-publishing a symbol the analyzer emitted, keyed on its own name, kind, owner and line, so a file with any declaration at all gains a duplicate and the fixture symbol-count pins fail. Caught by sql/sqld13-ontology-types (`d13_replace_me` equals 2, `d13_only_once` equals 1) and by every symbol-count pin in the lane.

Every relationship this analyzer emits carries `metadata.evidenceClass`, and before this round NONE of them did: the 1,460-file census recorded `evidenceClass` absent on 22,022 of 22,022 edges, which reads as "no heuristics" and means "nothing recorded". The honesty contract's §4 requires the heuristic/deterministic ratio to be a queryable number, and an absent field cannot answer it. Reverted by stripping the field off every edge. Caught by sql/sqld13-ontology-types, whose expectRelationships pin `meta.evidenceClass` on an `imports`, an `overrides` and an `instantiates` row — three different tiers, so the mutant also proves the mapping is per-type rather than one constant.

`CREATE EXTENSION name` loads a separately DISTRIBUTED unit into the database and the file cannot mean anything without it. The analyzer recorded the declaration as a `module` symbol and emitted no edge, so over the 1,460-file census 27 declarations were 27 symbols with zero dependencies - the one construct where SQL genuinely has a cross-unit dependency, and the only place it was invisible. Reverted by dropping every edge the analyzer published for a `CREATE EXTENSION`, which is the faithful shape of the pre-round behaviour. Caught by sql/sqld13-ontology-types, whose expectRelationshipCount pins `imports` at 5 (3 psql includes + 2 extension installs) and whose two `sql_extension` expectImports rows have no other source.

The two `imports` mechanisms this lane emits answer different questions and a consumer that cannot tell them apart will read one as evidence about the other. A psql `\i`/`\ir` names a FILE IN THIS REPOSITORY, which is resolvable in principle; `CREATE EXTENSION` names a DISTRIBUTION THAT MUST BE INSTALLED, which can never bind to anything this repository contains. `metadata.fileDependency` and `metadata.external` are what separate them, and a revert that claims the extension is a file makes a graph consumer try to resolve `global->hstore` as a path. Reverted by rewriting the two flags on every extension edge. Caught by sql/sqld13-ontology-types, whose `d13_uuid_ossp` row pins `meta.external true` and `meta.fileDependency false`.

Relationship identity in this analyzer is type/source/target, so a name derived from the wrong node collapses every extension in a file onto one target - a file that installs `pgcrypto`, `postgis` and `uuid-ossp` would report one dependency and name it arbitrarily. This is the same shape-versus-role error the override rule hit when it keyed on a bare name (Hasura's `CREATE FUNCTION f` at line 7 against its `CREATE TRIGGER f` at line 25) and the same shape SQL-D7 ruled for column types: the discriminator has to be a grammar position, not a match. Reverted by retargeting every extension edge at the file's FIRST extension declaration. Caught by sql/sqld13-ontology-types, whose two extension rows name two different targets.

SQL attaches its WITH list to the STATEMENT, so a statement nested inside a cte body inherits that statement's CTEs and nothing else. `parseState.localCtes` is documented as holding exactly that scope and the main walk honours it, because `processRoot` populates it before dispatching; the declaration sweep is a SEPARATE walk with no such step, so it dispatched a cte body's `statement` with both the per-node and the file-level CTE set empty. The guard in `addTableEdge` is `localCtes.has(leaf) || state.localCtes.has(leaf)`, so an unqualified `FROM earlier_cte` inside a later cte's body was published as a TABLE edge. This was not theoretical: it was the single false positive the m12 differential reported against 84 hand-audited facts - `FP rel:Queries.sql:uses:global:recent_users`, precision 0.988 - and the outer SELECT's own reference to the same CTE was suppressed correctly by the same guard, which is why the file published exactly the one edge it should not have. Reverted by publishing a `uses` edge for every unqualified reference the sweep reaches inside a cte body whose name matches a CTE of the enclosing statement. Caught by sql/sqld5-quoted-and-cte, whose forbidRelationships name `d5_first` and whose sibling expect row names the qualified `d5_real` so a fix cannot pass by suppressing qualified references too.

A CTE's body is a `statement` NESTED INSIDE the `cte` node that declares its name, so every scope set built from `descendants(node, "cte")` or `descendants(enclosingStatement, "cte")` excludes it - the node that names the CTE is an ANCESTOR of the reference. PostgreSQL binds the name inside its own body (that is what makes `WITH RECURSIVE t AS (... FROM t ...)` work, and it binds without RECURSIVE too), so `FROM t` there is the CTE and publishing `uses global->t` names a table no file can declare. Measured on the corpus: duckdb/benchmark/recursive_cte/queries/performance/asql_cyk_using_key.sql, a 4-CTE recursive query whose body reads its own name. This is the sibling of sql/declaration-sweep-drops-the-cte-scope, same wrong output, different entry point, and the pass-1 fix could not have caught it. Reverted by publishing an edge for every unqualified `FROM <name>` whose name is the alias of a `WITH <name> AS` list item. Caught by sql/sqld14-pass2-adversarial, whose forbidRelationships name `d14_self`, `d14_inner` and `d14_outer` and whose forbidSymbols forbid the three names as declarations.

`evidenceClassFor` has three tiers and its `reference_qualified` arm reads `metadata.qualified`. `addTableEdge` has always passed it, but `evidenceClassFor`'s `Uses` arm hardcoded `usage_contextual` without looking, and `processCalls`, `processTrigger`'s action edge and `recordDml` passed NO metadata at all - so for `calls` the field was undefined on every edge and the tier was UNREACHABLE, and for `uses` it was present on the edge and ignored. A corpus probe found 46 qualified invocations and 1,406 `uses` edges carrying `qualified` in metadata, every one of them published as `usage_contextual`: the tier that means the name was read from a bare slot with nothing to disambiguate it. `app.users` names its schema. Reverted by stripping `qualified` from every relationship's metadata, which is exactly what the analyzer did for `calls` before pass 2. Caught by sql/sqld14-pass2-adversarial, whose expectRelationships pin `meta.qualified` and `meta.evidenceClass: reference_qualified` on a `calls` from a trigger action, a `uses` from a view body and a `uses` from a qualified INSERT.

`processIndex` hardcoded `parent: null` when it created the index symbol, so EVERY index symbol in the corpus had `ownerName: undefined` while the edge two lines below published `contains table -> index` naming the table as owner. `bb_graph`'s owner-cascade and `bb_impact`'s reverse walk both read `ownerName`, so the member read as an orphan that happened to be named in an edge. 70 containment edges in a 200-file corpus slice were in that state. Reverted by clearing `ownerName`/`ownerKind`/`parent` on every symbol whose metadata says it is an index. Caught by sql/sqld14-pass2-adversarial, whose expectSymbols pin `ownerName: d14_base` on an index declared after its table and `ownerName: d14_really_late` + `meta.ownerDeclaredLater: true` on one declared BEFORE it - the second is the case the immediate lookup cannot see and the end-of-analyze adoption pass exists for.

`state.redeclared` was keyed on the NAME alone while its own field comment claimed the caller "has established that both declarations are the same KIND" - which nothing did. Two DIFFERENT objects that share a name therefore collided, and pass 1 measured the collision: the construct probe counted 15 same-kind OR REPLACE redeclarations against the analyzer's 22 emitted `overrides` edges, and the 7-edge gap was this. The shape is hasura-engine/server/src-rsr/migrations/10_to_11.sql lines 7 and 25 - `CREATE FUNCTION hdb_catalog.f()` then `CREATE TRIGGER f`. Reverted by turning every `overrides` edge into one that also fires when no prior same-kind declaration exists, which the analyzer cannot express directly, so it is expressed the other way: any symbol name that appears under more than one kind in the file gets a synthetic `overrides` edge naming the LATER kind's line as the replacement. Caught by sql/sqld14-pass2-adversarial, whose forbidRelationships name `d14_twin` (a function and a view sharing one name) and whose expectRelationshipCount pins `overrides` at 1.

`retargetContainmentEdges` rewrites every `contains` target to the member's qualified name (`<file>::<owner>.<member>`), which is the only spelling the store's resolution pass 1 matches exactly (`parallel-indexer.ts:3773`, `target_external = _res_qname.qualified_name`; pass 2 needs a bare name unique in the project and pass 3 needs a dot). Measured at the 600-file population of `validation/m14/fixtures/sql/contains-fqn-probe.mts`, a bare member name is unique for 2,067 of 5,552 `contains` targets and ambiguous for 3,485 (62.8%) — so the revert does not lose edges, it makes 62.8% of them bind by a rule the store chose rather than by an exact match. This mutant strips the qualification back off every `contains` target, reproducing the pre-pass spelling. Caught by the lane's fixtures, whose `contains` targets are pinned qualified: sqld15's `expectRelationshipCount` rows stop matching, and sqld14's forbid rows stop forbidding.

The pre-fix FK test matched ANY `object_reference` child of a `column_definition`, so a user-defined column TYPE (also an object_reference) was indistinguishable from a `REFERENCES` target: `CREATE TABLE t (b my_schema.my_type)` published `references t -> my_type` and the "Foreign Key Constraints" pattern — one phantom FK per custom-typed column, measured corpus-wide. Simulated as a faithful REVERT of the fix: a column that declares a type and declares NO reference is exactly the case the fix corrected, so the pre-fix state is re-derived from the fixed result by giving that column a reference equal to the type's last segment, plus the edge and the pattern the pre-fix code added. Caught by sql/sqld1-column-types, whose forbidRelationships name `references d1_columns->my_type` and `-> my_schema`.

The pre-fix parameter-type accessor matched `keyword_*` before the type, and a parameter MODE is a keyword, so `IN a integer` published `{ name: "a", type: "IN" }` — the mode recorded as the type for every mode-prefixed argument. The fixed result carries the mode in `direction` and the real type in `type`, so the pre-fix state is re-derived by copying the mode into `type`. Caught by sql/sqld3-routine-signature, whose forbidParameters pin `types: ["IN","OUT","INOUT"]`.

The pre-fix trigger read the first three `object_reference`s ANYWHERE in the subtree, and a `WHEN (old.a <> new.a)` clause contributes two more (old/new are object_references in this grammar) — so `… WHEN (old.a <> new.a) EXECUTE FUNCTION audit_it()` published `calls tg->old`, a call edge into a PL/pgSQL pseudo-variable, instead of `calls tg->audit_it`. The fixed result carries the CORRECT actionFunction; the trigger's own source line is what distinguishes a WHEN-bearing trigger, and the harness passes the source for exactly this. Faithful revert: for a trigger whose statement contains a WHEN clause, set actionFunction to `old` and repoint the calls edge. Caught by sql/sqld2-trigger-when, whose forbidRelationships name `calls d2_when->old` and `-> new`.

The pre-fix code had no reserved-word guard, so error recovery turned SQL keywords and role names into graph nodes: 49 keyword-target edges measured over 441 corpus files — `calls global->USING`, `uses global->WITH`, `calls get_brand_network_stats->FILTER` — and from `REVOKE … FROM joe` a bare `uses global->joe`, a ROLE published as a table. With GRANT/REVOKE now parsing, the honest place to re-inject the pre-fix state is the construct that USED to be an ERROR: a REVOKE whose grantee the old code read out of a `from` clause. Faithful: for a source with `REVOKE … FROM <role>`, emit the `uses global-><role>` edge the pre-fix parser produced. Caught by sql/sqld4-statement-dispatch, whose forbidRelationships name `uses global->some_role`.

The pre-fix CTE guard matched on the BARE LEAF, so a QUALIFIED reference whose leaf collided with a CTE name was suppressed with it: `WITH a AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM a JOIN s.a ON true` emitted NO relationship at all — both of the file's edges vanished on a real table. The fixed result HAS the qualified edge (the pattern proves a CTE is in play); the pre-fix state is its absence. Faithful: drop the `uses` edge from global to any target, in a source that declares a CTE. Caught by sql/sqld5-quoted-and-cte, whose `uses global->d5_cte` expect row fails when the edge is gone.

The pre-fix range helper emitted 0-BASED columns. The engine's own ParseError range (engine.ts:1180) and every other analyzer that builds a range use `startPosition.column + 1`, so SQL was the only 0-based range in the tree and all four column fields of EVERY SQL symbol were off by one, corpus-wide. Simulated generically: every symbol's range and every relationship's site line loses the 1-based base. Caught by sql/sqld8-range-and-ids, whose expectSymbolRanges pin startColumn 3 / endColumn 5 for two columns.

The pre-fix `id` was `parentId ?? name`, so two top-level entities sharing a bare name collided: `CREATE TABLE a.t` and `CREATE TABLE b.t` both got id `t` (measured ids ["t","t"]). Duplicate ids silently drop nodes from id-keyed graph consumers and conflate two distinct declarations — the RSD3 class. Simulated generically: every top-level symbol's id is rewritten to its bare name, so same-named top-level declarations collide. Caught by sql/sqld8-range-and-ids, whose expectUniqueIds name `d8_samename` (three declarations, one bare name).

The pre-fix `COMMENT ON COLUMN t.c` published a dependency on the COLUMN. The grammar nests a qualified column reference's table as a CHILD object_reference (`object_reference "t.c" > object_reference "t" + identifier "c"`), so a flat identifier walk saw only `c` and resolved the reference to the column — measured on database/migrations/20260702_inventory_categories_nutrition_translations.sql, which published `uses global->calories` for `COMMENT ON COLUMN business_inventory_items.calories`. The first version of the FIX took parts[0] and edged the SCHEMA instead, which the fixture's forbid row catches; the ruled answer is the second-to-last segment. The edge carries `metadata.column` precisely so the pre-fix target is reconstructable from the result, and this mutant is that reconstruction: a documented-column edge retargeted to the column it documents. Caught by sql/sqld10-qualified-and-recovery, whose forbidRelationships name `references global->total`, `-> qty` and `-> app`.

The pre-fix ALTER reader took the FIRST `add_column` descendant, but the grammar gives each added column its own `add_column` SIBLING rather than one comma list — so `ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN a int, ADD COLUMN b text, ADD COLUMN c numeric(6,2)` published `a` and dropped `b` and `c`. Measured on the corpus: a five-column `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` migration published one of its five. Simulated as a revert: keep only the FIRST added column of each table and drop the rest, which is exactly the pre-fix output. Caught by sql/sqld10-qualified-and-recovery, whose expectSymbols and expectSymbolCount name all three added columns.

The pre-fix analyzer returned `errors: []` UNCONDITIONALLY, so a file it could not parse at all read as a clean 0 symbols / 0 relationships / 0 errors. Every gate that calls `analyzer.analyze` directly — the fixture lane, this mutation harness, the m12 differential — saw a successful analysis of a total failure, and the m12 differential's error channel was vacuous for sql. Simulated generically: the analyzer's own `errors` array is emptied, keeping the result otherwise identical. Caught by sql/sqld7-error-honesty, whose expectErrors pin a warning and whose expectSymbols pin the declarations that survive beside the damaged lines — a suppression fix passes the first and fails nothing, so the second is what stops over-correction.

The pre-fix `statement` branch forwarded only `isDeclaration()` types and otherwise tested the children for a query shape, then RETURNED — so a statement holding anything else never reached the switch below it. Measured dead arms: set_statement, reset_statement and comment_statement (all three ARE produced by the pinned grammar, so "Session Configuration" and "SQL Documentation" could never fire), and merge/truncate, whose grammar rules are HIDDEN so the keywords inline into `statement` and an arm keyed on the node type can never run. Simulated generically: the patterns and edges those arms are the sole producers of are removed, and the merge/truncate/grant edges go with them. Caught by sql/sqld4-statement-dispatch, whose expectPatterns name all five.

A regression of the EXECUTE-literal pass: the analyzer only ever read declarations the PARSER handed it, so DDL a migration hands to the database as a string — `EXECUTE 'CREATE TRIGGER …'`, the dominant shape in PostgreSQL extension files — was invisible. Measured on 387 extension files the pass is worth +156 symbols and +234 relationships, and the pass reports itself in `ambiguity.executeLiterals` / `executeRecovered`. Simulated generically: everything the pass contributed is removed, keeping the main pass and the resync exactly as they are. Caught by sql/sqld11-execute-literal, whose source wraps a declaration in an EXECUTE literal and whose expectSymbols name it.

The EXECUTE-literal scanner without its comment guard. A migration that disables DDL leaves the text behind: `-- EXECUTE 'CREATE TABLE ghost (id int);'` and the same inside `/* … */`. Without skipping comments the scanner treats both as live and the analyzer publishes tables that do not exist. This is the pass's only false-positive path and it is invisible to any check that asks 'did it find the right things' — the finding is a symptom, not the defect. Simulated generically: a symbol whose own source text sits inside a comment is returned, which is what a comment-blind scanner produces. Caught by sql/sqld11-execute-literal, whose source contains both a commented-out and a live EXECUTE literal and whose expectSymbols require the ghost to be absent.

ERROR RECOVERY: the walk STOPS at the first recovery node. Nothing counts symbols-per-file against a floor, so a silently half-analysed document reads as analysed — and the module symbol spans the whole root, so a truncated document still has an identity and every visible count stays plausible. Svelte makes it sharper than html: an unclosed `{#if}` does not clip the damage to the broken line, the parser's ERROR span swallows the REST OF THE FILE, so the tail is valid markup inside the error region. Measured on the real corpus, 2.44% of files carry recovery nodes, and when one does what follows is usually good content — a stopping walk discards the majority of a damaged document. Modelled by dropping every relationship and symbol at or after the FIRST reported error, reading the analyzer's own diagnostic rather than the engine's so the mutated result still looks correctly reported. Caught by svelte/error-recovery, whose `Beta` at L12 and `uses shared` at L12 sit after the error and inside its span.

D12 obligation 1 of 2: the MEMBER-READ carriers are dropped. `bind:`, `class:` and `style:` each read a component member in the template, which is the S1 case, and every one was silent before the ruling — roughly 1,857 corpus occurrences including `bind:value` at 581, the most common attribute interaction in the corpus. Removing them drops the component's primary data-flow surface while the document still looks analysed. Selective on the `carrierDirective` provenance flag rather than on a blanket `uses` filter: a blanket drop is caught by a dozen unrelated fixtures and would prove nothing about D12, and the first version of this mutant used a `metadata.context` marker that only the CALL edges carry, so it SURVIVED. Caught by svelte/directive-carriers.

D12 obligation 2 of 2: the FRAMEWORK-INVOKED carriers are dropped. `use:`, `transition:`, `in:`, `out:` and `animate:` are call sites on exactly the argument that made `on:click` one under D8 — Svelte calls an action on mount and a transition on state change by the same mechanism. Their silence was an internal inconsistency rather than a position, and the mutant restores it. Selective by metadata marker so the `on:` handler edges survive and a failure is attributable to this family rather than to the D8 pass. Caught by svelte/directive-carriers.

D7: rune invocations are dropped. A named function handed to a rune that INVOKES its argument ($effect, $effect.pre, $effect.root, $effect.untracked, $derived.by, $host) is a call site, so a component that runs `fn` on every effect tick must say so in its graph — before the ruling these six forms emitted nothing, because the delegate suppresses the rune and the argument is an ordinary identifier no edge was made for. Selective rather than blanket: a blanket 'drop every calls edge' would be caught by any fixture and would prove nothing about D7. Only edges carrying the rune-pass marker are removed, so the js-delegate call inside `$effect(inlineCall())` and the D8 template-handler call both survive, which is what makes a failure attributable to the ruling rather than to the delegate. Caught by svelte/rune-invocations.

2026-10-23 — THE PRE-MIGRATION STATE: every SFC template render goes back to `instantiates`. The extended value `renders` is the honest relation for a component tag — the source contains no `new`, so `instantiates` claimed an allocation site the file does not have (types.ts' Renders contract: NOT `instantiates`). The transform is selective on the SFC provenance marker: `isComponentUsage` is written ONLY by the three template emission sites, so the JS/TS delegate's script `new` rows (the rows `instantiates` KEEPS) survive untouched and a failure is attributable to the render relation rather than to the seam. Caught by svelte/renders-component-tags, which forbids `instantiates Card/Widget/Panel.Root` — the negative of the same both-directions pin, so a migration that renames both sides or neither is caught rather than only one.

F27 (2026-10-12) regression, BOTH halves of the family in one revert because they are one defect: the walker loses the positional object-key rule AND the spread clause of the receiver rule. Pre-fix, a written property KEY was published as a member read (`{{ month: "january" }}` emitted `uses -> month`, measured at 49 edges over 38 of 6,439 corpus files, the worst of them RESOLVING because chart-pie-stacked.svelte declares `{#snippet tooltip()}` and published `uses -> tooltip` off a Recharts config key) and a SPREAD argument was suppressed (`[...list]` published nothing for `list`) because the token before the name is a dot. Reverted from the SOURCE, since both halves are absences or presences a result transform must reconstruct: every identifier followed by `:` inside a brace on a template line regains a `uses` row at its own line (skipping one that already exists), and every identifier after `...` loses its component-sourced template read. The ternary half is deliberately NOT reverted — the fixture's `cond`/`alpha`/`beta` rows are reads under both revisions, so a revert of them would be a second defect rather than this one. MEASURED catch set, not the intended one: `svelte/object-key-not-a-read` (its `month` forbid row and its `list` expect row), PLUS `svelte/declaration-tag-shadow` and `svelte/template-attr-shapes` — the key scan follows `word:` inside any brace on a template line, which is coarser than the analyzer's innermost-bracket rule, so it re-adds keys in two other fixtures. Recorded because a mutant whose description claims a narrower catch than it has is the same species of overstatement this registry exists to prevent.

F29 (2026-10-12) regression: the graph dedupe drops a losing row silently again, so a template read that collided with a script read of the same member leaves no trace on the surviving edge. Pre-fix, the survivor carried the script's line and the script's 0.6 confidence with no marker — measured on the 3,085 corpus files where an independent oracle's shadow model is provably equivalent to this analyzer's (no `{#each}`, `{#await}`, `{#snippet}` or `{@const}` anywhere in the file): 384 of 5,781 template reads, 6.6%, every one with a script twin, and a consumer could not tell the member is ALSO read by the template. This is a RESULT transform rather than a source-derived revert, and deliberately so: the dropped row is an ABSENCE on the survivor (a key the pre-fix tree simply did not write), so removing the keys reproduces the pre-fix payload EXACTLY — edge count, target, line_number and confidence all unchanged, which is the fixture's own contract. It scopes itself to non-template survivors: a row that IS a template read keeps `templateReadSites`, because a mutant that also stripped those would be reverting `template-read-collapse`'s green pin (a second defect, not this one).

F28 (2026-10-12) regression: a template BINDING PATTERN goes back to being a flat word list, so its READ positions publish nothing again. Pre-fix, every site that writes a pattern — `{#each … as …}`, `{#await … then …}`, `{:catch …}`, `{#snippet name(…)}`, `{let …}` / `{@const …}` heads — handed its text to `collectShadowNames`, which put EVERY word in the shadow set: the computed key `[firstString]` and the default `c = count` were never published (27 of the 35 template reads the grammar-derived oracle named over 6,439 corpus files, at 81 sites carrying a computed key or a default), and a PROPERTY name like `a` in `{ a: b }` was registered as a template-local, silencing a real member read of `a` for the whole block. Reverted from the SOURCE and expressed as a DELETION, because the pre-fix defect on the read side is an ABSENCE and no result transform can restore a suppression: the mutant re-derives the fix's read positions from the template text — the identifiers inside a computed key's `[ … ]` and the identifiers inside a default value's `= …`, on each line that carries a pattern head — and drops those names' `uses` rows. It therefore reproduces the LOST-READ half only; the FALSE-SHADOW half (a sibling read that the pre-fix shadow silenced) is pinned by the fixture's `firstProp`/`idx`/`value`/`bound` forbid rows instead, and that asymmetry is recorded here rather than implied. MEASURED catch set: `svelte/pattern-reads`, on its seven expect rows (`count`, `default_arg`, `firstString`, `labelKey`, `th`, `defaultHeight`, `pick`).

F26 (2026-10-12) regression: a Svelte 5.36 declaration tag stops BINDING again — `{let counter = …}` / `{const doubler = …}` is treated as an ordinary mustache, so the declared name is published as a component-member read of a declaration that shadows it. Reverted from the SOURCE, because the defect is the PRESENCE of a row the fix removed: every `let`/`const` tag's bound name (the head's identifiers, keyword excluded) becomes a component-sourced `uses` row at the tag's own line, skipping a name that already has one. The mutant reproduces the FABRICATION half only: the other half of the pre-fix state — that no shadow was registered, so a LATER sibling using the name still resolved to a member — cannot be restored by a result transform, because a suppressed read is absent from the output it would have polluted. That half is pinned by the fixture as an expect row on lines 45/46 instead, and it is recorded here rather than implied. Caught by svelte/declaration-tag-shadow's `uses -> doubler` forbid row.

F25 (2026-10-12) regression: a keyed `{#each}` block's KEY expression stops being a read again, which is the pre-fix state — `{#each rows as row (keyOf(row))}` published `uses rows` for the collection on the same line and NOTHING for `keyOf`, and `{#each rows as row (sortKey)}` published nothing for `sortKey`. The clause is located on one line, which every site of the fixture is; the corpus's 699 occurrences over 486 files were not re-measured for the multiline form, and a clause spanning lines is NOT reverted by this transform — recorded rather than implied, because a mutant that silently covers less than it claims is worse than a narrow one that says so. Caught by svelte/keyed-each-key-reads' `keyOf` and `sortKey` rows.

That asymmetry is the pre-fix state and it is why the fixture pins both: `{@render row(alpha)}` published `calls -> row` and not one `uses`. F23 (2026-10-12) regression: an event handler's own ARROW PARAMETERS go back to being published as component members. The pre-fix state is the presence of rows the fix removed, so it is re-derived from the SOURCE the way the walk produced it — for each `on:`/`onclick` carrier whose value is an arrow, the parameters written at its head become `uses` rows from the component at the handler's line. The analyzer's OWN recovery diagnostic is dropped, leaving the engine to report alone. The error-recovery contract is REPORTED / BYPASSED / KEEP PUBLISHING, and before this the toml analyzer pushed no diagnostics at all, so the reported half was entirely the engine's reached through a caller — a contract resting on someone else's completeness. The mutant removes only the analyzer-authored message, so the engine's `Syntax error (...)` survives and a fixture that merely counted errors would still pass; the fixture pins the analyzer's message verbatim, so this is caught. This is the mirror of the svelte lane's `namedChild` blindness: there the analyzer walked too few nodes, here it contributed nothing at all.

ERROR RECOVERY: the recovery region is turned into a SYMBOL. `ERROR` and `MISSING` are DIAGNOSTICS, not document constructs — they exist only where the parser could not read the source, and a node named after one joins to nothing a consumer can navigate to, which is the unresolvable-identity class reached through a malformed file rather than a missing edge. The companion half of the contract ("the region is REPORTED") is the engine's job — the toml analyzer pushes no errors of its own, so a mutation of analyzer output cannot remove a diagnostic; the fixture pins both and the mutant covers the half a mutant can reach. The fixture also pins what matters most and is easiest to get wrong: a walk that STOPPED at the recovery node would publish `t` and `t.before` and nothing after, and the document would still look analysed because its module is present. Caught by toml/malformed-and-rejected.

BARE-WRITABILITY, NOT PUNCTUATION: a path segment is quoted only when it contains `.`, `"` or `\`, so a segment that CANNOT be written bare is emitted bare. `[target."cfg(unix)".dependencies]` is real cargo syntax and `cfg(unix)` contains PARENTHESES — no punctuation the character test looks for — so the name came out `target.cfg(unix).dependencies`, which is not a spelling TOML can parse back. The same hole let a segment containing a SPACE through. Found by the differential oracle on cargo's own Cargo.toml, which is the argument for deriving the rule from the specification ("may this be written bare?") rather than from the characters that appear in the sample you happened to test. Caught by toml/dotted-and-quoted-paths.

ONE FUNCTION OWNS A PATH'S SPELLING: the ancestor lookup deciding which DECLARED table owns a section builds prefixes from RAW segments, while the declared-path table is keyed by the QUOTED spelling, so `target.cfg(unix).dependencies` never matches `target."cfg(unix)".dependencies` and a declared ancestor is reported as implied. The section is then filed under the MODULE. The symbol's NAME stays correct — the emit path does quote — so only the CONTAINMENT is wrong, which is why no symbol assertion could see it and why the fixture pins the edge's SOURCE. On cargo's Cargo.toml, `[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies.windows-sys]` was filed under the module rather than the parent declared three lines earlier. Caught by toml/dotted-and-quoted-paths.

TOML-IDENTITY: a symbol's name becomes its LAST SEGMENT instead of its full dotted path, so `[workspace.lints.rust]` is `rust` and `package.name` is `name`. The first manifest anyone writes collides — cargo's own has a key named `name` under `[package]` AND under every `[[bin]]` — so the flattened names are not unique and a `contains` edge naming `name` resolves to two nodes. The full path is what makes a file's names unique without a synthetic suffix on every collision. Caught by toml/identity-and-paths.

TOML-IDENTITY: a quoted key segment is joined like a bare one, so a segment containing a dot loses its quotes. Inside `[t]`, `a.b.c` and `"a.b".c` are DIFFERENT TOML keys — three nested tables versus a table literally named `a.b` — and both assemble to `t.a.b.c`, after which the dedupe invents `t.a.b.c#2` and asserts the document declared one key twice when it declared two distinct ones. That is the unresolvable-identity class arriving through the NAMING SCHEME rather than through a missing edge, and re-quoting is TOML's own disambiguation, not an invented escape. Caught by toml/identity-and-paths, which writes all three spellings side by side.

IDENTITY: the module does not own its name in its own file, so a table may take the file's stem. `doc/book/book.toml` declares `[book]`, and relationships address nodes by NAME, so every `contains` edge naming `book` resolves to two nodes. The module's identity comes from its PATH and is not negotiable. This is html's precedence exactly (its `usedNames` starts `{ [moduleName]: 1 }`), and the rule was found by the CORPUS rather than by a fixture: 2 collisions in 684 cargo files, both `<stem>.toml` containing `[<stem>]`. Caught by toml/module-name-collision.

IMPLIED PARENTS: `[workspace.lints.rust]` invents symbols for `workspace` and `workspace.lints`, which the file never declares. The ruling is that they are RECORDED in `metadata.impliedParents` precisely because fabricating a table is a guess dressed as a fact — the graph would claim the document contains headers it does not, and a consumer diffing a config against its graph would see phantom entries. Caught by toml/identity-and-paths's forbidSymbols.

INLINE-TABLE SCOPING: an inline table's keys become symbols of the file. The ruling is that they are part of ONE value expression — `x = { a = 1 }` makes `x` the symbol — and a manifest with 200 dependencies written as `{ version = "...", features = [...] }` would publish 600+ symbols naming nothing a consumer can navigate to alone. Their names are recorded on the key in `metadata.inlineKeys`, so this mutant loses information as well as adding noise. Caught by toml/arrays-and-values.

R12 regression: a parameter stops shadowing a same-named file-level symbol, so the reference pass resolves the body read to the wrong declaration. With `interface Deps { root: string }` in the file, `function f(root: string) { return root }` publishes `f->root` again — the graph recording a function as referencing an interface property it never touches, purely because its own parameter had that name. The pass resolves by NAME, and it already suppressed locally-bound names through `locals` (destructuring patterns and local declarators); a parameter was simply missing, and the fix belongs at the references guard rather than in `locals` because `locals` also gates the `uses` edge, where an edge to a parameter is wanted (interp-uses pins `greet -> name`). The transform re-adds a `references` edge from every symbol to any of its own parameter names that also exists as a file-level symbol — the exact pre-fix shape. parameter-shadows-file-symbol kills it, and its positive pins (`usesConst -> root`, `callsHelper -> helper`, `annotates -> Deps`) are what stop a fix that over-suppresses from passing.

R11 regression: CommonJS `require()` stops being a module dependency, and the module loader starts being published as a call instead — the two halves of the same construct, which is why the twin skips the bare `require` callee while still recording the dependency. The transform drops every `imports` edge carrying `meta.isRequire` and re-publishes each as a `calls` edge to a function named `require`, which is what the analyzer did before the port. It covers all four require spellings at once — the plain call, a destructuring binding, a bare-identifier binding, and TypeScript's `import m = require("m")` whose path lives in an `import_require_clause` rather than the statement's `source` field — because the last one is the shape most likely to regress silently: reading only the `source` field skips it with no error. `imports` is the second-largest edge class in this lane (2,692 edges over 600 tracked files) so a silently missing dependency is a hole in impact analysis. commonjs-require-module-graph kills it, including the exact-count pins that separate a legitimate member call named `require` from a spurious one.

R10 regression: a declaration inside a function body inherits the enclosing class or namespace as its owner again, so `contains Report->helper` — the graph claims the class has a member that belongs to a closure inside one of its methods. Two causes, both restored by re-attributing every ownerless declaration to the file's containers: the eager scope pop in extractClass/extractInterface/extractEnum, and `getOwnerInfo()` being asked about lexical nesting that an accumulating resource stack cannot answer. The transform adds a containment edge from every container to every ownerless function/type/interface symbol, which is the observable shape of the pre-fix output; the lane's new independent contains oracle is the instrument that found it (8 false edges over 200 files of an external corpus). declaration-in-body-is-local kills it on the forbidRelationships pins, and its positives — three ordered members, and a body-local type alias still containing its own members — are what stop a fix that simply suppressed ownership from passing.

R8 regression: bodyless function DECLARATIONS stop emitting. `declare function f(): T` parses to `function_signature`, not `function_declaration`, and the pre-fix analyzer had no reference to that node type at all — while the spec listed it as handled_verified and the coverage gate was satisfied by a fixture that merely PARSED one. Every exported function in a .d.ts was therefore invisible: no symbol, no call edge, no complexity, no api-contract row. The transform reproduces that by dropping every function symbol that is marked as an ambient declaration, and it also clears the flag itself, because pre-fix nothing could have set it (the `declare` keyword is not a child of the node; it sits on a wrapping ambient_declaration). ambient-function-signature kills it.

R7 regression: an object-literal get/set pair stops collapsing to one property. The fix keeps the LAST accessor of a pair; the defect emitted one symbol per accessor, and because containment emits one `contains` row per member symbol, the same edge appeared twice. This transform reconstructs that output by giving every object-literal PROPERTY member a second declaration — the observable shape of the pre-fix analyzer. It cannot read the AST, so it cannot know which properties were accessor pairs, and it therefore over-applies: the point is that object-literal-accessor-pair's exact-count pin (contains o->size equals 1) MUST fail, which is the only assertion in the suite that can fail on a duplicate at all, since expectSymbols is a >=1 match and passes happily with both symbols present.

Restores the pre-fix signal scan, which read child_process only off an import_statement or an `import ... = require(...)` clause. A CommonJS `require("child_process")` — a CALL, not an import — no longer arms the rule, so a bare exec-family call in such a file loses its command_injection sink and no flow into it can be reported: the false NEGATIVE direction, which costs a real vulnerability rather than adding noise. taint-sink-require-child-process kills it (a bare execFileSync whose only evidence is the require form). The transform is the exact inverse of the fix: a bare exec-family sink is kept when the file's import list already proves child_process, and stripped when the ONLY evidence was the call.

H1 regression: restores bare-name/bare-LEAF sink matching — RegExp.prototype.exec, a project-local execute() and the project's own spawn() are reported as command_injection / sql_injection again, and because the store multiplies sources by sinks, one req.body read beside any .exec() manufactures a persisted command-injection flow. taint-sink-receiver kills it on the notIncludesVuln pins (the exact-snippet pins cannot catch a rebuilt snippet, which is why the vulnerability_type pins are in the fixture)

M4 regression: an anonymous default export emits an `exports` edge to `default` again — a target no symbol in this or any other file can own; arrow-contracts-and-exports forbidRelationships kills it

M3 regression, the dangerous half: removes the per-function REBINDING while keeping the boundary removal — the payload walk started at a symbol and charged every call below it to that symbol, so a nested function's or object-literal method's calls were ALSO listed on the enclosing symbol (enclosing lists helper besides inner; mixed lists persist besides save). qualified-calls-nested-scope kills it on the notIncludes pins, which is the only shape that can tell 'omitted' from 'double-counted'

M7 regression: restores the bare-name-only builtin table — node:fs/promises, node:test, stream/promises and every other subpath Node ships resolve to external:<specifier> again, so the index claims npm packages named 'fs/promises' and 'test' (node-builtin-subpaths meta.resolvedPath pins catch it; lodash/merge stays external in both, so the pin set cannot be satisfied by classifying everything external)

R15 (243dc36f) regression: an arrow function's parameters stop shadowing a same-named file-level symbol, so a read inside the arrow resolves by NAME to the unrelated module declaration. `function f(bbEntry: string) { return (root) => root() }` republishes `references f->root` against a module-level `function root()`. It fell through R12 and R13 for a structural reason: an arrow is not a named declaration, so the reference pass never rebinds its current symbol when it descends into one, and the ENCLOSING function stays current — whose parameter list is a different one (`bbEntry`), so the shadow set was well-formed and simply lacked the name. Measured at the time: 227 false `references` over 1000 tracked files in 66 of them, the largest of the three shadowing defects. The transform re-adds a `references` edge from every symbol to any file-level symbol whose name equals one of the symbol's own parameters, which is the pre-fix arrow shape because the arrow's parameters never reached the shadow set. The fixture's `shadowDoesNotLeak -> file` expectation is the pin that keeps the fix scoped.

PRE-FIX: `Public Sub New()` has no `name` field -- the grammar lexes `New` as an anonymous token -- so `declaredName` returned empty and the 'declaration without a name' guard RETURNED before the naming contract was reached. The contract existed and was dead code: 12,549 symbols across 435 files contained ZERO constructors. Simulated as a faithful revert by dropping every Constructor symbol and the containment edge into it, which is exactly the state that guard produced. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects two `constructor` symbols and two `contains -> constructor` edges.

PRE-FIX: containment was emitted per visitor, and the visitors for nested TYPES emitted none. A nested type therefore carried `ownerName` on its symbol and NO `contains` edge into it -- the owner recorded and then unreachable, so containment navigation stopped at the enclosing class. Found by the F5 differential and not by a fixture: 48 `contains Namespace -> Class` rows and every nested-type edge were invisible to a symbol count. Simulated as a faithful revert by dropping the `contains` edge into any type whose owner is itself a symbol of this file, which is precisely the set the per-visitor dispatch failed to cover. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects `contains Box -> Kind` and the enum members under it.

PRE-FIX: a construction IS a call, and the grammar spells it with one of TWO node types -- `New Box()` is an `invocation_expression`, but `New Box(1, 2)` is an `array_creation_expression` with a `type` field and no `function` field. Keying on the invocation alone dropped every call edge for a construction WITH ARGUMENTS: 15,577 occurrences across 1,718 of the corpus's 2,660 files. Recorded for a second reason: the F5 differential reported 100 % WITH THIS DEFECT PRESENT, because the oracle keyed on `invocation_expression` too. Two implementations that share an assumption are one implementation with a witness -- divergence has to cover the assumptions, not only the traversal. Simulated as a faithful revert by dropping every `calls` edge the analyzer itself marked `constructed` with a node type other than `object_creation_expression`, read off the edge's own metadata so the mutant cannot silently stop matching when the fixture changes. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects `calls Build -> Box` at line 55.

PRE-FIX: `interface_method_declaration`, `interface_property_declaration` and `interface_event_declaration` were in NEITHER DECLARATION_NODES nor SILENT_INTERNAL, which is the whole defect -- nothing visited them, so every interface was published as an EMPTY SHELL with a name and no members, while the class implementing it had all of them. Found by the F8 node-type census, which counted 146 distinct named node types in the corpus against 42 classified: the `every construct is accounted for` claim was 29% true and nothing had measured it. Simulated as a faithful revert by dropping interface-owned members. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects `IMeasurable` to own `Area` and `Label`.

PRE-FIX: NO OPERATOR WAS EVER PUBLISHED, for two independent reasons. `operator_declaration` has no `name` field -- the operator is an anonymous token -- so the same empty-name guard that hid constructors hid every operator; and `visitOperator` then skipped that very token because `isKeyword` returns true for any token not starting with a letter, which was meant to reject `(` but also rejected every operator SYMBOL. Word operators (`Operator CType`) fail a second time: the keyword and the word are inlined away and exist nowhere in the tree, so there is no node to name from. Found by the F8 census, which found `operator_declaration` classified as a declaration while the walker never produced one. Simulated as a faithful revert by dropping symbols named by the operator contract literal. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects an `operator` symbol owned by `Square` and its containment edge.

PRE-FIX: `modifierNames` read `childForFieldName("modifiers")`, which returns ONE node — and this grammar emits the field REPEATEDLY, once per modifier. `Public Overrides Sub` is `modifiers: (...) modifiers: (...)`, so the read returned `public` and dropped `overrides` silently. Every modifier-dependent fact was wrong wherever the modifier was not written first: `Public Shared Sub` reported isStatic=false, `Public Overrides` published ZERO overrides edges across 435 files, and `Const` fields were published as Variables, with `MustOverride`, `ReadOnly` and `NotInheritable` missed the same way. VB writes `Public` first by convention, so the one modifier that was ever read was the one least worth reading. Found because the documentation claimed `overrides` was published and it was not. Simulated as a faithful revert: drop the modifiers that are not the first, which is exactly what the singular read did. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, whose `MaxDepth` is a `constant` and not a `variable`, and whose `Size`/`Reset` carry `Overridable`.

PRE-FIX: `Private _watcher As New Timers.Timer()` puts an `array_type` in `declared_type` -- the `()` reads as bounds -- and the naming helper had no case for that wrapper, so the field published `references _watcher -> "Timers.Timer()"`: the whole expression, parens included. Not a name in the file, not navigable, and unmatchable by any independent oracle. Found by auditing `references`, the label that had been 37% of the index and agreed with by no second implementation. Reverted from the SOURCE rather than a hardcoded string, because the pre-fix target is the grammar node's own text and the fixed result no longer carries it; reading the `As New T(...)` the fixture actually contains is also what keeps this from silently ceasing to match when the fixture changes.

PRE-FIX SHAPE, not a pre-fix absence: the `overrides` edge named the base member by its bare name, so `Public Overrides Property Size` published `overrides Size -> Size` — a SELF-EDGE. A self-edge is not navigable and cannot answer the only question anyone asks of it, "what does this override?"; the same un-navigable shape the member-level `implements` edge had before it was qualified to `IThing.Refresh`. Simulated by stripping the base-type qualifier from the target, which is the pre-fix string exactly. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects `overrides Size -> Square.Size` and forbids `overrides Size -> Size`.

PRE-FIX: `visitHeritage` was called from exactly one place -- the TYPE visitor -- so a member's own `Implements IThing.Refresh` clause was never read and the whole member-level heritage form published nothing, on every member in the language. Found by the FULL-CORPUS sweep, not by a fixture: 17 of 23 missing rows on a 483-file draw, and every one of them read as a self-edge (`implements Initialize -> Initialize`) because a member that implements `IThing.Refresh` is NAMED `Refresh` -- so last-segment reduction collapses the edge onto itself. Simulated as a faithful revert by dropping `implements`/`extends` edges whose metadata records the member heritage form. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects `implements Draw -> IShape.Draw` and forbids `implements Draw -> Draw`.
