F12 regression, THIRD path: the OPTIONS-API hoist stops resolving — `props: optionProps` / `emits: optionEmits` naming a declaration declared in the same file go back to extracting nothing. Distinct from vue/named-contract-drop, which reverts the script-setup binding only: both were broken by the same shape (Vue hoists the contract to a const in either style) and both need their own mutant, or a fixture that pins one half leaves the other unpinned. Caught by vue/options-named-contract's four component-owned symbol rows and their four contains rows.

F1 regression: Options-API INHERITANCE stops producing a relationship, so `extends:`/`mixins:` are invisible again and the base component falls back to the bare `uses` a name mention earns — the exact pre-fix state, where the SAME text as a .ts file emitted a real `extends` and vue emitted none. Caught by vue/options-inheritance's three `extends` rows. Distinct from vue/mixin-label-swap: one mutant reverting both would pass if either half were pinned, which is the M49 T6 lesson.

F1 regression, the DISTINCTION half: every heritage row is labelled `isMixin: true`, so `extends: BasePanel` (class inheritance) and `mixins: [M1]` (an options merge) become indistinguishable in the payload. Caught ONLY by the negative rows in vue/options-inheritance, which pin isMixin:false on the `extends` row — a fixture that pinned only presence would pass this mutant unchanged. This is the vue-side twin of the family's same-shape defect (a label computed from a substring rather than the construct).

F10 regression: an unquoted object-literal KEY reads as a component member again — `{{ { count: 1 } }}` emits Uses(count) when nothing in that expression reads the member. Measured at 432 of the 1,150 restored corpus files. Caught by vue/template-object-key's two forbid rows; the fixture declares no `count` and no `label` in its data, so any Uses of either there can only be the defect.

F10's TRAP, and the reason the fix tracks a pending `?` per brace depth: the naive key rule — an identifier followed by a colon is a key — deletes the VALUE side of every ternary. In `show ? count : total` the `count` is what the `?` selected and the colon is the ternary's own. Caught ONLY by vue/template-ternary-value, whose every row is a require; vue/template-object-key's forbid rows would score this mutant as a clean pass, which is precisely why the two halves are separate fixtures. This mutant is the FALSE NEGATIVE the F10 fix exists to avoid, and it is silent: fewer edges, no error, every gate that forbids rather than requires still green.

F6 regression: the bracket-led-key guard is removed from the three sites that lacked it, so `[dyn]` survives as a symbol name from a computed data key, a computed props/emits key, and an index signature inside an inline type literal — names no graph can resolve, and ones the store's name+line key can DISPLACE a real member with. Caught by vue/computed-key-guard's two forbid rows. The controls (plain / plainProp / save / plainInline) are what make the guard POSITIONAL rather than bracket-wide: an implementation that skipped the whole `[...]` would pass a fixture that only forbade the bad names.

F5 regression: the Options `setup` symbol is removed, so a component whose whole body is `setup(props) { return { … } }` loses the only symbol that names its entry point — 21 corpus files produce a graph with no way in. Caught by vue/options-setup-method. That fixture also expects `mounted`, so this mutant cannot be satisfied by emitting the wrong thing: the fix has to ADD setup without disturbing the lifecycle branch it deliberately does not share a predicate with.

F9(a) regression: a namespaced builtin tag is reported as a component usage. tree-sitter-vue spells `<svg:circle/>` in full and neither builtin set contains a colon, so the pre-fix analyzer published `instantiates -> svg:circle` — a target no components registry holds. Caught by vue/tag-namespace-and-dotted. The mutation is synthesized rather than reverted, because after the fix the bad row is absent from the result and there is nothing to un-do; the honest simulation of "the namespace check did not run" is to emit the row it would have emitted. The fixture's FORBID rows also carry `svg`, `math` and `math:mi`, so an implementation that suppressed only the exact strings it knew would still be caught.

F9(b) regression: the leaf of a dotted tag is dropped. The grammar's `tag_name` spells only the root segment, so reading it alone — the pre-fix behaviour — made `<Form.Input/>` record `instantiates -> Form` and lose `.Input`; the graph then claimed the whole component for a template that uses one sub-component. Caught by vue/tag-namespace-and-dotted, whose expected rows require `member`. Note this mutant cannot be satisfied by pointing the target at `Form.Input` instead: the fixture FORBIDS that name, because the components registry holds `Form` and a resolver must be able to match it — the leaf belongs in metadata, which is what this mutant deletes.

F3 regression: the `withDefaults` defaults are dropped again. The macro handler visits the inner `defineProps` call and never looked one frame up at the withDefaults wrapping it, so `withDefaults(defineProps<T>(), { … })` — the documented way to give a typed prop a default — silently lost every default; measured on 98 corpus files, all of which use the NAMED form. BOTH paths are reverted in one mutant on purpose: a fixture that only pinned the per-prop `defaultValue` would be satisfied by a fix that wired the symbol path and skipped the edge, which is precisely the fix that would have looked in one piece and changed nothing on the real corpus. The fixture asserts `defaultKeys` (a count) as well as `defaultValue`, so neither path can be the only one checked.

F13 regression: the IDENTIFIER elements of a `defineProps([…])` / `defineEmits([…])` array stop producing contract edges. `propEntries` accepts string elements only, which is right — an identifier is a declaration, not an event name, and a symbol for it would be the F6 phantom class again — but DROPPING it was worse than either: measured at the 829-file corpus draw, 6 files with an identifier in a macro array lose those rows, and time-select.vue's `defineEmits([CHANGE_EVENT, 'blur', 'focus', 'clear', UPDATE_MODEL_EVENT])` published three events where the component emits five. The differential surfaced the loss as MISSING rows before any of this was found (`time-select -> CHANGE_EVENT`, `picker -> UPDATE_MODEL_EVENT`). Caught by vue/declare-emits-identifier-array, which pins the string control `blur` in the SAME array so an implementation cannot satisfy it by changing how strings are read.

F14 regression: contract PARTICIPANTS are read by a blind first-`type_identifier` search again, which reaches into the object literal's property signatures and names a PROP'S TYPE as the contract. Two corpus files caught this in opposite directions at the 829-file draw: node.vue's `defineProps<{ node: NodeShape; menuId?: string }>()` has NO participant (the props are symbols; NodeShape is one prop's type, already a delegate declared_type row) yet the oracle derived one — a permanent MISSING; and menu.vue's `defineProps<{ nodes: NodeShape[] } & Pick<CommonProps, 'height'>>()` should name `Pick` but the analyzer took `NodeShape`, so the two sides each manufactured half of one disagreement. The mutation re-adds a participant row for any type identifier appearing anywhere under a macro's type arguments, which is exactly the old rule. Caught by vue/contract-type-participant's FORBID row, which is scoped to a contract-marked edge from the COMPONENT so the delegate's legitimate declared_type row to NodeShape — sourced at the `intersect` variable — survives to prove the rule is about participants and not about erasing type references.

F14's other half: `genericMacroEntries` goes back to reading a DIRECT `object_type` child of the type arguments, which an INTERSECTION does not have — `defineProps<{ … } & Pick<X, 'a'>>()` matches nothing and publishes no props at all. Measured: cascader-panel/src/menu.vue emitted prop symbols `[]` before this fix and `['nodes','index']` after. Distinct from the participant mutant on purpose, because the two halves were fixed in different methods and a single mutant reverting both would pass whenever only one was pinned.

V4/M49 character regression: the v-for parser stops at end-of-input instead of BACKTRACKING the greedy separator, so the collection is read as part of the directive rather than after it. The regex engine gave characters back from the separator until the collection had something to match, and that backtracking is observable: for `v-for="item in  "` the final space WAS the collection. This was a REAL bug in the first hand-written replacement, caught by a 799-shape equivalence sweep rather than by any fixture — 170 of 799 shapes differed. Simulated on the output as a collection read whose TARGET absorbed the separator, which is what an un-backtracked parse yields. Caught by vue/v-for-directive-shapes, which expects the four collections to resolve.

V4/M49 character regression: the v-for alias head is taken GREEDILY, so `(row, i) in grid` binds ONE name instead of two and the loop variables stop SHADOWING the members they share a name with — every template read of an alias becomes a spurious member read. The head is the SHORTEST run without a `)` for which the keyword matches, which is what makes `(row, i)` bind two names and `item in items` bind `item` rather than `item in items`. Simulated faithfully without reaching into the parser: a member that has a symbol but NO use edge is precisely a member whose every template read was shadowed, so publishing a use for it is exactly what losing the shadowing produces. Caught by vue/v-for-directive-shapes, whose twelve forbidden rows are all shadowed members.

F16 regression: the `name` inside `defineOptions({ … })` is ignored again, so a `<script setup>` component that declares its identity the Vue 3.3+ way falls back to the FILE STEM. The macro was in VUE_COMPILER_MACROS purely so its call edge would be filtered, and nothing looked inside it — measured on the corpus, `td-wrapper.vue` (`name: 'TableTdWrapper'`) was published as `td-wrapper` and `split-bar.vue` (`name: 'ElSplitterBar'`) as `split-bar`. Caught by vue/define-options-name, whose `size` prop is declared with the inline generic form on purpose: it is owned by the DECLARED name, so the mutant fails on ownership as well as on the component's own name, which is what distinguishes a correct rename (with its re-point) from a bare rename that orphans the members.

F17 regression: a `name:` option whose value is an IDENTIFIER is published as the component's identity again — the variable's name becomes the component name. Measured on the restored corpus, option.vue published a component called `COMPONENT_NAME` with 21 edges sourced at it and select.vue one with 43: a name not written anywhere as that component's name, held by no registry, resolvable by no consumer, and strictly worse than the file-stem fallback F8 already chose on purpose. Simulated on the output as the component symbol renamed to the unresolved name it used to read. Caught by vue/component-name-identifier, whose `declaredNameUnreadable` expectation fails as well: the flag only exists because the stem was kept, so this mutant is caught on both the name AND the honesty about why.

F18 regression: drop the provided members that are not `key: value` pairs — the SHORTHAND (`contentRef`), the SHORTHAND METHOD (`close`) and the members of a WRAPPED object (`reactive({ nodes, index })`). This is the defect the `contains` oracle measured across dropdown.vue (6 shorthand keys) and form.vue (every member of its reactive payload).

F8 regression: the split component identity returns — a `name:` option pushes a SECOND Class symbol beside the SFC's own instead of renaming it. Measured through the store on `WidgetFile.vue` declaring `name: 'ActualName'`: 6 edges sourced the file stem and 2 contained edges sourced the option name, neither reachable as a target, so one component had two answers and no edge unified them. Caught by vue/options-rename-identity's forbidSymbols row (the file-stem Class) plus its two meta rows on the surviving symbol (meta.moduleName / meta.isOptionsComponent) — a bare count assertion would pass with the second symbol still there under a different name.

F8 regression, the EDGE half: the single Class symbol is correct but the edges still source the file stem, so the one component symbol is unreachable from every script and template edge — the exact half a symbol-count assertion cannot see. Caught ONLY by vue/options-rename-identity's four `from: ActualName` relationship rows, and its four mirrored `from: <file-stem>` forbid rows, which are what pin the template `instantiates` edge specifically: the first version of this fix re-pointed only the DELEGATED rows in the merge loop and left every template edge on the file stem.

F2 regression: the provide/inject CONTRACT edges are dropped, so a provider and a consumer of one key are not joinable — the exact pre-fix state, where the corpus's 79 call sites emitted only the bare `calls` edge the sub-analyzer makes and the relationship between them did not exist. Caught by vue/provide-inject-contract's four `references` rows. Distinct from vue/provided-owner-drop: one mutant reverting both would pass if either claim were pinned, which is the M49 T6 lesson.

F2 regression, the OWNERSHIP half: the keys of an inline `provide(K, { … })` value go back to being ownerless symbols — indistinguishable in the graph from module-level functions, which the corpus census measured as 4 real rows on element-plus tour.vue (updateModelValue, onClose, onFinish). Caught ONLY by vue/provide-inject-contract's two ownerName + meta.isProvided symbol rows. This is also the mutant that proves the ANNOTATION was necessary: re-PUSHING the symbols instead of annotating them would collide on the store's owner-blind symbol key and silently replace the sub-analyzer's row (VSD25), which is why the fix annotates in place.

F7 regression: `hasTypeInference` goes back to the hardcoded `false`, so every SFC reports the same thing regardless of which grammar parsed its script. Caught by vue/ts-type-inference (a lang="ts" SFC whose interface/annotation members the TypeScript analyzer extracted correctly while the flag denied it). Its negative twin vue/js-type-inference is what makes this pair a gate rather than a claim — see vue/type-inference-always-true for the other direction.

F7 regression, the OTHER direction: `hasTypeInference` is flipped to `true` unconditionally, which passes a one-sided fixture and is exactly as false as the original constant. Caught ONLY by the negative half, vue/js-type-inference — a plain `<script>` SFC whose block goes to the JavaScript analyzer, where no type inference was available. Recorded because it is the mutant a ts-only fixture cannot see, and the reason the fixture pair exists.

F12 regression: the macro extraction goes back to INLINE literals only — the same-file BINDING form stops resolving, so `defineProps(boundProps)` / `defineEmits(boundEmits)` emit no Property/Event symbols. This is the exact pre-fix state: on the restored corpus it cost 22 of 22 `defineProps(binding)` and 67 of 67 `defineEmits(binding)` sites their whole contract. Caught by vue/named-contract's four component-owned symbol rows and their four contains rows. The named/imported EDGE half is deliberately NOT removed here — that is the second mutant below, because one mutant that reverts both halves proves only that ONE of them is pinned, which is how the M49 T6 lesson (a claim with no fixture) starts.

F12 regression, second half: the contract EDGE is dropped — `defineProps<Named>()` / `defineEmits<Named>()` and any unresolvable binding stop pointing at the declaration that carries their members, so a component's public contract is unanswerable from the component. Distinct from vue/named-contract-drop on purpose: one mutant reverting both halves would pass if EITHER half were pinned, which is exactly the coverage hole the M49 T6 lesson names. Caught by vue/named-contract's four `references` rows with meta.isPropContract / meta.isEmitContract.

M49 W2 (#769) regression: only the LAST prop-default() factory survives (the sibling-object dedup collapse): the earlier factory's body is dead-spanned and its random/toFixed calls vanish (prop-default-factory-calls' corpus-shape expects fail; the lane's own truth derives them)
M49 dup-key ruling (#745) regression: reverts Options-API member emission to first-wins — the later save() body is dropped instead of surviving (fixture pins the LAST body's qualified call)
M49 #762 regression: Options-API prop-default factory body calls invisible again — random/toFixed member-call edges dropped from the embedded script result (prop-default-factory-calls pin catches it)

F32 regression: a component whose `name:` value is bound by a LOCAL CONSTANT keeps the file stem again — the pre-F32 shape, and the one F17 generalized to every identifier on the premise that the value 'lives in another module'. Measured before the fix: 253 of 724 unresolved component-usage instantiates edges named a component whose name is assigned as a literal in the declaring file (ElInput 59, ElSelect 42, ElSwitch 33, 25 names). Expressed from the analyzer's OWN metadata (nameFromLocalConst), so it stays a regression of the rule as the rule changes: whatever name the lane resolved, the mutant un-resolves it and re-points the edges back to the stem, which is exactly what the rename+re-point pair exists to prevent. Caught by vue/component-name-local-const and vue/options-name-local-const, whose stem-as-Class forbids and whose expectSymbols both fire.

F31 regression: publishes template component tags AS WRITTEN again, dropping the registry name — <el-button/> targets `el-button` while the corpus declares `ElButton`, which is the CASING row vue-instantiates-targets.mts rules the analyzer owns (1,409 of 2,267 edges, 62.2%, pre-fix) — vue/kebab-registry-name pins the normalized target and forbids the written spelling, so reverting loses 7 rows and adds 6 forbid violations

F21 regression: the provide/inject pass goes back to a bare NAME test, so a call whose CALLEE TEXT is `inject`/`provide` is a Vue contract whatever BINDS the name — `@inject("db")` (a DI decorator, not Vue's function) fabricates `references ContractShapes -> db`, `import { inject } from 'vue-router'` fabricates `foreignKey`, and a local `function inject(key)` that shadows the global fabricates `shadowedKey`. This is the exact pre-fix state of three separate fixtures' forbid rows, and the state the corpus could not see: of 1,162 `.vue` files over the restored draw, all 96 provide/inject call sites are `import … from 'vue'`, so zero corpus rows move and the fixtures ARE the evidence. Caught by vue/contract-call-name-shapes' two `db` forbid rows + its `foreignKey` row, and independently by vue/contract-call-local-shadow's `shadowedKey` row. Distinct from vue/provide-inject-edge-drop (the F2 half): that one deletes the contract edges the fix ADDED, this one re-adds the rows the fix REMOVED, and a single mutant reverting both would pass whenever either half were pinned — the M49 T6 lesson.

Finding G1 (the grammar repair's half that lives in the ANALYZER's reach). A processing instruction's content is the `_pi_content` external token, which the wired grammar used to fail to produce unless the byte after `?>` was a newline, so a content-bearing PI became an ERROR node the analyzer could not dispatch. Reverted generically: a `module` symbol the analyzer recorded with `isProcessingInstruction` and that the SOURCE spells with content between its target and `?>` is dropped, together with its edge. The pre-repair shape is not a missing symbol here — the analyzer is unchanged and the GRAMMAR is what changed — so the mutant models the observable consequence: the PI the grammar can no longer produce. Pinned by xml/pi-and-stylesheet, whose `<?catalog-processing build="12"?>` is content-bearing; the pre-existing M12 fixture used `<?catalog-processing?>`, the one spelling the broken grammar handled.

Finding G2, and the worst class in the lane: a PUBLISHED LIE rather than a missing fact. `<![INCLUDE[<!ELEMENT a EMPTY>]]>` inside an internal subset made the pre-repair grammar wrap the `doctypedecl` in an ERROR; the parser then took a LATER `Name` as the DTD's name, and the position-blind `findDirectChild(node, "Name")` published a Type symbol literally named `INCLUDE` with a `contains` edge from it. Reverted generically: the analyzer's own DTD-position guard is removed, so the FIRST `Name` beneath a `doctypedecl` becomes the DTD's name — which is the pre-fix behaviour verbatim, because the position-blind lookup and the recovery shape together produced exactly that. Pinned by xml/conditional-section, which forbids a symbol named `INCLUDE` and an edge from one.

Finding X1, the largest recall hole in the lane. In a schema language a construct's DECLARED NAME is the value of its `name` attribute, so the pre-fix analyzer published the TAG and the corpus filed every XSD type under one of six names — `xsd:element` alone appeared 5,914 times — while `bb_search("EntryType")` returned nothing. Measured: 1,197 of 26,578 in-vocabulary declarations published under their declared name, recall 0.045; after the fix, 18,490, recall 0.696, with the 29,196 out-of-vocabulary `name` attributes left untouched. Reverted generically: every symbol the analyzer recorded with `isVocabDeclaration` is relabelled to its `tagName` and the edges that name it are retargeted, which is the pre-fix reading exactly. Pinned by xml/declared-name-xsd.

The M60.R10 class, inverted. A `references` edge's target must be the NAME a declaration carries — the local part — because that is what resolves in the graph. Publishing the written value `tns:CatalogType` puts a value where a name belongs, and no declaration anywhere carries it, so every consumer following the edge finds nothing. Reverted generically: every reference edge the analyzer recorded as `attribute_qname_reference` is retargeted to the written `qname` from its own metadata. Pinned by xml/declared-name-xsd and xml/type-graph, which both forbid a colon-bearing target.

Finding L1 (M59.A7 / #825). The edge's target is the PATH, so the edge's line is the line the path is written on. The pre-fix code passed the whole `ExternalID` node, so `<!DOCTYPE hibernate-mapping PUBLIC 
 	"…/…-pubid"
 	"…/…-3.0.dtd">` pointed the edge at line 2, the `PUBLIC` keyword's line — the line of no name in the edge. Measured on the corpus: 8 of the first 60 files wrong, every multi-line DOCTYPE. Reverted generically: every `imports` edge whose metadata says it came from an external ID is moved to the line of the OWNING declaration's start, which is where the keyword is. Pinned by xml/dtd-declarations, which asserts `shared -> shared.dtd` on 3 while the doctypedecl opens on 2, and by the M12 contract probe's `the external-ID edge points at the PATH's line` check.

The no-unknown-symbols rule for `references`. The post-fix analyzer emits a reference only when the target RESOLVES in this document or is a known specification built-in, because a value naming nothing the document declares would put a name in the graph that no file supports. Reverted generically: every attribute value that is lexically a QName becomes a reference, resolvable or not — which is the pre-fix measurement (7,039 distinct QName values, recall 0.001, and 25,381 declarations whose name the analyzer did not resolve). Pinned by xml/type-graph, whose forbid list refuses a reference to an undeclared name, and by the M12 probe's `a call to a template the document does not declare is refused`.

Finding X3. Edge identity is `source|type|target`, so N declarations of one pair necessarily share one edge — a property of the schema, and the differential measures it separately for that reason. What was a defect is that the analyzer let the first line stand for all of them: 544,304 declaration occurrences collapsed onto 42,901 edges, and every occurrence after the first was unreachable with nothing recording it. Reverted generically: the collapse bookkeeping is undone — `occurrences` and `lines` are deleted and the edge's line is left wherever the walk first put it, so a later declaration's EARLIER line (a DTD content model read after the element it names) is lost. Pinned by xml/edge-collapse, which asserts occurrences 3 and lines [3,4,5], and by xml/dtd-declarations, whose `catalog -> entry` edge is one edge for two writings with the line at the DECLARATION site.

Finding X4. The pre-fix lane published 27,228 symbols from 177 files it simultaneously reported as erroneous, with nothing on any of them saying so; the shipped check `malformed XML creates no recovery symbols` was a FIXTURE ACCIDENT (an unterminated element yields no `element` node to publish, so the check passed for a reason unrelated to the analyzer's policy). The fix LABELS rather than suppresses, because a 90 %-parseable vendor template is thousands of real declarations and must stay visible. Reverted generically: the `syntaxErrors` label is stripped from every symbol and edge, which is the pre-fix reading — the symbols are still published, which is exactly the dishonest state. Pinned by xml/recovery-labelling, whose every expectation carries the label.

M59 (#825) regression: xml's relationships go back to carrying NO line. xml had no fixture lane at all before this round, so nothing pinned its line contract even though it was one of only two analyzers that emitted one. Caught by xml/lines-825, which pins every element, every attribute, the default-namespace edge (whose target is the synthesised name `default`) and the prefixed-namespace edge.

M18 (ATTLIST-default round) regression: an entity reference inside an ATTRIBUTE'S DECLARED DEFAULT stops being a use. `<!ATTLIST foo bar CDATA "<>"">` says `bar`'s default value is assembled from `lt`, `gt` and `quot`, and an attribute cannot be given its default without expanding them — 10 of the then-21-site residual across 4 files, 9 of them the PREDEFINED entities and therefore `builtin` rather than dangling. Dropped because an `EntityRef` was only collected under an OWNING ELEMENT and a DTD declaration has no element above it. Reverted by dropping every `entity_reference` edge whose source is an attribute declaration, which is the shape this analyzer records as `dtd_attribute_declaration`.

M18 (PEReference round) regression: a parameter entity reference stops being a USE. `<!DOCTYPE root [ <!ENTITY % defroot ’…’> %defroot; ]>` is how a DTD pulls in another one, which is the same fact `entity_external_id` already recorded for `<!ENTITY % pe SYSTEM "common.dtd">` reached by reference instead of by ExternalID — and it was recorded only for the ExternalID form. All 24 PEReference sites in the corpus produced no edge at all, so the graph could say a document imports a DTD and nothing about the `%defroot;` the author actually wrote. Reverted by dropping every `parameter_entity_reference` edge, which also removes the `unresolved` label on an undeclared parameter entity.

M18 (PEReference round) regression: the parameter-entity VALUE form is published as a reference. `% name 'replacement'` is how a parameter entity is DEFINED and names nothing — libxml2's corpus holds `% zz '<'` right beside real references, precisely so a rule accepting any `%…;` is caught. Accepting it invents names out of literal percent signs, so the mutant adds an edge from every value-form site. The fixture forbids `references -> zz` and this is what that forbid half is for; a forbid that can never match is worse than none, because it reads as coverage.

M18 regression: the five predefined entities go back to being UNRESOLVED. `< > & ' "` are declared by the XML specification itself, in every document, whether or not a DTD mentions them (XML 1.0 §4.6) — the same argument X8 settled for the `xml` and `xmlns` prefixes. The grammar reports each as an `EntityRef` and the resolver had exactly two answers, so all of them took the second: 4,575 sites across 180 files were stamped `resolvable: "unresolved"` with `danglingEntityReference: true`, which is the analyzer asserting that a well-formed document references an entity nothing defines. Reverted by removing `builtin` from the three-way label. ` ` is NOT in the set and must stay unresolved — an XML document using an undeclared HTML entity really does reference something undefined, so a fix that widened the set to make the other five pass would be the wrong fix.

M18 regression: an entity reference inside ANOTHER ENTITY'S REPLACEMENT TEXT goes back to being unowned. `<!ENTITY shout "&greeting; THERE">` is a real dependency — shout cannot be expanded without greeting — and it was dropped, because an `EntityRef` was only collected under an OWNING ELEMENT and replacement text has no element above it. 611 of the then-651-site shortfall sat in this shape over 16 files; libxml2's `test/recurse/lol_ig_content.xml` was the extreme at 147 sites and 1 edge. Reverted by re-anchoring each such edge to the DTD that holds the declaring entity, which is the owner that existed before the fix and the wrong one.

M19 regression: a vocabulary DECLARATION goes back to being reported on the line of the TAG that opens it rather than the line its `name=` value is written on. The two are routinely different — a formatted document puts the attribute on the next line, and sometimes the keyword and the value are split across two of them. Measured over the 2,500-file blast radius: 4 of 19,852 declarations, in 2 files, and invisible to every other instrument because each asks the analyzer a question it can answer correctly while the LINE is wrong, and the differential compares label+target only. Reverted generically from the analyzer's own `metadata.elementRange`, which the fix added precisely so the structural span stays available after the anchor moves to the name.

Finding X8. The `xml` and `xmlns` prefixes are bound by the Namespaces specification ITSELF, in every document, and re-binding `xml` is an error — so a well-formed file CANNOT supply them. A resolver reading only declarations therefore never resolved `xml`, the reference pass found no namespace to test for built-inness, and REFUSED the edge: 71 references over 20 corpus files, including every xml:lang in docx4j's Dublin Core schemas. The knowledge was present and unreachable — BUILTIN_NAMESPACE_URIS already held the xml namespace, consulted only when a binding existed, for the one prefix guaranteed never to bring one. Reverted generically: every reference edge whose qname uses a prefix the spec binds implicitly is deleted. Pinned by xml/xsd-implicit-xml-prefix, which declares NO xmlns:xml on purpose — adding one would make the fixture pass against the broken analyzer, which is the trap it exists to catch — and which uses the prefix xs rather than xsd so a normalising fixture would fail rather than pass.

Finding X7. A references edge whose prefix is bound to a namespace the document IMPORTS points at a component declared in ANOTHER FILE. The reference pass refused it, and the refusal is right for a prefix bound to nothing — that would put a name in the graph no file supports, the M60.R10 lie. It was wrong for an imported namespace, where the document already names the file: the imports edge for the same xsd:import says where the name lives. ~108 edges lost corpus-wide, and a schema set stopped being a graph and became a pile of files. Reverted generically: every reference edge carrying resolvable === 'external' is deleted, which is the pre-fix suppression, and NO symbol is added — a reversion that also published a phantom local symbol would be testing a different defect than the one that existed. Pinned by xml/xsd-external-reference, which writes its reference BEFORE the import that authorises it (the ordinary spelling) and forbids both the phantom symbols and the still-refused unimported prefix, so a fix that simply emitted every prefixed value would fail it.

Finding X13. A BARE reference on an attribute that carries one, whose OWNER is in a declaration vocabulary, and which this document does not declare, is a REAL claim — the document says this element's type is that name — and it was being DROPPED, which is the defect this review has been closing throughout: a claim the graph cannot see. Two corpus cases are indistinguishable from inside one file. vdv-first5_0.xsd xs:includes a file declaring its OWN `date` at line 32, and `type="date"` must be that type and not XSD's built-in of the same name; cxf's calculator.xsd writes `type="xsd:int"` with no xmlns:xsd declared, which is malformed and must be refused. So the bare-built-in rule makes the first confidently WRONG and a blanket refusal makes both unresolvable for no stated reason. The fix is a FOURTH resolvability class — `unresolved`, with `ambiguousWithBuiltin` when the name is also a built-in — and the target symbol is still not published, so it adds an edge and never a phantom declaration. 413 such edges across 59 corpus files, 103 flagged ambiguous, and the most frequent unresolved targets are custom OOXML types that live in included schema files. Reverted generically: every reference edge carrying resolvable === 'unresolved' is deleted, which is the pre-fix suppression. NO symbol is added — a reversion that also published one would be testing a different defect. Pinned by xml/xsd-included-reference, which holds all three cases including the malformed undeclared prefix that must still be REFUSED, so a fix that simply emitted every bare value would fail it.

Finding X10. XML Schema's QName datatype carries the `collapse` whiteSpace facet, so a QName-typed attribute value has its whitespace runs collapsed and its ends trimmed BEFORE it is read as a name. The analyzer did not, so `type="CT_GeoHierarchyEntity "` — a trailing space, written by a human and legal, since XML only normalises tab and newline in an attribute value and leaves inner spaces alone — failed the QName parse and the reference was REFUSED. One corpus site, where a complex type declared 7 lines above went unreferenced because of one character. Reverted generically: every reference target and qname is re-read from the RAW attribute text rather than the collapsed reading the analyzer stored, which is what the pre-fix code did — the deferred pass parsed `candidate.value`, and pre-fix that WAS the raw value. Pinned by xml/xsd-qname-whitespace, which pins four spellings rather than the one that was seen in the corpus, because the facet distinguishes them: trailing, leading and a double run all collapse to the same name, and an interior space must still be refused, since collapse replaces a run with ONE space and an interior space leaves the value not a QName. A fix that merely trimmed the ends would pass a fixture pinning only the trailing case and would accept a different and wrong set of values.

Finding X6. A self-loop guard read `if (type === References || type === Imports) { if (source === target) return }`. Sound for a REFERENCE, where both ends are component names and equality is a cycle in the document. Unsound for an IMPORT, whose ends are DIFFERENT KINDS OF THING: `source` is a symbol name, `target` is a path read out of a SYSTEM identifier, and when the strings coincide they still denote a symbol and a file. `<!ENTITY cover.gif SYSTEM "cover.gif" NDATA gif>` names a real file. It was dropped ASYMMETRICALLY, which is what makes it a defect and not a policy: `extractExternalId` had already pushed the ImportInfo, so the file was in the analyzer's `imports` array and absent from its relationship graph — the analyzer contradicting itself inside one call, with the graph the part consumers read. 46 edges in the corpus. Reverted generically: every imports edge whose source equals its target is deleted, which is exactly the pre-fix suppression, and the ImportInfo is LEFT ALONE so the mutant reproduces the asymmetry rather than tidying it — a reversion that also fixed the inconsistency would not be testing the defect. Pinned by xml/dtd-self-named-external-id, whose `cover` and `cover.gif` differ by a dot and nothing else, so a normaliser that stripped path punctuation would collapse them and pass a broken analyzer.

Finding X5, and the mirror image of M60.R10. A declaration's name is a NAME; `xsl:output`'s `method` attribute names the output METHOD (`xml`/`html`/`text`) and nothing else, yet DECLARATION_NAME_ATTRIBUTE mapped `output -> method`, so `<xsl:output method="html"/>` was published as a component called `html` marked isVocabDeclaration, with `method`/`encoding`/`indent` hung off IT, and the real name `xsl:output` absent from the graph entirely. Corpus cost 182 sites over 250 files (92 as `xml`, 53 as `text`, 37 as `html`), and where a stylesheet also contained a real `<html>` element the two unrelated components shared one name. Reverted generically and SELF-CONTAINEDLY: an element that carries a `method` attribute takes that attribute's VALUE as its own name, which is the pre-fix reading, and every attribute it owned is re-owned by the renamed symbol so the whole subgraph moves with it — the second half matters, because renaming the element without re-owning its attributes leaves `method` pointing at a name that no longer exists, and the fixture's forbidden `contains html -> method` would then pass for the wrong reason. Pinned by xml/xslt-output-is-not-a-name, which contains a real `<html>` element so the collision is unavoidable rather than theoretical.

Y0 REVERT, the lane's most severe defect: every sequence item is renumbered to index 0, which is what the unreachable `sibling === itemNode` scan produced (web-tree-sitter returns a fresh wrapper per call, so the early return was dead code and the loop returned a file-wide count). PRE-FIX (M60 ontology round): GitHub Actions gives the `uses` key three meanings and only the path decides which. At `jobs.<job>.uses` it names a reusable workflow this job INVOKES; at `jobs.<job>.steps[].uses` it names an action this step runs. Before the role was read from the path, both took the imports branch, so all 196 job-level reusable-workflow references in the corpus were labelled as imports of third-party actions. Measured: 196 edges in 92 of 16371 admitted files, and the corpus-wide conservation is exact — the stride draw's `imports` fell by exactly the 12 edges `calls` gained. Caught by yaml/workflow-call-role, whose forbid rows name both reusable workflows under `imports`: a first draft asserted only that the calls exist, which a relabel satisfies, so the forbids are the assertion carrying the weight.

The role rule INVERTED rather than removed: every `uses:` is promoted to a call, so `actions/checkout@v4` acquires a caller. This is the failure a value-shape heuristic makes — `acme/infra/x.yml@ref` and `actions/checkout@v4` both contain a `/`, and only one of them names a workflow. Caught by yaml/workflow-call-role, which forbids a `calls` edge to both the remote action and the local one.

The `calls` edges removed entirely, as if the role branch had never been written. Nothing else in the output changes, so this is the mutant that separates `calls` being emitted from `calls` being emitted CORRECTLY. Caught by yaml/workflow-call-role's two expectRelationships rows, one local and one remote.

The file-shape gate removed, so a document carrying top-level `jobs` and a job-level `uses:` but declaring neither `on:` nor the `.github/workflows` path is treated as a workflow. `jobs.<id>.uses` is defined by GitHub Actions and by nothing else in YAML, so this promotes an unproven reference to a call naming a caller that may not exist — the fabricated-edge shape. Caught by yaml/workflow-call-role-negative, which forbids any `calls` edge in a file that does not claim to be a workflow.

The materialized-action re-route REVERTED: `imports yaml_action_use` edges whose target is a `./D` path a PRIOR SAME-JOB checkout materializes go back to the literal path with `isExternal: true`, i.e. the unsupportable claim the fix replaced. This is the class the corpus found 10 sites of (`./security-scanner` ×7, `./ci-actions/.github/actions/setup` ×2, `./integration-release-action` ×1) and the reason it is a fix rather than a ruling: the referent is a named repository the arbiter can VERIFY, and a path the runner creates can only ever be `externalUnverified`. Caught by yaml/materialized-action, whose expect row pins the re-routed target `hashicorp/security-scanner@main` with `meta.remoteRef` and whose forbid row names the literal `./security-scanner` at the very site that must not carry it.

The root-anchored rewrite reverted: `uses: $/.github/actions/cache-restore` is emitted on its RAW spelling and re-stated as `remoteRef`, i.e. `$` claimed as a GitHub owner and `.github` as the repository under it. That claim is not merely weaker, it is false — the target is a path in the checked-out tree, and `terragrunt/.github/actions/cache-restore/action.yml` is a file the project carries — so the edge is read as `externalUnverified` and blocks an incoming PASS. Caught by yaml/root-anchored-action, whose forbid rows name the raw `$/.github/…` targets and whose expect rows pin `meta.isExternal: false` plus `meta.actionSpelling`.

The override DIRECTION reversed, so the entry that gets replaced claims to override its replacement. Caught by yaml/duplicate-key-overrides, which pins the direction on the two-occurrence chain and forbids the reverse.

Last-wins collapsed to all-to-first: the third occurrence of a key claims to replace the FIRST rather than the second. Both readings look defensible in prose, which is why this is worth a mutant — the loader replaces the value currently in effect, which after the second occurrence is the second. Caught by yaml/duplicate-key-overrides, whose forbid row names `child#3 -> child` specifically.

The one MUTANT here about honesty rather than structure, and the reason the harness keeps `confidenceMax` as a pinnable field. The two entries of a duplicate key are a parse FACT; that the later REPLACES the earlier is loader behaviour, not a grammar guarantee — YAML 1.2 leaves duplicate mapping keys undefined and GitHub Actions rejects them outright. This mutant claims confidence 1.0 and evidenceClass structural, i.e. it asserts the convention as if the grammar had said it, and drops the reason code the M14 contract §4 requires. Caught by yaml/duplicate-key-overrides on `confidenceMax`.

Z18 regression, RE-AIMED at the current contract (#924-E, a7368a80). The original transform matched a published target spelled `@"..."` and stripped its junk class; since quoting syntax is no longer part of a published NAME, that condition never fired and the mutant SURVIVED at 0 -> 0 — which is what a suite reports when a fixture is realigned and a mutant is left pointing at the old spelling. The defect is real and the reconstruction is still sound: a published zig name can contain a space or a bracket ONLY if it came from a quoted identifier (the grammar will not spell `fn weird type()` unquoted), so mangling the interior of such a name IS the Z18 defect under either spelling. Caught by zig/declared-type-leaf and zig/relationship-classes, whose expect rows name `odd field` and `weird type` — the correct published spellings.

Caught by the `meta.relationshipType` assertions on seven fixture rows across zig/kinds-and-owners and zig/relationship-classes, and by the invariant gate `zigw-invariants.ts`. CALIBRATED, not assumed: removing the code by hand turns F3 from 7/7 to 5/7, so the rows are known to bite.

Z38 regression: the type-position guard goes back to testing the DIRECT parent, so it cannot see a DOTTED type path — in this grammar `std.Build.LazyPath` is a chain of `field_expression` nodes, so every segment of a qualified type in a signature is published as a `uses` READ of a type name, attributed to the function whose signature it appears in, and duplicating the declared-type class that already publishes the same text. 480 rows over 200 corpus files, invisible at name level because the target IS a real type name. Caught by zig/relationship-classes' forbidRelationships on the three `uses` rows for `Local`/`Opts`/`Res`, and by the source-keyed gate (zigw-uses-calls.ts), which convicts it in both directions. NOTE THE DIRECTION: the pre-fix state ADDS these edges, so the mutant has to ADD them. The first version removed them — which is the state the FIX produces, so it passed the fixture and the suite correctly reported it as a survivor: a mutant that reconstructs the fixed state instead of the defect is a mutant of nothing.

Z39 regression: the source attribution goes back to recognising `function_declaration` only, so every read and call inside a NAMED TEST is attributed to `(global)` — a file-scope source for work plainly inside one named block. Caught by zig/relationship-classes' expectRelationships on `uses readsInsideANamedTestAreAttributedToTheTest -> fileLevelValue`, and by the source-keyed gate, which is the only instrument that looks at the source at all: the shared F5 matcher keys on `label + normTarget(target)` and discards it.

limitations.description: mutants wrap analyzer output rather than rewriting analyzer source; equivalent at the suite level but not a compiler-level injection
mutation coverage currently spans java + groovy (the wave languages); other languages add mutants when their waves start
each lane runs in its own process: the wasm parser is not safely reused across grammar switches in one process (measured abort, svelte→cpp)
